+import { Alert, App, Badge, Button, Card, Empty, Flex, Spin, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';
+import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
+
+import {
+  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,
+  CONNECTION_TYPES,
+  type Connection,
+  type ConnectionType,
+  listConnections,
+  testConnection,
+} from '../api/connections';
+
+const ENV_COLORS: Record<string, string> = {
+  dev: 'blue',
+  qa: 'gold',
+  uat: 'purple',
+  prod: 'red',
+};
+
+type LoadState =
+  | { status: 'loading' }
+  | { status: 'ok'; connections: Connection[] }
+  | { status: 'error'; error: string };
+
+export function Connections() {
+  const [state, setState] = useState<LoadState>({ status: 'loading' });
+
+  useEffect(() => {
+    let cancelled = false;
+    listConnections()
+      .then((connections) => {
+        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', connections });
+      })
+      .catch((err: unknown) => {
+        if (!cancelled) {
+          setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
+        }
+      });
+    return () => {
+      cancelled = true;
+    };
+  }, []);
+
+  if (state.status === 'loading') {
+    return <Spin tip="Loading connections…" size="large" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;
+  }
+  if (state.status === 'error') {
+    return (
+      <Alert
+        type="error"
+        showIcon
+        title="Failed to load connections"
+        description={state.error}
+        style={{ margin: 24 }}
+      />
+    );
+  }
+
+  const { connections } = state;
+  return (
+    <Flex vertical gap={24}>
+      <Typography.Title level={3} style={{ margin: 0 }}>
+        Connections
+      </Typography.Title>
+      {connections.length === 0 ? (
+        <Empty description="No connections configured yet" />
+      ) : (
+        // One section per type that has connections, in canonical type order.
+        CONNECTION_TYPES.filter((type) => connections.some((c) => c.type === type)).map((type) => (
+          <ConnectionTypeSection
+            key={type}
+            type={type}
+            connections={connections.filter((c) => c.type === type)}
+          />
+        ))
+      )}
+    </Flex>
+  );
+}
+
+function ConnectionTypeSection({
+  type,
+  connections,
+}: {
+  type: ConnectionType;
+  connections: Connection[];
+}) {
+  return (
+    <Flex vertical gap={12}>
+      <Typography.Title level={5} style={{ margin: 0 }}>
+        {CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[type]}
+      </Typography.Title>
+      <Flex wrap gap={12}>
+        {connections.map((connection) => (
+          <ConnectionCard key={connection.id} connection={connection} />
+        ))}
+      </Flex>
+    </Flex>
+  );
+}
+
+function ConnectionCard({ connection }: { connection: Connection }) {
+  const { message } = App.useApp();
+  const [testing, setTesting] = useState(false);
+
+  const onTest = async () => {
+    setTesting(true);
+    try {
+      const { ok } = await testConnection(connection.id);
+      if (ok) message.success(`${connection.name}: connection OK`);
+      else message.error(`${connection.name}: connection test failed`);
+    } catch (err) {
+      message.error(`${connection.name}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'test failed'}`);
+    } finally {
+      setTesting(false);
+    }
+  };
+
+  return (
+    <Card size="small" style={{ minWidth: 280 }}>
+      <Flex justify="space-between" align="center" gap={12}>
+        <Flex vertical gap={6}>
+          <Typography.Text strong>{connection.name}</Typography.Text>
+          <Flex gap={8} align="center">
+            <Tag color={ENV_COLORS[connection.env]}>{connection.env.toUpperCase()}</Tag>
+            {connection.has_secret ? (
+              <Badge status="success" text="credential set" />
+            ) : (
+              <Badge status="warning" text="no credential" />
+            )}
+          </Flex>
+        </Flex>
+        <Button size="small" loading={testing} onClick={onTest}>
+          Test
+        </Button>
+      </Flex>
+    </Card>
+  );
+}

+import { App as AntApp } from 'antd';
+import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
+import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
+import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+
+import { type Connection, listConnections, testConnection } from '../../src/api/connections';
+import { Connections } from '../../src/pages/Connections';
+
+// Keep the real CONNECTION_TYPES / labels; mock only the network functions.
+vi.mock('../../src/api/connections', async (importOriginal) => {
+  const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import('../../src/api/connections')>();
+  return { ...actual, listConnections: vi.fn(), testConnection: vi.fn() };
+});
+
+const mockList = vi.mocked(listConnections);
+const mockTest = vi.mocked(testConnection);
+
+function conn(overrides: Partial<Connection>): Connection {
+  return {
+    id: 'c1',
+    name: 'sf-dev',
+    type: 'snowflake',
+    env: 'dev',
+    config: {},
+    has_secret: true,
+    created_by: 'u1',
+    ...overrides,
+  };
+}
+
+// ConnectionCard uses antd's App.useApp() for messages → wrap in <AntApp>.
+function renderPage() {
+  return render(
+    <AntApp>
+      <Connections />
+    </AntApp>,
+  );
+}
+
+afterEach(() => {
+  vi.clearAllMocks();
+});
+
+describe('Connections', () => {
+  it('groups connections by type with env + credential badges', async () => {
+    mockList.mockResolvedValue([
+      conn({ id: 'c1', name: 'sf-dev', type: 'snowflake', env: 'dev', has_secret: true }),
+      conn({ id: 'c2', name: 's3-prod', type: 's3', env: 'prod', has_secret: false }),
+    ]);
+
+    renderPage();
+
+    expect(await screen.findByText('sf-dev')).toBeInTheDocument();
+    expect(screen.getByText('Snowflake')).toBeInTheDocument();
+    expect(screen.getByText('AWS S3')).toBeInTheDocument();
+    expect(screen.getByText('DEV')).toBeInTheDocument();
+    expect(screen.getByText('PROD')).toBeInTheDocument();
+    expect(screen.getByText('credential set')).toBeInTheDocument();
+    expect(screen.getByText('no credential')).toBeInTheDocument();
+  });
+
+  it('shows an empty state when there are no connections', async () => {
+    mockList.mockResolvedValue([]);
+
+    renderPage();
+
+    expect(await screen.findByText('No connections configured yet')).toBeInTheDocument();
+  });
+
+  it('runs a connectivity test from a card', async () => {
+    mockList.mockResolvedValue([conn({ id: 'c1', name: 'sf-dev' })]);
+    mockTest.mockResolvedValue({ ok: true });
+
+    renderPage();
+    await screen.findByText('sf-dev');
+    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Test' }));
+
+    expect(mockTest).toHaveBeenCalledWith('c1');
+  });
+
+  it('surfaces a load error', async () => {
+    mockList.mockRejectedValue(new Error('boom'));
+
+    renderPage();
+
+    expect(await screen.findByText('Failed to load connections')).toBeInTheDocument();
+    expect(screen.getByText('boom')).toBeInTheDocument();
+  });
+});
```

## Review: `feat/week4-connections-ui`

Scope note: correctness out of scope (I did not flag the `Alert title=`/`description=` prop usage — it's copied verbatim from the pre-existing `Home.tsx`, so it's an established repo pattern, not introduced here).

### Ranked findings

**1. [PLAUSIBLE — altitude, will be copied] `ENV_COLORS: Record<string, string>` is untyped on the key — `frontend/src/pages/Connections.tsx:13`**
`connections.ts` exports `ConnectionEnv` (`'dev'|'qa'|'uat'|'prod'`) and `CONNECTION_ENVS`, but the color map keys off `string`. Cost: if a 5th env is added to `ConnectionEnv`, TS won't flag the missing color — `ENV_COLORS[connection.env]` silently returns `undefined` → an uncolored tag, caught only at runtime/visually. The labels map right above it (`CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS: Record<ConnectionType, string>`) already demonstrates the correct exhaustive pattern. Fix: `Record<ConnectionEnv, string>`. Cheap, and this is the first env-tag in the app — suites/checks/runs pages will copy it. Worth extracting an `<EnvTag env={...}/>` component now if you expect reuse (the prompt's "reusable pattern vs bandaid" point).

**2. [CONFIRMED — simplification/efficiency, will be copied] Double-iteration group-by is O(types × conns) — `frontend/src/pages/Connections.tsx:73-79`**
```ts
CONNECTION_TYPES.filter((type) => connections.some((c) => c.type === type)).map((type) => (
  <ConnectionTypeSection ... connections={connections.filter((c) => c.type === type)} />
))
```
This scans the full `connections` array once for `.some()` and again for `.filter()`, per type — 6 types means up to 12 full passes every render (no memoization). A single group-by pass produces the same canonically-ordered sections:
```ts
const byType = Map<ConnectionType, Connection[]> // one pass, then iterate CONNECTION_TYPES for order
```
Cost is small at Week-4 data volumes, but this group-by-then-render shape is exactly what suites-by-X and checks-by-X pages will copy. Establishing the single-pass version now sets the better precedent.

**3. [CONFIRMED — reuse] Load-state machine + loading/error JSX is copy-pasted from `Home.tsx` — `frontend/src/pages/Connections.tsx:20-58` vs `Home.tsx:6-44`**
The `LoadState` union, the `useEffect` with the `cancelled` guard, the `Spin` loading branch, and the `Alert` error branch are duplicated near-verbatim (only the fetch fn and copy differ). This is now the **second** copy — the third (suites page) will make it three. Cost: every future page re-derives the cancelled-effect dance by hand; a bug in one copy (e.g. forgetting the cleanup) won't be fixed in the others. Recommend extracting a `useAsyncData(fetchFn)` hook returning `LoadState`, plus a small `<LoadStateView loading error>` wrapper, before the pattern multiplies. This PR is the right moment since it's the first duplication.

**4. [PLAUSIBLE — altitude] Nav `selectedKeys` via `startsWith` + a `NAV_ITEMS`-derived array — `frontend/src/App.tsx:21-23`**
```ts
const selectedKeys = NAV_ITEMS.map((i) => i.key).filter((k) => location.pathname.startsWith(k));
```
Two concerns as routes grow: (a) `startsWith` is prefix-collision-prone — once you add e.g. `/connection-groups`, both `/connections` and a sibling could match a path; and (b) `/profile` and `/connections` happen not to collide today, but nothing enforces it. For a flat first slice it's fine, but as nested routes (`/connections/:id`) arrive this needs to become "longest-matching prefix" or react-router's `useMatch`/`NavLink active` instead. Flagging as a latent gap the next nav-touching PR should harden, not a blocker now.

**5. [CONFIRMED — minor] `Routes` defines `/connections` and `/profile` but no catch-all — `frontend/src/App.tsx:46-50`**
An unknown path renders an empty `<Content>` with no redirect/404. Low cost now (only two real routes + the `/` redirect), but the next page-adding PR will keep forgetting it. A single `<Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/connections" replace />} />` closes it.

### Good / no action
- `api/connections.ts` matches `me.ts` conventions cleanly (`const`-tuple + derived union types, JSDoc tied to backend schema, secret-never-returned comment) — good altitude, no notes.
- Test file mocks only the network seam (`importOriginal` keeps real `CONNECTION_TYPES`/labels) — exactly the "don't mock the seam under test" discipline; covers empty/error/test-click. Solid.

### Bottom line
Nothing blocking. The two that matter most because **this is the first of several Week-4 pages that will be copied**: **#1** (type the env map / extract `EnvTag`) and **#3** (extract the load-state hook before the third duplication). **#2** is a cheap single-pass win worth doing while the group-by pattern is new. #4/#5 are "harden on the next nav PR."

CONFIRMED correct.
- **Removed-behavior (`<Home/>` `/`→`/profile`, `<Routes>` inside `<AuthGate>`)** — `/` now redirects to `/connections`; `Home` renders intact at `/profile`; `AuthGate` semantics unchanged (gates the whole `<Routes>`, which is the intended behavior). CONFIRMED no regression.

It still renders (mapped internally to `description`), so behavior is correct; just swap `tip` → `description` to silence the warning. PLAUSIBLE/cosmetic. Note `Home.tsx` uses the same pattern, so it's pre-existing.

  "content": "import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';\n\n/** Three-state result of a one-shot async fetch. */\nexport type AsyncState<T> =\n  | { status: 'loading' }\n  | { status: 'ok'; data: T }\n  | { status: 'error'; error: string };\n\n/**\n * Fetch once on mount, with a cancelled-guard so a late resolution after unmount\n * doesn't set state, and rejection normalised to a string `error`. Shared by the\n * data pages (Home, Connections, …) so the cancelled-effect dance lives in one\n * place rather than being re-derived per page.\n */\nexport function useAsyncData<T>(fetcher: () => Promise<T>): AsyncState<T> {\n  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<T>>({ status: 'loading' });\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    let cancelled = false;\n    fetcher()\n      .then((data) => {\n        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', data });\n      })\n      .catch((err: unknown) => {\n        if (!cancelled) {\n          setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });\n        }\n      });\n    return () => {\n      cancelled = true;\n    };\n    // Fetch once on mount; the fetcher identity is intentionally not a dependency.\n    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps\n  }, []);\n\n  return state;\n}\n"
}

  "new_string": "import { Alert, App, Badge, Button, Card, Empty, Flex, Spin, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nimport {\n  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,\n  CONNECTION_TYPES,\n  type Connection,\n  type ConnectionEnv,\n  type ConnectionType,\n  listConnections,\n  testConnection,\n} from '../api/connections';\nimport { useAsyncData } from '../hooks/useAsyncData';\n\nconst ENV_COLORS: Record<ConnectionEnv, string> = {\n  dev: 'blue',\n  qa: 'gold',\n  uat: 'purple',\n  prod: 'red',\n};\n\n/** Group connections by type in one pass, preserving canonical type order. */\nfunction groupByType(connections: Connection[]): [ConnectionType, Connection[]][] {\n  const byType = new Map<ConnectionType, Connection[]>();\n  for (const c of connections) {\n    const group = byType.get(c.type);\n    if (group) group.push(c);\n    else byType.set(c.type, [c]);\n  }\n  return CONNECTION_TYPES.filter((type) => byType.has(type)).map((type) => [\n    type,\n    byType.get(type) as Connection[],\n  ]);\n}\n\nexport function Connections() {\n  const state = useAsyncData(listConnections);\n\n  if (state.status === 'loading') {\n    return <Spin tip=\"Loading connections…\" size=\"large\" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;\n  }\n  if (state.status === 'error') {\n    return (\n      <Alert\n        type=\"error\"\n        showIcon\n        title=\"Failed to load connections\"\n        description={state.error}\n        style={{ margin: 24 }}\n      />\n    );\n  }\n\n  const connections = state.data;\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical gap={24}>\n      <Typography.Title level={3} style={{ margin: 0 }}>\n        Connections\n      </Typography.Title>\n      {connections.length === 0 ? (\n        <Empty description=\"No connections configured yet\" />\n      ) : (\n        groupByType(connections).map(([type, group]) => (\n          <ConnectionTypeSection key={type} type={type} connections={group} />\n        ))\n      )}\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}"
}

10	Before merging any PR into `main` in the DataQ repo, run the `/review` skill against the PR's diff.
11	
12	**If `/review` surfaces findings:**
13	- Post them as PR review comments on the PR (use `gh pr review` or `gh pr comment`), not as silent in-line fixes.
14	- Each finding goes as a separate comment so it can be triaged independently.
15	- Findings that require code changes follow the standard defect workflow ([[dataq-working-agreements]] rule #3): if the finding is a genuine defect rather than a style nit, raise a GitHub issue and address in a follow-up PR. If it's a small in-PR fix that fits within the PR's scope, push a fixup commit to the branch.
16	
17	**If `/review` is clean:**
18	- Proceed to merge.
19	
20	**Why:** User wants `/review` as a hard pre-merge gate. Combines with the ruleset's `required_review_thread_resolution: true` — comments must be resolved before merge, so findings can't be accidentally bypassed. Keeps quality bar high while the team is small / solo, and avoids the "merge first, fix later, lose context" trap.
21	
22	**How to apply:**
23	- When preparing to merge a PR, run `/review` first.
24	- Use `gh pr view <N>` to fetch the diff if needed.
25	- Post findings via `gh pr comment <N> --body "..."` or `gh api /repos/.../pulls/<N>/comments` for line-anchored comments.
26	- Never `--no-verify` past hooks or merge with unresolved review threads.
27	
28	Related: [[dataq-working-agreements]]

=== snowflake.py (config + connstring + runner connect) ===
"""Snowflake datasource adapter (GX Core 1.17).

All Great-Expectations-specific machinery for Snowflake lives here, behind the
`CheckRunner` seam in ``base.py`` — per CLAUDE.md, the GX version-specific API
must not leak into the suite / check / result layer (GX v1 has drifted across
point releases).

The full GX chain (``add_snowflake`` → ``add_table_asset`` →
``add_batch_definition_whole_table`` → ``ValidationDefinition.run``) connects to
Snowflake at asset-build time, so ``run_checks`` cannot run without a live
warehouse. Tests therefore exercise the GX-free parts directly — config
validation, connection-string building, the snake_case→GX-class translation,
and the GX-result→`CheckOutcome` mapping (fed a canned result) — and inject a
fake `CheckRunner` elsewhere. End-to-end validation against a real Snowflake DEV
warehouse is a tracked follow-up.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import quote_plus

import great_expectations as gx
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from backend.app.core.secrets import SecretStore
from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckSpec, SuiteOutcome

# GX-translation machinery is shared across runners (see `gx_runner`); re-exported
# here so existing importers (and tests) keep resolving these from `snowflake`.
from backend.app.datasources.gx_runner import (
    UnknownExpectationError,
    _expectation_class_name,
    _to_gx_expectation,
    run_expectations,
    to_suite_outcome,
)

__all__ = [
    "SnowflakeCheckRunner",
    "SnowflakeConfig",
    "SnowflakeConnectionAdapter",
    "UnknownExpectationError",
    "_expectation_class_name",
    "_to_gx_expectation",
    "build_connection_string",
    "build_snowflake_runner",
    "to_suite_outcome",
]


class SnowflakeConfig(BaseModel):
    """Non-secret Snowflake connection config (the password comes from secrets).

    Maps from ``Connection.config``. ``schema`` is aliased to ``schema_`` to
    avoid shadowing pydantic's ``BaseModel.schema``.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True, extra="forbid")

    account: str
    user: str
    database: str
    schema_: str = Field(alias="schema")
    warehouse: str
    role: str | None = None


def build_connection_string(config: SnowflakeConfig, password: str) -> str:
    """Assemble a snowflake-sqlalchemy URL. User/password/params are URL-encoded."""
    params = {"warehouse": config.warehouse}
    if config.role:
        params["role"] = config.role
    query = "&".join(f"{key}={quote_plus(value)}" for key, value in params.items())
    return (
        f"snowflake://{quote_plus(config.user)}:{quote_plus(password)}"
        f"@{config.account}/{config.database}/{config.schema_}?{query}"
    )


class SnowflakeCheckRunner:
    """`CheckRunner` for Snowflake. Building the asset connects to the warehouse."""

    def __init__(self, config: SnowflakeConfig, password: str) -> None:
        self._config = config
        self._connection_string = build_connection_string(config, password)

    def run_checks(
        self,
        *,
        table: str,
        schema: str | None,
        checks: list[CheckSpec],
    ) -> SuiteOutcome:
        context = gx.get_context(mode="ephemeral")
        datasource = context.data_sources.add_snowflake(
            name=f"sf-{table}",
            connection_string=self._connection_string,
        )
        asset = datasource.add_table_asset(
            name=table,
            table_name=table,
            schema_name=schema or self._config.schema_,
        )
        # The table asset resolves its own batch, so no batch_parameters; the
        # ephemeral context makes the fixed suite/vd names safe across runs.
        batch_definition = asset.add_batch_definition_whole_table(name="whole_table")
        return run_expectations(
            context, batch_definition=batch_definition, checks=checks, name=f"suite-{table}"
        )


def build_snowflake_runner(
    *,
    config: dict[str, Any],

) -> SnowflakeCheckRunner:
    """Build a runner from a `Connection` row's config + secret_ref.

    Takes primitives (not the ORM model) to keep the adapter decoupled from the

# Snowflake connector timeouts (seconds) for the connectivity test — fail fast
# rather than hanging the request thread on an unreachable account.
_TEST_LOGIN_TIMEOUT = 10
_TEST_NETWORK_TIMEOUT = 10


class SnowflakeConnectionAdapter:
    """`ConnectionAdapter` for Snowflake — config validation + a SELECT 1 test."""

    def validate_config(self, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> SnowflakeConfig:
        return SnowflakeConfig.model_validate(raw)

    def test(self, raw: dict[str, Any], secret: str) -> None:
        """Open a connection and run ``SELECT 1``; raise on any failure.

        Deliberately GX-free — a lightweight connectivity probe, not a suite run.
        """
        from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text

        config = self.validate_config(raw)
        engine = create_engine(
            build_connection_string(config, secret),
            connect_args={
                "login_timeout": _TEST_LOGIN_TIMEOUT,
                "network_timeout": _TEST_NETWORK_TIMEOUT,
            },
        )
        try:
            with engine.connect() as conn:
                conn.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
        finally:
            engine.dispose()

User/password/params are URL-encoded.\"\"\"\n    params = {\"warehouse\": config.warehouse}\n    if config.role:\n        params[\"role\"] = config.role\n    query = \"&\".join(f\"{key}={quote_plus(value)}\" for key, value in params.items())\n    return (\n        f\"snowflake://{quote_plus(config.user)}:{quote_plus(password)}\"\n        f\"@{config.account}/{config.database}/{config.schema_}?{query}\"\n    )",
  "new_string": "    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True, extra=\"forbid\")\n\n    account: str\n    user: str\n    database: str\n    schema_: str = Field(alias=\"schema\")\n    warehouse: str\n    role: str | None = None\n    # Auth method. 'password' (default — back-compat for existing configs that\n    # carry no auth_type) puts the password in the DSN. 'key_pair' authenticates\n    # with an RSA private key: the secret is the **PEM private key** (v1: an\n    # unencrypted key) passed as `private_key` connect-arg, and the DSN carries\n    # no password. Both share the same SecretStore `secret_ref`.\n    auth_type: Literal[\"password\", \"key_pair\"] = \"password\"\n\n\ndef _private_key_der(pem: str) -> bytes:\n    \"\"\"Load a PEM RSA private key (v1: unencrypted) → DER PKCS8 bytes.\n\n    snowflake-connector's `private_key` connect-arg wants DER PKCS8, not PEM.\n    Encrypted keys (passphrase) are a follow-up — v1 key-pair uses unencrypted keys.\n    \"\"\"\n    key = serialization.load_pem_private_key(pem.encode(), password=None)\n    return key.private_bytes(\n        encoding=serialization.Encoding.DER,\n        format=serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,\n        encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),\n    )\n\n\ndef build_connection_string(config: SnowflakeConfig, secret: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Assemble a snowflake-sqlalchemy URL. User/password/params are URL-encoded.\n\n    For key-pair auth the DSN carries **no password** (the key rides in\n    connect-args, see `build_connect_args`); ``secret`` is then ignored here.\n    \"\"\"\n    params = {\"warehouse\": config.warehouse}\n    if config.role:\n        params[\"role\"] = config.role\n    query = \"&\".join(f\"{key}={quote_plus(value)}\" for key, value in params.items())\n    credentials = (\n        quote_plus(config.user)\n        if config.auth_type == \"key_pair\"\n        else f\"{quote_plus(config.user)}:{quote_plus(secret)}\"\n    )\n    return (\n        f\"snowflake://{credentials}\"\n        f\"@{config.account}/{config.database}/{config.schema_}?{query}\"\n    )\n\n\ndef build_connect_args(config: SnowflakeConfig, secret: str) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"SQLAlchemy `connect_args` carrying the key-pair credential, if any.\n\n    Empty for password auth (the password is in the DSN). For key-pair, the\n    loaded DER private key under `private_key` (the snowflake-connector arg).\n    \"\"\"\n    if config.auth_type == \"key_pair\":\n        return {\"private_key\": _private_key_der(secret)}\n    return {}"

135	        context = gx.get_context(mode="ephemeral")

147	        batch_definition = asset.add_batch_definition_whole_table(name="whole_table")
148	        return run_expectations(

154	    *,
155	    config: dict[str, Any],
156	    secret_ref: str | None,
157	    secret_store: SecretStore,
158	) -> SnowflakeCheckRunner:
159	    """Build a runner from a `Connection` row's config + secret_ref.
160	
161	    Takes primitives (not the ORM model) to keep the adapter decoupled from the
162	    DB layer.
163	    """
164	    if not secret_ref:
165	        raise ValueError("Snowflake connection requires secret_ref for the password")
166	    sf_config = SnowflakeConfig.model_validate(config)
167	    password = secret_store.get(secret_ref)
168	    return SnowflakeCheckRunner(sf_config, password)

## Review: `feat/snowflake-keypair-auth`

Overall a clean, well-factored change. `build_connect_args` is the right seam and composes correctly with both registries. Two real, actionable items (one test gap, one cosmetic), plus a consistency note.

### 1. Reuse / altitude — GOOD, no action

`build_connect_args(config, secret)` is the correct seam. The three call sites (runner `__init__`, `adapter.test`, profiler `_snowflake_engine_args`) each need their *own* `connect_args` dict anyway (runner wraps it in GX's `kwargs={"connect_args": ...}`; the other two merge it into their existing timeout dicts), so there's no further centralization to extract — the duplication is just three `**build_connect_args(...)` spreads, which is the right altitude. Key-pair does **not** leak special-casing into the `_PROFILERS` registry or `build_check_runner`: the branch is fully contained inside `build_connect_args`/`build_connection_string`, and `_snowflake_engine_args` stays a plain registry entry. Good.

### 2. Simplification — minor, actionable (cosmetic)

`backend/app/datasources/snowflake.py` ~line 100:
```python
return (
    f"snowflake://{credentials}" f"@{config.account}/{config.database}/{config.schema_}?{query}"
)
```
The adjacent-string concat is a leftover from the edit and is now pointless — the original split was on the `:password@` boundary, which `credentials` now subsumes. **Cost:** trivial, but it's a confusing artifact (reads like a typo'd missing comma) that a maintainer will trip over. Collapse to one f-string. Low priority.

No redundant branching elsewhere — the ternary in `build_connection_string` and the `if` in `build_connect_args` are both minimal.

### 3. Consistency — actionable (worth a maintainer's attention)

`s3.py` and `adls.py` both pair `auth_type: Literal[...]` with an `@model_validator(mode="after")` that enforces the secret semantics of each variant (e.g. S3 raises `access_key_id is required when auth_type is 'access_key'`; both reject the deferred variant with a documented message). Snowflake's new `auth_type` has **no such validator** — the key-pair contract ("secret is an unencrypted PEM key") is documented only in a field comment and is enforced lazily, deep in `_private_key_der`, at connect time.

**Cost:** divergence from the established pattern. A malformed/encrypted key surfaces as a raw `cryptography` `ValueError` during a run/profile (in the Celery worker), not as a clean config-validation error at save time like the sibling adapters produce. Consider an after-validator (even just to document/normalize) for parity, or at minimum it's worth a deliberate note that Snowflake intentionally validates the key at connect-time rather than config-time.

### 4. Test coverage — one real gap, actionable

The unit-level helpers are well covered (`build_connect_args` password-empty / key-pair-DER / malformed-key; connection-string omits password; auth_type default/accept/reject). But two **integration-shaped paths the diff actually changed are untested**:

- **Adapter test path (the one you flagged):** `test_adapter_test_runs_select_1_and_disposes` (line 331) only exercises password auth and asserts `connect_args == {"login_timeout": 10, "network_timeout": 10}`. There is **no test that `SnowflakeConnectionAdapter.test` merges `private_key` into `connect_args` for `key_pair`.** The merge at snowflake.py:204 (`**build_connect_args(config, secret)`) is the load-bearing new line in the adapter and it's uncovered. The existing test already captures `connect_args` via `fake_create_engine`, so a parallel key-pair case is ~10 lines.

- **Profiler `_snowflake_engine_args` key-pair path:** the new `**build_connect_args(sf, secret)` at profile_service.py:248 has **no test** asserting `private_key` lands in the returned connect-args dict for `auth_type="key_pair"`. `_snowflake_engine_args` is a pure function — trivial to assert directly.

- **Runner `kwargs={"connect_args": ...}` wrapping** (snowflake.py:140-142) is also uncovered, though that one's harder to test without GX and is lower value than the two above.

**Cost:** the two new wiring lines that route the private key through the *actual* adapter-test and profiler entrypoints could both regress (e.g. someone drops the `**` spread, or rewraps the dict) and every existing test would still pass. The helper tests prove `build_connect_args` works in isolation but not that the three call sites consume it. Given CONTRIBUTING rule 4a (test failure modes / don't only cover the helper), the two missing call-site tests are the meaningful ones.

### Summary
- **Must-fix:** add the two call-site key-pair tests (adapter `.test` merges `private_key`; profiler `_snowflake_engine_args` includes `private_key`).
- **Should-fix:** consistency — add a `model_validator` for `auth_type`/key semantics to match s3/adls, or explicitly note the connect-time-validation choice.
- **Nice-to-have:** collapse the leftover adjacent-string f-string concat.

## Review: `feat/snowflake-keypair-auth`

I read all three changed files, traced every caller, and verified behavior against the **installed GX 1.17.2** and snowflake-connector source.

### Correctness

**1. GX runner uses the *deprecated* connect_args path — emits a `DeprecationWarning` (PLAUSIBLE, low severity)**
`backend/app/datasources/snowflake.py:140-147`
GX 1.17.2's `SnowflakeDatasource._validate_and_process_kwargs` explicitly deprecates `kwargs={"connect_args":{"private_key":...}}` and tells you to pass `private_key=` directly to `add_snowflake()`:
> "Passing 'private_key' via kwargs['connect_args'] is deprecated. Please pass 'private_key' as a keyword argument directly to add_snowflake()..."
Failure scenario: every key-pair suite run logs a `DeprecationWarning`; the path also relies on GX's internal base64 encode-then-decode round-trip (`_validate_and_process_kwargs` → `_build_engine_with_connect_args`). I empirically verified that round-trip is safe for real DER PKCS8 keys (0/20 false-positives in `_is_b64_encoded`), so it is **functionally correct today** but rides on deprecated, fragile internals. A maintainer would likely switch to the supported `private_key=` kwarg. Note this only affects the GX runner; the adapter-`test` and profiler paths call `create_engine` directly with raw DER bytes, which snowflake-connector accepts natively (`keypair.py:61`) — those are correct and not deprecated.

Everything else checks out clean:

- **Password path is byte-identical.** For `auth_type="password"`, `build_connect_args` returns `{}`, the `if self._connect_args:` guard skips `add_kwargs` entirely, so `add_snowflake` is called exactly as before. The `f"..." f"..."` adjacent-literal concatenation is valid and produces the identical DSN. Confirmed by passing test `test_connection_string_*`.
- **DSN omits password for key_pair** and never carries the key — only `user@host`. Confirmed (`test_key_pair_connection_string_omits_password`).
- **`add_snowflake` signature** does have a `kwargs` param in 1.17.2 (verified via `inspect.signature`).

### Security — no leak (REFUTED concerns)

- `_private_key_der` malformed-input exception is a `ValueError("Unable to load PEM file. ... MalformedFraming")` — **carries no key material** (verified by running it).
- Private key only ever lives in `connect_args` / DER bytes, never the URL/DSN.
- `backend/app/core/logging.py:25` already lists `"private_key"` in the redaction keyset, so the structlog PII redactor scrubs it from logged dicts.

### Back-compat — clean

- `auth_type` defaults to `"password"`; existing JSONB configs with no `auth_type` validate and behave exactly as before (no migration needed). Confirmed by `test_config_auth_type_defaults_to_password`. Follows the existing ADLS/S3/Airflow `auth_type` discriminator pattern.

### Cross-file — no breakage

Traced all callers of the renamed/changed functions:
- `build_snowflake_runner` callers — `dryrun_service.py:88`, `registry.py:80` — both keyword-only, signature unchanged.
- `SnowflakeCheckRunner(config, secret)` — only constructed inside `build_snowflake_runner`; the `password`→`secret` rename is positional-only, no external caller names the param.
- `build_connection_string` / `build_connect_args` — only internal + `profile_service.py` (updated in the PR) + tests.
- No caller anywhere passes `password=` by name.

All 28 tests in `test_snowflake.py` pass locally.

**Bottom line:** One real-but-minor finding (deprecated GX connect_args API → `DeprecationWarning` on every key-pair run; recommend switching to the `private_key=` kwarg). No correctness, security, or back-compat blockers.

class _FakeEngine:
    def __init__(self, executed: list[str]) -> None:
        self._executed = executed
        self.disposed = False

        return _FakeConn(self._executed)

    def dispose(self) -> None:
        self.disposed = True


def test_adapter_validate_config_returns_model() -> None:
    cfg = SnowflakeConnectionAdapter().validate_config(_CONFIG)
    assert isinstance(cfg, SnowflakeConfig)
    assert cfg.schema_ == "FINANCE"

def test_adapter_test_runs_select_1_and_disposes(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    executed: list[str] = []
    engine = _FakeEngine(executed)
    captured: dict[str, object] = {}

    def fake_create_engine(url: str, **kwargs: object) -> _FakeEngine:
        captured["url"] = url
        captured["connect_args"] = kwargs.get("connect_args")
        return engine

    monkeypatch.setattr("sqlalchemy.create_engine", fake_create_engine)
    SnowflakeConnectionAdapter().test(_CONFIG, "p@ss")

    assert executed == ["SELECT 1"]
    assert engine.disposed is True
    assert captured["connect_args"] == {"login_timeout": 10, "network_timeout": 10}
    assert "p%40ss" in str(captured["url"])  # password URL-encoded into the DSN


def test_adapter_test_disposes_engine_on_failure(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    engine = _FakeEngine([])

    def boom_connect() -> _FakeConn:
        raise RuntimeError("warehouse unreachable")

    engine.connect = boom_connect  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    monkeypatch.setattr("sqlalchemy.create_engine", lambda url, **kw: engine)

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="warehouse unreachable"):
        SnowflakeConnectionAdapter().test(_CONFIG, "p@ss")

=== current useAsyncData (to extend with reload) ===
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

/** Three-state result of a one-shot async fetch. */
export type AsyncState<T> =
  | { status: 'loading' }
  | { status: 'ok'; data: T }
  | { status: 'error'; error: string };

/**
 * Fetch once on mount, with a cancelled-guard so a late resolution after unmount
 * doesn't set state, and rejection normalised to a string `error`. Shared by the
 * data pages (Home, Connections, …) so the cancelled-effect dance lives in one
 * place rather than being re-derived per page.
 */
export function useAsyncData<T>(fetcher: () => Promise<T>): AsyncState<T> {
  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<T>>({ status: 'loading' });

  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false;
    fetcher()
      .then((data) => {
        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', data });
      })
      .catch((err: unknown) => {
        if (!cancelled) {
          setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
        }
      });
    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
    };
    // Fetch once on mount; the fetcher identity is intentionally not a dependency.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  return state;
}
```

{

  "content": "import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from 'react';\n\n/** Three-state result of an async fetch. */\nexport type AsyncState<T> =\n  | { status: 'loading' }\n  | { status: 'ok'; data: T }\n  | { status: 'error'; error: string };\n\n/**\n * Fetch on mount (and on `reload()`), with a cancelled-guard so a late\n * resolution after unmount doesn't set state, and rejection normalised to a\n * string `error`. Shared by the data pages (Home, Connections, …) so the\n * cancelled-effect dance lives in one place rather than being re-derived per page.\n *\n * `reload` re-runs the fetcher (e.g. after a mutation) while keeping the current\n * data visible until the refetch resolves — no flash back to the loading state.\n */\nexport function useAsyncData<T>(fetcher: () => Promise<T>): {\n  state: AsyncState<T>;\n  reload: () => void;\n} {\n  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<T>>({ status: 'loading' });\n  const [nonce, setNonce] = useState(0);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    let cancelled = false;\n    fetcher()\n      .then((data) => {\n        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', data });\n      })\n      .catch((err: unknown) => {\n        if (!cancelled) {\n          setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });\n        }\n      });\n    return () => {\n      cancelled = true;\n    };\n    // Re-run on mount and whenever `reload` bumps the nonce; the fetcher identity\n    // is intentionally not a dependency.\n    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps\n  }, [nonce]);\n\n  const reload = useCallback(() => setNonce((n) => n + 1), []);\n  return { state, reload };\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/components/connections/ConnectionTypeFields.tsx",
  "content": "import { Form, Input, Select, type FormInstance } from 'antd';\n\nimport type { ConnectionType } from '../../api/connections';\n\n/**\n * Type-specific config + secret form fields for the add-connection drawer.\n *\n * Config fields are namespaced under `config` (e.g. name={['config','account']})\n * so the drawer can submit `config` as one object; the write-only credential is\n * the top-level `secret`. Each type's fields mirror its backend Pydantic config\n * (extra=\"forbid\"), and the auth-type selects drive which credential fields show\n * and whether a secret is required (managed-identity / IAM-role need none).\n */\n\nconst required = [{ required: true }];\n\ninterface TextField {\n  name: string;\n  label: string;\n  required?: boolean;\n}\n\n// Always-shown text fields per type (the auth-type-driven parts are below).\nconst TEXT_FIELDS: Record<ConnectionType, TextField[]> = {\n  snowflake: [\n    { name: 'account', label: 'Account', required: true },\n    { name: 'user', label: 'User', required: true },\n    { name: 'database', label: 'Database', required: true },\n    { name: 'schema', label: 'Schema', required: true },\n    { name: 'warehouse', label: 'Warehouse', required: true },\n    { name: 'role', label: 'Role (optional)' },\n  ],\n  adls_gen2: [\n    { name: 'account_url', label: 'Account URL', required: true },\n    { name: 'container', label: 'Container', required: true },\n  ],\n  s3: [\n    { name: 'bucket', label: 'Bucket', required: true },\n    { name: 'region', label: 'Region', required: true },\n  ],\n  unity_catalog: [\n    { name: 'workspace_url', label: 'Workspace URL', required: true },\n    { name: 'warehouse_id', label: 'Warehouse ID', required: true },\n  ],\n  adf: [\n    { name: 'subscription_id', label: 'Subscription ID', required: true },\n    { name: 'resource_group', label: 'Resource group', required: true },\n    { name: 'factory_name', label: 'Factory name', required: true },\n    { name: 'tenant_id', label: 'Tenant ID', required: true },\n    { name: 'client_id', label: 'Client ID', required: true },\n  ],\n  airflow: [{ name: 'base_url', label: 'Base URL', required: true }],\n};\n\nfunction TextFields({ fields }: { fields: TextField[] }) {\n  return (\n    <>\n      {fields.map((f) => (\n        <Form.Item\n          key={f.name}\n          name={['config', f.name]}\n          label={f.label}\n          rules={f.required ? required : undefined}\n        >\n          <Input />\n        </Form.Item>\n      ))}\n    </>\n  );\n}\n\n/** A required secret input (password-masked, or multiline for PEM keys). */\nfunction SecretField({ label, multiline = false }: { label: string; multiline?: boolean }) {\n  return (\n    <Form.Item name=\"secret\" label={label} rules={required}>\n      {multiline ? <Input.TextArea rows={4} autoComplete=\"off\" /> : <Input.Password autoComplete=\"off\" />}\n    </Form.Item>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction AuthTypeSelect({ options }: { options: { value: string; label: string }[] }) {\n  return (\n    <Form.Item name={['config', 'auth_type']} label=\"Auth type\" rules={required}>\n      <Select options={options} />\n    </Form.Item>\n  );\n}\n\nexport function ConnectionTypeFields({ type, form }: { type: ConnectionType; form: FormInstance }) {\n  const authType = Form.useWatch(['config', 'auth_type'], form) as string | undefined;\n  const base = <TextFields fields={TEXT_FIELDS[type]} />;\n\n  switch (type) {\n    case 'snowflake':\n      // Password vs key-pair: the secret is the password or the PEM private key.\n      return (\n        <>\n          {base}\n          <AuthTypeSelect\n            options={[\n              { value: 'password', label: 'Password' },\n              { value: 'key_pair', label: 'Key pair (RSA)' },\n            ]}\n          />\n          {authType === 'key_pair' ? (\n            <SecretField label=\"Private key (PEM)\" multiline />\n          ) : (\n            <SecretField label=\"Password\" />\n          )}\n        </>\n      );\n    case 'adls_gen2':\n      // SAS needs a token; managed identity needs no stored secret.\n      return (\n        <>\n          {base}\n          <AuthTypeSelect\n            options={[\n              { value: 'sas', label: 'SAS token' },\n              { value: 'managed_identity', label: 'Managed identity' },\n            ]}\n          />\n          {authType !== 'managed_identity' && <SecretField label=\"SAS token\" />}\n        </>\n      );\n    case 's3':\n      // Access key needs an id + secret; IAM role needs neither.\n      return (\n        <>\n          {base}\n          <AuthTypeSelect\n            options={[\n              { value: 'access_key', label: 'Access key' },\n              { value: 'iam_role', label: 'IAM role' },\n            ]}\n          />\n          {authType !== 'iam_role' && (\n            <>\n              <Form.Item name={['config', 'access_key_id']} label=\"Access key ID\" rules={required}>\n                <Input />\n              </Form.Item>\n              <SecretField label=\"Secret access key\" />\n            </>\n          )}\n        </>\n      );\n    case 'airflow':\n      // Basic auth needs a username; token auth does not. Both need a secret.\n      return (\n        <>\n          {base}\n          <AuthTypeSelect\n            options={[\n              { value: 'token', label: 'Bearer token' },\n              { value: 'basic', label: 'Basic auth' },\n            ]}\n          />\n          {authType === 'basic' && (\n            <Form.Item name={['config', 'username']} label=\"Username\" rules={required}>\n              <Input />\n            </Form.Item>\n          )}\n          <SecretField label={authType === 'basic' ? 'Password' : 'Bearer token'} />\n        </>\n      );\n    case 'unity_catalog':\n      return (\n        <>\n          {base}\n          <SecretField label=\"Personal access token (PAT)\" />\n        </>\n      );\n    case 'adf':\n      return (\n        <>\n          {base}\n          <SecretField label=\"Client secret\" />\n        </>\n      );\n  }\n}\n\n/** Default `config.auth_type` for the types that have one (so the select starts set). */\nexport const DEFAULT_AUTH_TYPE: Partial<Record<ConnectionType, string>> = {\n  snowflake: 'password',\n  adls_gen2: 'sas',\n  s3: 'access_key',\n  airflow: 'token',\n};\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/components/connections/AddConnectionDrawer.tsx",
  "content": "import { App, Button, Drawer, Flex, Form, Input, Select } from 'antd';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nimport {\n  CONNECTION_ENVS,\n  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,\n  CONNECTION_TYPES,\n  type ConnectionCreate,\n  type ConnectionType,\n  createConnection,\n} from '../../api/connections';\nimport { ConnectionTypeFields, DEFAULT_AUTH_TYPE } from './ConnectionTypeFields';\n\ninterface FormValues {\n  name: string;\n  type: ConnectionType;\n  env: ConnectionCreate['env'];\n  config?: Record<string, unknown>;\n  secret?: string;\n}\n\nexport function AddConnectionDrawer({\n  open,\n  onClose,\n  onCreated,\n}: {\n  open: boolean;\n  onClose: () => void;\n  /** Called after a successful create (so the list can refresh). */\n  onCreated: () => void;\n}) {\n  const { message } = App.useApp();\n  const [form] = Form.useForm<FormValues>();\n  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);\n  const type = Form.useWatch('type', form) as ConnectionType | undefined;\n\n  // Switching type invalidates the previous config fields — reset them and seed\n  // the new type's default auth_type so its conditional fields render correctly.\n  const onTypeChange = (next: ConnectionType) => {\n    const authType = DEFAULT_AUTH_TYPE[next];\n    form.setFieldsValue({ config: authType ? { auth_type: authType } : {}, secret: undefined });\n  };\n\n  const onFinish = async (values: FormValues) => {\n    setSubmitting(true);\n    try {\n      await createConnection({\n        name: values.name,\n        type: values.type,\n        env: values.env,\n        config: values.config ?? {},\n        secret: values.secret || undefined,\n      });\n      message.success(`Connection “${values.name}” created`);\n      form.resetFields();\n      onCreated();\n    } catch (err) {\n      message.error(`Create failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);\n    } finally {\n      setSubmitting(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Drawer\n      title=\"Add connection\"\n      open={open}\n      onClose={onClose}\n      width={520}\n      destroyOnHidden\n      footer={\n        <Flex justify=\"end\" gap={8}>\n          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>\n          <Button type=\"primary\" loading={submitting} onClick={() => form.submit()}>\n            Create\n          </Button>\n        </Flex>\n      }\n    >\n      <Form form={form} layout=\"vertical\" onFinish={onFinish} requiredMark=\"optional\">\n        <Form.Item name=\"name\" label=\"Name\" rules={[{ required: true }]}>\n          <Input />\n        </Form.Item>\n        <Form.Item name=\"env\" label=\"Environment\" rules={[{ required: true }]}>\n          <Select\n            options={CONNECTION_ENVS.map((e) => ({ value: e, label: e.toUpperCase() }))}\n            placeholder=\"Select an environment\"\n          />\n        </Form.Item>\n        <Form.Item name=\"type\" label=\"Type\" rules={[{ required: true }]}>\n          <Select\n            placeholder=\"Select a connection type\"\n            onChange={onTypeChange}\n            options={CONNECTION_TYPES.map((t) => ({ value: t, label: CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[t] }))}\n          />\n        </Form.Item>\n        {type && <ConnectionTypeFields type={type} form={form} />}\n      </Form>\n    </Drawer>\n  );\n}\n"
}

## Review findings — `feat/week4-add-connection-drawer`

Ranked. The headline issue is altitude (#1), since it's the one most expensive to copy across the remaining Week-4 PRs.

### Worth fixing now (before the pattern multiplies)

**1. Auth-type/secret knowledge is split across two files and silently coupled by a magic-string contract — `ConnectionTypeFields.tsx` + `AddConnectionDrawer.tsx:21-26`**
The per-type auth options live in `ConnectionTypeFields`'s switch (e.g. `snowflake` → `password`/`key_pair`), but the *default* for each lives in a separate `DEFAULT_AUTH_TYPE` map in the drawer. These must agree by hand: `DEFAULT_AUTH_TYPE.snowflake = 'password'` only works because `'password'` is also an option value in the switch. Add a type, or rename an option value, and you must edit both files in sync with zero compile-time enforcement — `unity_catalog`/`adf` correctly have no default and no select, but nothing stops a future type from getting a default with no matching option (or vice versa). 
Maintenance cost: this is exactly the spec that the remaining connection PRs will extend; every new auth type is a two-file edit with a string contract the compiler can't check. **Fixing it now is cheap** — a single declarative per-type spec, e.g.:
```ts
const CONN_SPEC: Record<ConnectionType, {
  textFields: TextField[];
  auth?: { default: string; options: {value;label}[]; secretFor: (a) => SecretSpec | null };
}>
```
keyed off the option list so the default is `options[0].value` (or an explicit member of it) — collapses `TEXT_FIELDS`, `DEFAULT_AUTH_TYPE`, and the switch into one source of truth, and makes "which types need a secret vs not" (`managed_identity`/`iam_role` → none) data instead of scattered `authType !== '...'` conditionals. This is the right depth and the right moment.

**2. Env-label upper-casing duplicated — `AddConnectionDrawer.tsx:96` vs `Connections.tsx:136`**
`CONNECTION_ENVS.map((e) => ({ value: e, label: e.toUpperCase() }))` in the drawer and `{connection.env.toUpperCase()}` in the page Tag are the same display rule re-derived. Small, but it's display metadata about a shared enum living in two UI sites; the next PRs (suites, runs) will render env labels again. 
Maintenance cost: low individually, but it's the kind of literal that ends up in 5+ places. Cheap to hoist a `CONNECTION_ENV_LABELS` (or an `envLabel()` helper) next to `CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS` in `api/connections.ts` now, before it spreads. Worth doing as part of #1.

### Fine to defer

**3. Select-option test selector relies on an antd internal class — `AddConnectionDrawer.test.tsx:32**`
`findByText(option, { selector: '.ant-select-item-option-content' })` couples the suite to an antd DOM class. It's the conventional way to drive antd Select in RTL and the AntD v6 upgrade is already in `main`, so the immediate brittleness is bounded — but since this test is the template the other Week-4 component tests will copy, the `selectOption` helper is worth lifting into a shared `tests/support/antd.ts` (one place to fix if the class changes) rather than re-pasted per test file. Defer the extraction to whenever the second component test lands, but don't copy-paste the helper inline.

**4. `ResizeObserver` stub in `setup.ts` — fine.** Correct, standard jsdom gap fill, global and one-time. No action.

### Non-issues (checked, clearing them)
- `useAsyncData` `{state, reload}` change with `nonce` + keep-current-data-on-reload is clean and correctly migrated at both call sites (`Home.tsx` destructures `{state}`, `Connections.tsx` uses `reload`). Good.
- The `ConnectionsBody` extraction (header/drawer always mounted, body switches on state) is the right refactor — it fixes the prior bug where the "Add connection" button would've been hidden during loading/error. No notes.
- `secret: values.secret || undefined` correctly avoids sending an empty string for the no-secret auth types.

**Bottom line:** one finding genuinely worth acting on before merge — **#1**, fold `TEXT_FIELDS` + `DEFAULT_AUTH_TYPE` + the switch into a single per-type spec so adding a connection type is a one-place, compiler-checked edit. #2 rides along with it. #3/#4 are defer.

## Correctness review — `feat/week4-add-connection-drawer`

I read the diff, the antd v6 / rc-field-form v2.7 + rc-util `setFieldsValue` / `getFieldsValue` source, and the backend `ConnectionCreate` + all six per-type Pydantic configs (`extra="forbid"`).

### Premise corrections (candidates 2 & 3 — REFUTED)

The prompt's two headline worries do **not** materialize, because of how rc-field-form builds the `onFinish` payload:

- `onFinish`/`submit` → `validateFields()` → `getFieldsValue()` collects values **only from currently-mounted field entities** (`getFieldEntities(true)` filters to registered fields), reconstructing nested `config` from those name paths via `cloneByNamePathList`.
- Therefore unmounted Form.Items — whether hidden by a **type switch** or an **auth-type switch** — are excluded from the submitted payload, regardless of antd's `preserve: true` default (preserve keeps the value in `store`, but the entity is gone from `fieldEntities`, so it isn't emitted).

Concretely verified in `/tmp` against rc-field-form 2.7.0 / rc-util 5.43.0:
- **Candidate 2 (type-switch stale config → 422): REFUTED.** Switch Snowflake→S3 leaves `config.account` etc. in `store`, but they aren't mounted, so they never reach `createConnection`. (Note: the `onTypeChange` comment "reset them" is technically wrong — `setFieldsValue` does `merge(store, {config:{auth_type}})`, a deep merge that does *not* delete prior `config.*` keys — but the outcome is still correct because of the mounted-only collection.)
- **Candidate 3 (hidden secret / `access_key_id` leak on auth switch): REFUTED.** Same mechanism — the unmounted `secret` / `config.access_key_id` items are not collected.
- **Candidate 4 (useAsyncData reload race): REFUTED.** Each effect run captures its own `cancelled`; the prior run's cleanup sets `cancelled = true`, so a late first-fetch resolution after `reload()` can't write state. No stale closure (fetcher intentionally excluded; nonce drives re-run).
- **Candidate 5 (`secret: values.secret || undefined`): correct.** For credential-less modes the SecretField is unmounted → `values.secret` undefined → key omitted; backend `secret: str | None = None` accepts it. Field-name mapping (snowflake account/user/database/`schema`(aliased, `populate_by_name=True`)/warehouse/role, adls account_url/container, s3 bucket/region/access_key_id, uc workspace_url/warehouse_id, adf subscription_id/resource_group/factory_name/tenant_id/client_id, airflow base_url/username) all match the Pydantic configs; envs (`dev/qa/uat/prod`) match `models.ENVS`.

### CONFIRMED findings

**1. Frontend offers auth modes the backend rejects at create (422) — S3 `iam_role` and ADLS Gen2 `managed_identity`.**
- `frontend/src/components/connections/ConnectionTypeFields.tsx:148-152` (S3 `iam_role` option) and `:131-135` (ADLS `managed_identity` option).
- Backend: `backend/app/datasources/s3.py:47-51` (`model_validator` raises "iam_role auth is deferred to Week 7") and `backend/app/datasources/adls.py:53-57` ("managed_identity auth is deferred to Week 7"). These run on `validate_config` → `model_validate` at create time (`connection_service.create_connection` → `_validated_config`, before any test).
- Failure scenario: user picks S3 + "IAM role" (or ADLS + "Managed identity"), fills the visible fields (no secret prompted — consistent with "no stored credential"), clicks Create → backend 422. The form presents a v1-impossible path as a first-class choice. A maintainer should drop these options for v1 (or disable + label them "deferred").

**2. Backend validation `detail` is swallowed — every create failure shows a generic message.**
- `frontend/src/components/connections/AddConnectionDrawer.tsx:60` — `message.error(\`Create failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}\`)`.
- `frontend/src/api/client.ts` has only a **request** interceptor (`:20`); no response interceptor maps the FastAPI error envelope's `detail` onto the thrown error. So `err.message` is axios's generic `"Request failed with status code 422"`.
- Failure scenario: any create rejection — the deferred-auth 422 above, an `extra="forbid"` key, or the orchestrator-singleton/duplicate-name **409** (`connection_service` raises a precise `detail`) — all surface to the user as `"Create failed: Request failed with status code 4xx"`, discarding the actionable backend message (e.g. "an orchestration connection of type 'adf' already exists in env 'dev'"). Worth either a response interceptor that unwraps `detail`, or unwrapping at this call site.

### Notes (no action needed)
- Tests don't cover type-switch-after-fill or auth-switch-after-fill (the scenarios the prompt worried about). They're safe per the analysis above, but adding a "switch type then submit" assertion would lock in that the payload stays clean if antd internals ever change.
- `onTypeChange` comment is misleading (deep-merge, not reset) but behaviorally harmless — optional cleanup.

Net: the form-payload correctness (field names, type/auth switching, secret omission, reload race) is sound. The two real, maintainer-actionable issues are both at the UX/error-surfacing boundary: offering backend-rejected auth modes, and swallowing the backend's `detail` on failure.

(\n        <Input.TextArea rows={4} autoComplete=\"off\" />\n      ) : (\n        <Input.Password autoComplete=\"off\" />\n      )}\n    </Form.Item>\n  );\n}\n\nexport function ConnectionTypeFields({ type, form }: { type: ConnectionType; form: FormInstance }) {\n  const spec = SPECS[type];\n  const authType = Form.useWatch(['config', 'auth_type'], form) as string | undefined;\n  const activeAuth = spec.auth?.find((a) => a.value === authType) ?? spec.auth?.[0];\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      {spec.textFields.map((f) => (\n        <ConfigTextField key={f.name} field={f} />\n      ))}\n\n      {spec.auth && (\n        <Form.Item name={['config', 'auth_type']} label=\"Auth type\" rules={requiredRule}>\n          <Select options={spec.auth.map((a) => ({ value: a.value, label: a.label }))} />\n        </Form.Item>\n      )}\n\n      {activeAuth?.extraField && <ConfigTextField field={activeAuth.extraField} />}\n\n      {activeAuth ? (\n        <SecretField label={activeAuth.secretLabel} multiline={activeAuth.multilineSecret} />\n      ) : (\n        spec.secretLabel && <SecretField label={spec.secretLabel} />\n      )}\n    </>\n  );\n}\n"

fields and either an auth-type select (the\n * first option is the default) or a single secret. v1 only declares the auth\n * modes the backend accepts — ADLS Gen2's managed-identity and S3's IAM-role\n * modes are deferred, so they're absent here; every declared mode needs a secret.\n */\n\nexport interface TextField {\n  name: string;\n  label: string;\n  optional?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface AuthOption {\n  value: string;\n  label: string;\n  /** Label for the secret this mode needs. */\n  secretLabel: string;\n  /** Secret is a multi-line PEM key rather than a single-line password. */\n  multilineSecret?: boolean;\n  /** An extra config field this mode needs (e.g. Airflow basic → username). */\n  extraField?: TextField;\n}\n\nexport interface TypeSpec {\n  textFields: TextField[];\n  /** Present → the type has an auth-type select; the first option is the default. */\n  auth?: AuthOption[];\n  /** Present (and no `auth`) → a single secret field with this label. */\n  secretLabel?: string;\n}\n\nexport const CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS: Record<ConnectionType, TypeSpec> = {\n  snowflake: {\n    textFields: [\n      { name: 'account', label: 'Account' },\n      { name: 'user', label: 'User' },\n      { name: 'database', label: 'Database' },\n      { name: 'schema', label: 'Schema' },\n      { name: 'warehouse', label: 'Warehouse' },\n      { name: 'role', label: 'Role', optional: true },\n    ],\n    auth: [\n      { value: 'password', label: 'Password', secretLabel: 'Password' },\n      {\n        value: 'key_pair',\n        label: 'Key pair (RSA)',\n        secretLabel: 'Private key (PEM)',\n        multilineSecret: true,\n      },\n    ],\n  },\n  adls_gen2: {\n    textFields: [\n      { name: 'account_url', label: 'Account URL' },\n      { name: 'container', label: 'Container' },\n    ],\n    secretLabel: 'SAS token',\n  },\n  s3: {\n    textFields: [\n      { name: 'bucket', label: 'Bucket' },\n      { name: 'region', label: 'Region' },\n      { name: 'access_key_id', label: 'Access key ID' },\n    ],\n    secretLabel: 'Secret access key',\n  },\n  unity_catalog: {\n    textFields: [\n      { name: 'workspace_url', label: 'Workspace URL' },\n      { name: 'warehouse_id', label: 'Warehouse ID' },\n    ],\n    secretLabel: 'Personal access token (PAT)',\n  },\n  adf: {\n    textFields: [\n      { name: 'subscription_id', label: 'Subscription ID' },\n      { name: 'resource_group', label: 'Resource group' },\n      { name: 'factory_name', label: 'Factory name' },\n      { name: 'tenant_id', label: 'Tenant ID' },\n      { name: 'client_id', label: 'Client ID' },\n    ],\n    secretLabel: 'Client secret',\n  },\n  airflow: {\n    textFields: [{ name: 'base_url', label: 'Base URL' }],\n    auth: [\n      { value: 'token', label: 'Bearer token', secretLabel: 'Bearer token' },\n      {\n        value: 'basic',\n        label: 'Basic auth',\n        secretLabel: 'Password',\n        extraField: { name: 'username', label: 'Username' },\n      },\n    ],\n  },\n};\n\n/** Initial `config` for a freshly-selected type (seeds the default auth_type). */\nexport function initialConfigForType(type: ConnectionType): Record<string, unknown> {\n  const auth = CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS[type].auth;\n  return auth ? { auth_type: auth[0].value } : {};\n}\n"

(\n        <Input.TextArea rows={4} autoComplete=\"off\" />\n      ) : (\n        <Input.Password autoComplete=\"off\" />\n      )}\n    </Form.Item>\n  );\n}\n\nexport function ConnectionTypeFields({ type, form }: { type: ConnectionType; form: FormInstance }) {\n  const spec = CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS[type];\n  const authType = Form.useWatch(['config', 'auth_type'], form) as string | undefined;\n  const activeAuth = spec.auth?.find((a) => a.value === authType) ?? spec.auth?.[0];\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      {spec.textFields.map((f) => (\n        <ConfigTextField key={f.name} field={f} />\n      ))}\n\n      {spec.auth && (\n        <Form.Item name={['config', 'auth_type']} label=\"Auth type\" rules={requiredRule}>\n          <Select options={spec.auth.map((a) => ({ value: a.value, label: a.label }))} />\n        </Form.Item>\n      )}\n\n      {activeAuth?.extraField && <ConfigTextField field={activeAuth.extraField} />}\n\n      {activeAuth ? (\n        <SecretField label={activeAuth.secretLabel} multiline={activeAuth.multilineSecret} />\n      ) : (\n        spec.secretLabel && <SecretField label={spec.secretLabel} />\n      )}\n    </>\n  );\n}\n"
}

=== api/connections.ts (current) ===
import { api } from './client';

/**
 * Connections API — the six configurable connection types (CLAUDE.md §4).
 * ADF + Airflow are orchestration providers, not datasources, but they are
 * still `connections` rows and managed through the same CRUD surface.
 */

export const CONNECTION_TYPES = [
  'snowflake',
  'adls_gen2',
  's3',
  'unity_catalog',
  'adf',
  'airflow',
] as const;
export type ConnectionType = (typeof CONNECTION_TYPES)[number];

export const CONNECTION_ENVS = ['dev', 'qa', 'uat', 'prod'] as const;
export type ConnectionEnv = (typeof CONNECTION_ENVS)[number];

/** Display label for an env (single source for the list page + the drawer). */
export const envLabel = (env: ConnectionEnv): string => env.toUpperCase();

/** Mirrors the backend `ConnectionRead` schema (secret is never returned). */
export interface Connection {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  type: ConnectionType;
  env: ConnectionEnv;
  config: Record<string, unknown>;
  has_secret: boolean;
  created_by: string;
}

/** Human-readable labels for the connection types, for grouping + display. */
export const CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS: Record<ConnectionType, string> = {
  snowflake: 'Snowflake',
  adls_gen2: 'ADLS Gen2',
  s3: 'AWS S3',
  unity_catalog: 'Unity Catalog',
  adf: 'Azure Data Factory',
  airflow: 'Airflow',
};

export async function listConnections(params?: {
  type?: ConnectionType;
  env?: ConnectionEnv;
}): Promise<Connection[]> {
  const { data } = await api.get<Connection[]>('/connections', { params });
  return data;
}

/** Live connectivity test — a green result means the credential authenticates. */
export async function testConnection(id: string): Promise<{ ok: boolean }> {
  const { data } = await api.post<{ ok: boolean }>(`/connections/${id}/test`);
  return data;
}

/** Mirrors the backend `ConnectionCreate` schema (secret is write-only). */
export interface ConnectionCreate {
  name: string;
  type: ConnectionType;
  env: ConnectionEnv;
  config: Record<string, unknown>;
  secret?: string;
}

export async function createConnection(payload: ConnectionCreate): Promise<Connection> {
  const { data } = await api.post<Connection>('/connections', payload);
  return data;
}

import type { ConnectionType } from '../../api/connections';

/**
 * Single source of truth for the add-connection form's per-type fields.
 *
 * Each type declares its config text fields and either an auth-type select (the
 * first option is the default) or a single secret. v1 only declares the auth
 * modes the backend accepts — ADLS Gen2's managed-identity and S3's IAM-role
 * modes are deferred, so they're absent here; every declared mode needs a secret.
 */

export interface TextField {
  name: string;
  label: string;
  optional?: boolean;
}

export interface AuthOption {
  value: string;
  label: string;
  /** Label for the secret this mode needs. */
  secretLabel: string;
  /** Secret is a multi-line PEM key rather than a single-line password. */
  multilineSecret?: boolean;
  /** An extra config field this mode needs (e.g. Airflow basic → username). */
  extraField?: TextField;
}

export interface TypeSpec {
  textFields: TextField[];
  /** Present → the type has an auth-type select; the first option is the default. */
  auth?: AuthOption[];
  /** Present (and no `auth`) → a single secret field with this label. */
  secretLabel?: string;
}

=== Connections.tsx (current) ===
import { Alert, App, Badge, Button, Card, Empty, Flex, Spin, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';
import { useState } from 'react';

import {
  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,
  CONNECTION_TYPES,
  type Connection,
  type ConnectionEnv,
  type ConnectionType,
  envLabel,
  listConnections,
  testConnection,
} from '../api/connections';
import { AddConnectionDrawer } from '../components/connections/AddConnectionDrawer';
import { type AsyncState, useAsyncData } from '../hooks/useAsyncData';

const ENV_COLORS: Record<ConnectionEnv, string> = {
  dev: 'blue',
  qa: 'gold',
  uat: 'purple',
  prod: 'red',
};

/** Group connections by type in one pass, preserving canonical type order. */
function groupByType(connections: Connection[]): [ConnectionType, Connection[]][] {
  const byType = new Map<ConnectionType, Connection[]>();
  for (const c of connections) {
    const group = byType.get(c.type);
    if (group) group.push(c);
    else byType.set(c.type, [c]);
  }
  return CONNECTION_TYPES.filter((type) => byType.has(type)).map((type) => [
    type,
    byType.get(type) as Connection[],
  ]);
}

export function Connections() {
  const { state, reload } = useAsyncData(listConnections);
  const [drawerOpen, setDrawerOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <Flex vertical gap={24}>
      <Flex justify="space-between" align="center" gap={12}>
        <Typography.Title level={3} style={{ margin: 0 }}>
          Connections
        </Typography.Title>
        <Button type="primary" onClick={() => setDrawerOpen(true)}>
          Add connection
        </Button>
      </Flex>
      <ConnectionsBody state={state} />
      <AddConnectionDrawer
        open={drawerOpen}
        onClose={() => setDrawerOpen(false)}
        onCreated={() => {
          setDrawerOpen(false);
          reload();
        }}
      />
    </Flex>
  );
}

function ConnectionsBody({ state }: { state: AsyncState<Connection[]> }) {
  if (state.status === 'loading') {
    return <Spin tip="Loading connections…" size="large" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;
  }
  if (state.status === 'error') {
    return (
      <Alert
        type="error"
        showIcon
        title="Failed to load connections"
        description={state.error}
        style={{ margin: 24 }}
      />
    );
  }
  const connections = state.data;
  if (connections.length === 0) {
    return <Empty description="No connections configured yet" />;
  }
  return (
    <>
      {groupByType(connections).map(([type, group]) => (
        <ConnectionTypeSection key={type} type={type} connections={group} />
      ))}
    </>
  );
}

function ConnectionTypeSection({
  type,
  connections,
}: {
  type: ConnectionType;
  connections: Connection[];
}) {
  return (
    <Flex vertical gap={12}>
      <Typography.Title level={5} style={{ margin: 0 }}>
        {CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[type]}
      </Typography.Title>
      <Flex wrap gap={12}>
        {connections.map((connection) => (
          <ConnectionCard key={connection.id} connection={connection} />
        ))}
      </Flex>
    </Flex>
  );
}

function ConnectionCard({ connection }: { connection: Connection }) {
  const { message } = App.useApp();
  const [testing, setTesting] = useState(false);

  const onTest = async () => {
    setTesting(true);
    try {
      const { ok } = await testConnection(connection.id);
      if (ok) message.success(`${connection.name}: connection OK`);
      else message.error(`${connection.name}: connection test failed`);
    } catch (err) {
      message.error(`${connection.name}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'test failed'}`);
    } finally {
      setTesting(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <Card size="small" style={{ minWidth: 280 }}>
      <Flex justify="space-between" align="center" gap={12}>
        <Flex vertical gap={6}>
          <Typography.Text strong>{connection.name}</Typography.Text>
          <Flex gap={8} align="center">
            <Tag color={ENV_COLORS[connection.env]}>{envLabel(connection.env)}</Tag>
            {connection.has_secret ? (
              <Badge status="success" text="credential set" />
            ) : (
              <Badge status="warning" text="no credential" />
            )}
          </Flex>
        </Flex>
        <Button size="small" loading={testing} onClick={onTest}>
          Test
        </Button>
      </Flex>
    </Card>
  );
}
=== AddConnectionDrawer.tsx (current) ===
import { App, Button, Drawer, Flex, Form, Input, Select } from 'antd';
import { useState } from 'react';

import {
  CONNECTION_ENVS,
  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,
  CONNECTION_TYPES,
  type ConnectionCreate,
  type ConnectionType,
  createConnection,
  envLabel,
} from '../../api/connections';
import { ConnectionTypeFields } from './ConnectionTypeFields';
import { initialConfigForType } from './connectionFormSpec';

interface FormValues {
  name: string;
  type: ConnectionType;
  env: ConnectionCreate['env'];
  config?: Record<string, unknown>;
  secret?: string;
}

export function AddConnectionDrawer({
  open,
  onClose,
  onCreated,
}: {
  open: boolean;
  onClose: () => void;
  /** Called after a successful create (so the list can refresh). */
  onCreated: () => void;
}) {
  const { message } = App.useApp();
  const [form] = Form.useForm<FormValues>();
  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
  const type = Form.useWatch('type', form) as ConnectionType | undefined;

  // Switching type invalidates the previous config fields — reset them and seed
  // the new type's default auth_type so its conditional fields render correctly.
  // (Submission only collects mounted fields, but reset keeps the live form tidy.)
  const onTypeChange = (next: ConnectionType) => {
    form.setFieldsValue({ config: initialConfigForType(next), secret: undefined });
  };

  const onFinish = async (values: FormValues) => {
    setSubmitting(true);
    try {
      await createConnection({
        name: values.name,
        type: values.type,
        env: values.env,
        config: values.config ?? {},
        secret: values.secret || undefined,
      });
      message.success(`Connection “${values.name}” created`);
      form.resetFields();
      onCreated();
    } catch (err) {
      message.error(`Create failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
    } finally {
      setSubmitting(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <Drawer
      title="Add connection"
      open={open}
      onClose={onClose}
      width={520}
      destroyOnHidden
      footer={
        <Flex justify="end" gap={8}>
          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>
          <Button type="primary" loading={submitting} onClick={() => form.submit()}>
            Create
          </Button>
        </Flex>
      }
    >
      <Form form={form} layout="vertical" onFinish={onFinish} requiredMark="optional">
        <Form.Item name="name" label="Name" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
          <Input />
        </Form.Item>
        <Form.Item name="env" label="Environment" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
          <Select
            options={CONNECTION_ENVS.map((e) => ({ value: e, label: envLabel(e) }))}
            placeholder="Select an environment"
          />
        </Form.Item>
        <Form.Item name="type" label="Type" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
          <Select
            placeholder="Select a connection type"
            onChange={onTypeChange}
            options={CONNECTION_TYPES.map((t) => ({ value: t, label: CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[t] }))}
          />
        </Form.Item>
        {type && <ConnectionTypeFields type={type} form={form} />}
      </Form>
    </Drawer>
  );
}
```

  "content": "import { App, Button, Drawer, Flex, Form, Input, Select } from 'antd';\nimport { useEffect, useState } from 'react';\n\nimport {\n  CONNECTION_ENVS,\n  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,\n  CONNECTION_TYPES,\n  type Connection,\n  type ConnectionCreate,\n  type ConnectionType,\n  createConnection,\n  envLabel,\n  updateConnection,\n} from '../../api/connections';\nimport { ConnectionTypeFields } from './ConnectionTypeFields';\nimport { initialConfigForType } from './connectionFormSpec';\n\ninterface FormValues {\n  name: string;\n  type: ConnectionType;\n  env: ConnectionCreate['env'];\n  config?: Record<string, unknown>;\n  secret?: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Create or edit a connection. In edit mode (`connection` present), type + env\n * are immutable (the backend `ConnectionUpdate` rejects them) and the secret is\n * omitted — credential rotation is the separate Re-auth flow.\n */\nexport function ConnectionDrawer({\n  open,\n  onClose,\n  onSaved,\n  connection,\n}: {\n  open: boolean;\n  onClose: () => void;\n  /** Called after a successful create or update (so the list can refresh). */\n  onSaved: () => void;\n  connection?: Connection;\n}) {\n  const isEdit = connection !== undefined;\n  const { message } = App.useApp();\n  const [form] = Form.useForm<FormValues>();\n  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);\n  const watchedType = Form.useWatch('type', form) as ConnectionType | undefined;\n  const type = isEdit ? connection.type : watchedType;\n\n  // Prefill when opening in edit mode (the Drawer's destroyOnHidden remounts the\n  // form each open, so this re-seeds for whichever connection is being edited).\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (open && connection) {\n      form.setFieldsValue({\n        name: connection.name,\n        type: connection.type,\n        env: connection.env,\n        config: connection.config,\n      });\n    }\n  }, [open, connection, form]);\n\n  // Switching type (create only) invalidates the previous config fields.\n  const onTypeChange = (next: ConnectionType) => {\n    form.setFieldsValue({ config: initialConfigForType(next), secret: undefined });\n  };\n\n  const onFinish = async (values: FormValues) => {\n    setSubmitting(true);\n    try {\n      if (isEdit) {\n        await updateConnection(connection.id, {\n          name: values.name,\n          config: values.config ?? {},\n        });\n        message.success(`Connection “${values.name}” updated`);\n      } else {\n        await createConnection({\n          name: values.name,\n          type: values.type,\n          env: values.env,\n          config: values.config ?? {},\n          secret: values.secret || undefined,\n        });\n        message.success(`Connection “${values.name}” created`);\n      }\n      form.resetFields();\n      onSaved();\n    } catch (err) {\n      message.error(\n        `${isEdit ? 'Update' : 'Create'} failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`,\n      );\n    } finally {\n      setSubmitting(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Drawer\n      title={isEdit ? 'Edit connection' : 'Add connection'}\n      open={open}\n      onClose={onClose}\n      width={520}\n      destroyOnHidden\n      footer={\n        <Flex justify=\"end\" gap={8}>\n          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>\n          <Button type=\"primary\" loading={submitting} onClick={() => form.submit()}>\n            {isEdit ? 'Save' : 'Create'}\n          </Button>\n        </Flex>\n      }\n    >\n      <Form form={form} layout=\"vertical\" onFinish={onFinish} requiredMark=\"optional\">\n        <Form.Item name=\"name\" label=\"Name\" rules={[{ required: true }]}>\n          <Input />\n        </Form.Item>\n        <Form.Item name=\"env\" label=\"Environment\" rules={[{ required: true }]}>\n          <Select\n            disabled={isEdit}\n            options={CONNECTION_ENVS.map((e) => ({ value: e, label: envLabel(e) }))}\n            placeholder=\"Select an environment\"\n          />\n        </Form.Item>\n        <Form.Item name=\"type\" label=\"Type\" rules={[{ required: true }]}>\n          <Select\n            disabled={isEdit}\n            placeholder=\"Select a connection type\"\n            onChange={onTypeChange}\n            options={CONNECTION_TYPES.map((t) => ({ value: t, label: CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[t] }))}\n          />\n        </Form.Item>\n        {type && <ConnectionTypeFields type={type} form={form} showSecret={!isEdit} />}\n      </Form>\n    </Drawer>\n  );\n}\n"
}
