{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/components/connections/ReauthModal.tsx",
  "content": "import { App, Form, Input, Modal } from 'antd';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nimport { type Connection, reauthConnection } from '../../api/connections';\n\n/**\n * Rotate a connection's stored credential. The backend verifies the new\n * credential against the datasource, so a bad value surfaces as an error and the\n * old credential is unaffected. `connection === null` means the modal is closed.\n */\nexport function ReauthModal({\n  connection,\n  onClose,\n  onDone,\n}: {\n  connection: Connection | null;\n  onClose: () => void;\n  /** Called after a successful rotation (so the list can refresh `has_secret`). */\n  onDone: () => void;\n}) {\n  const { message } = App.useApp();\n  const [form] = Form.useForm<{ secret: string }>();\n  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);\n\n  const onOk = async () => {\n    if (!connection) return;\n    const { secret } = await form.validateFields();\n    setSubmitting(true);\n    try {\n      await reauthConnection(connection.id, secret);\n      message.success(`${connection.name}: credential rotated`);\n      form.resetFields();\n      onDone();\n    } catch (err) {\n      message.error(`Re-auth failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);\n    } finally {\n      setSubmitting(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Modal\n      title={connection ? `Re-authenticate “${connection.name}”` : 'Re-authenticate'}\n      open={connection !== null}\n      onOk={onOk}\n      onCancel={onClose}\n      confirmLoading={submitting}\n      okText=\"Rotate credential\"\n      destroyOnHidden\n    >\n      <Form form={form} layout=\"vertical\">\n        <Form.Item\n          name=\"secret\"\n          label=\"New credential\"\n          rules={[{ required: true }]}\n          extra=\"Rotates the stored credential and verifies it against the datasource.\"\n        >\n          <Input.Password autoComplete=\"off\" />\n        </Form.Item>\n      </Form>\n    </Modal>\n  );\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { MoreOutlined } from '@ant-design/icons';\nimport { Alert, App, Badge, Button, Card, Dropdown, Empty, Flex, Spin, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nimport {\n  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,\n  CONNECTION_TYPES,\n  type Connection,\n  type ConnectionEnv,\n  type ConnectionType,\n  deleteConnection,\n  envLabel,\n  listConnections,\n  testConnection,\n} from '../api/connections';\nimport { ConnectionDrawer } from '../components/connections/ConnectionDrawer';\nimport { ReauthModal } from '../components/connections/ReauthModal';\nimport { type AsyncState, useAsyncData } from '../hooks/useAsyncData';\n\nconst ENV_COLORS: Record<ConnectionEnv, string> = {\n  dev: 'blue',\n  qa: 'gold',\n  uat: 'purple',\n  prod: 'red',\n};\n\n/** Per-card actions, threaded from the page so they can mutate shared state. */\ninterface ConnectionActions {\n  onEdit: (connection: Connection) => void;\n  onReauth: (connection: Connection) => void;\n  onChanged: () => void;\n}\n\n/** Group connections by type in one pass, preserving canonical type order. */\nfunction groupByType(connections: Connection[]): [ConnectionType, Connection[]][] {\n  const byType = new Map<ConnectionType, Connection[]>();\n  for (const c of connections) {\n    const group = byType.get(c.type);\n    if (group) group.push(c);\n    else byType.set(c.type, [c]);\n  }\n  return CONNECTION_TYPES.filter((type) => byType.has(type)).map((type) => [\n    type,\n    byType.get(type) as Connection[],\n  ]);\n}\n\nexport function Connections() {\n  const { state, reload } = useAsyncData(listConnections);\n  // `drawer.connection === undefined` while open = create mode; a connection = edit.\n  const [drawer, setDrawer] = useState<{ open: boolean; connection?: Connection }>({ open: false });\n  const [reauthing, setReauthing] = useState<Connection | null>(null);\n\n  const actions: ConnectionActions = {\n    onEdit: (connection) => setDrawer({ open: true, connection }),\n    onReauth: setReauthing,\n    onChanged: reload,\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical gap={24}>\n      <Flex justify=\"space-between\" align=\"center\" gap={12}>\n        <Typography.Title level={3} style={{ margin: 0 }}>\n          Connections\n        </Typography.Title>\n        <Button type=\"primary\" onClick={() => setDrawer({ open: true })}>\n          Add connection\n        </Button>\n      </Flex>\n      <ConnectionsBody state={state} actions={actions} />\n      <ConnectionDrawer\n        open={drawer.open}\n        connection={drawer.connection}\n        onClose={() => setDrawer({ open: false })}\n        onSaved={() => {\n          setDrawer({ open: false });\n          reload();\n        }}\n      />\n      <ReauthModal\n        connection={reauthing}\n        onClose={() => setReauthing(null)}\n        onDone={() => {\n          setReauthing(null);\n          reload();\n        }}\n      />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction ConnectionsBody({\n  state,\n  actions,\n}: {\n  state: AsyncState<Connection[]>;\n  actions: ConnectionActions;\n}) {\n  if (state.status === 'loading') {\n    return <Spin tip=\"Loading connections…\" size=\"large\" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;\n  }\n  if (state.status === 'error') {\n    return (\n      <Alert\n        type=\"error\"\n        showIcon\n        title=\"Failed to load connections\"\n        description={state.error}\n        style={{ margin: 24 }}\n      />\n    );\n  }\n  const connections = state.data;\n  if (connections.length === 0) {\n    return <Empty description=\"No connections configured yet\" />;\n  }\n  return (\n    <>\n      {groupByType(connections).map(([type, group]) => (\n        <ConnectionTypeSection key={type} type={type} connections={group} actions={actions} />\n      ))}\n    </>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction ConnectionTypeSection({\n  type,\n  connections,\n  actions,\n}: {\n  type: ConnectionType;\n  connections: Connection[];\n  actions: ConnectionActions;\n}) {\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical gap={12}>\n      <Typography.Title level={5} style={{ margin: 0 }}>\n        {CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[type]}\n      </Typography.Title>\n      <Flex wrap gap={12}>\n        {connections.map((connection) => (\n          <ConnectionCard key={connection.id} connection={connection} actions={actions} />\n        ))}\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction ConnectionCard({\n  connection,\n  actions,\n}: {\n  connection: Connection;\n  actions: ConnectionActions;\n}) {\n  const { message, modal } = App.useApp();\n  const [testing, setTesting] = useState(false);\n\n  const onTest = async () => {\n    setTesting(true);\n    try {\n      const { ok } = await testConnection(connection.id);\n      if (ok) message.success(`${connection.name}: connection OK`);\n      else message.error(`${connection.name}: connection test failed`);\n    } catch (err) {\n      message.error(`${connection.name}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'test failed'}`);\n    } finally {\n      setTesting(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  const onDelete = () => {\n    modal.confirm({\n      title: `Delete “${connection.name}”?`,\n      content: 'This removes the connection and its stored credential.',\n      okText: 'Delete',\n      okType: 'danger',\n      onOk: async () => {\n        try {\n          await deleteConnection(connection.id);\n          message.success(`${connection.name} deleted`);\n          actions.onChanged();\n        } catch (err) {\n          message.error(`Delete failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);\n          throw err; // keep the confirm modal open on failure\n        }\n      },\n    });\n  };\n\n  const menuItems = [\n    { key: 'edit', label: 'Edit', onClick: () => actions.onEdit(connection) },\n    { key: 'reauth', label: 'Re-authenticate', onClick: () => actions.onReauth(connection) },\n    { type: 'divider' as const },\n    { key: 'delete', label: 'Delete', danger: true, onClick: onDelete },\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <Card size=\"small\" style={{ minWidth: 280 }}>\n      <Flex justify=\"space-between\" align=\"center\" gap={12}>\n        <Flex vertical gap={6}>\n          <Typography.Text strong>{connection.name}</Typography.Text>\n          <Flex gap={8} align=\"center\">\n            <Tag color={ENV_COLORS[connection.env]}>{envLabel(connection.env)}</Tag>\n            {connection.has_secret ? (\n              <Badge status=\"success\" text=\"credential set\" />\n            ) : (\n              <Badge status=\"warning\" text=\"no credential\" />\n            )}\n          </Flex>\n        </Flex>\n        <Flex gap={8} align=\"center\">\n          <Button size=\"small\" loading={testing} onClick={onTest}>\n            Test\n          </Button>\n          <Dropdown menu={{ items: menuItems }} trigger={['click']}>\n            <Button size=\"small\" icon={<MoreOutlined />} aria-label={`${connection.name} actions`} />\n          </Dropdown>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n    </Card>\n  );\n}\n"
}

I have enough to assess all five points. Let me verify one detail about the `message`/error-toast pattern count by checking the original Connections card handler (the `onTest`) which I've already seen in the diff. I have the full picture.

Here is my review.

## Overall verdict

This is a clean, well-judged PR. The generalization to `ConnectionDrawer` is the right call, naming is consistent with the existing codebase, and the tests assert behavior that matters. I found no bugs and nothing that blocks landing. Below are the honest answers per your five points — mostly "acceptable now, watch later," with one cheap cleanup worth doing in this PR.

---

### 1. The async-action-with-toast duplication — real, but file as follow-up (don't extract yet)

The `setSubmitting(true)` → `try { await X; message.success } catch { message.error } finally { setSubmitting(false) }` shape now appears in four places:

- `ConnectionDrawer.tsx:68-95` (`onFinish`)
- `ReauthModal.tsx:25-40` (`onOk`)
- `Connections.tsx:171-181` (`onTest`)
- `Connections.tsx:184-198` (`onDelete`, slightly different — uses modal `onOk` + rethrow)

A `useAsyncAction` hook returning `{ run, loading }` would collapse the first three cleanly. **But I'd file this, not do it now**, for two honest reasons:

- The error-message *prefix* differs per call (`Create/Update failed`, `Re-auth failed`, `Test failed`, `Delete failed`), and the success message differs, so the helper needs both passed in — it saves the `try/finally/useState` boilerplate (~5 lines each) but not the message strings. Real but modest payoff.
- `onDelete` is the odd one out (rethrow to keep the confirm modal open), so it wouldn't share the helper cleanly — meaning you'd get 3-of-4 unification, and the page would have two patterns side by side.

Concrete cost if left: each new mutating action (suites, check editor) re-derives the `submitting` state + try/finally. That's exactly the `useAsyncData` situation the codebase already solved once for fetches. The symmetry is the argument *for* extracting — but it's a Week-5 pre-suites task, not a this-PR blocker. **Recommendation: file an issue "extract `useAsyncAction` toast helper before suites page" and land this PR as-is.** Extracting it now under-specified (before you see the suites call sites) risks the wrong shape.

### 2. `AddConnectionDrawer` → `ConnectionDrawer` (create+edit) — right altitude, not over-branched

This is the correct shape. The `isEdit` branching is shallow and localized:

- `ConnectionDrawer.tsx:42` — `const isEdit = connection !== undefined;` single derivation.
- The branches are: title, button label, the submit call (`updateConnection` vs `createConnection`), two `disabled={isEdit}` props, and `showSecret={!isEdit}`. That's it — ~6 touchpoints, all one-liners, no nested conditionals.

The form, validation, type-fields rendering, and layout are fully shared — which is the whole point and what a split would duplicate. Splitting into `CreateDrawer`/`EditDrawer` would duplicate the entire `<Form>` body (the spec-driven fields, the Drawer chrome) to avoid 6 trivial ternaries. That's a worse trade. **Keep it merged.** One thing to watch as it grows: if a 3rd mode appears (e.g. "clone"), `isEdit: boolean` becomes a `mode` enum — but that's a YAGNI concern, not now.

Minor: `ConnectionDrawer.tsx:48` `type = isEdit ? connection.type : watchedType` is a clean way to freeze the type in edit mode while keeping the watch for create. Good.

### 3. Prop-drilling `actions` through `ConnectionsBody → ConnectionTypeSection → ConnectionCard` — acceptable, smell is borderline

It's threaded through 2 intermediate components that don't use it (`ConnectionsBody:101`, `ConnectionTypeSection:138` both just forward). That's the classic prop-drilling tell. **But it's acceptable here** because:

- Depth is only 3, and these are all private components in one ~250-line file — not a cross-module context.
- A `ConnectionsContext` would be more ceremony than the problem warrants at this size.

Concrete cost: when you add a 4th action, you don't touch the intermediates (the `actions` object absorbs it) — so the drilling cost is paid once and is now flat. That's actually the *reason* bundling them into one `ConnectionActions` object (vs. 3 separate props) was the right move. **Acceptable as-is.** If a 4th level of nesting appears, reach for context then.

### 4. Dead code / redundant state / cleverness — one cheap fix

**Worth fixing in this PR:**
- `ReauthModal.tsx:30` — `const { secret } = await form.validateFields();` is **outside** the `try`. If validation rejects (empty field), the rejection is unhandled. It happens to be harmless because antd swallows the `validateFields` rejection into the form UI, but it's inconsistent with `ConnectionDrawer` (which uses `onFinish`, so antd validates first) and relies on antd's promise being safely ignorable. Low cost, but a maintainer copying this into the suites modal might not realize the ordering matters. Minor — optional.

**Not dead, but worth noting:**
- `Connections.tsx:62-66` — the `actions` object is recreated every render. Harmless (the children aren't memoized), but if anyone later wraps `ConnectionCard` in `React.memo` for the wrap-grid, this silently defeats it. Not worth a `useMemo` now; just be aware.

No actual dead code. No redundant state. The `drawer: { open, connection? }` single-state-object (`Connections.tsx:63`) is a nice consolidation vs. two `useState`s. The comment at `:62` explaining `connection === undefined while open = create` is exactly the right level of inline doc — consistent with the codebase's commenting style.

Naming is consistent: `onSaved`/`onDone`/`onChanged` follow the existing `onCreated` convention, `ConnectionActions` mirrors the spec-driven type style. Good.

### 5. Test quality — solid, asserts behavior not implementation

The tests are genuinely good and not over-mocked:

- `ConnectionDrawer.test.tsx:140-165` (edit) asserts the **real** prefill-via-effect (`waitFor(... toHaveValue('acc1'))`), that the secret field is **absent**, and that `updateConnection` (PATCH) is called — not `createConnection`. The `expect(mockCreate).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` is the assertion that actually proves the branch. This is testing behavior that matters.
- It mocks only the two network functions and keeps the real `connectionFormSpec`/labels (`importOriginal` + spread) — so the spec-driven field rendering is exercised for real. That's the right mock boundary.
- `Connections.test.tsx:101-119` drives the **full** menu→confirm-modal→delete path through the DOM, including the nice disambiguation comment about both buttons being labelled "Delete" (`within(dialog)`). Not brittle — it goes through roles/labels, not test-ids or component internals.
- `ReauthModal.test.tsx` covers both the happy path and the empty-credential guard.

One small brittleness note, not worth changing: `ReauthModal.test.tsx:58` asserts the empty-credential case via `getAllByText('New credential').length > 0` — that's asserting "the label still renders" as a proxy for "validation blocked submit," which is indirect. The load-bearing assertion is the next line (`mockReauth not called`), which is correct. The label check is weak filler but harmless.

| 1 | `useAsyncAction` toast helper (4th copy) | **File follow-up issue**, do before suites page — not in this PR |
| 2 | `ConnectionDrawer` create+edit merge | **Keep as-is** — correct altitude |

| 4 | `ReauthModal.tsx:30` validateFields outside try | Optional cheap tidy; move inside `try` or note it |
| 5 | Tests | **Good** — land as-is |

Net: clean PR, safe to land. The only thing I'd actively do is file the `useAsyncAction` issue so the pattern is extracted *before* it gets copied into the suites/check-editor pages (which the prompt flags as the real risk) rather than after the 6th copy.

## Review findings — `feat/week4-connection-edit-reauth-delete`

One real bug, confirmed empirically. The rest of the candidates are sound.

### 1. CONFIRMED — ReauthModal: `validateFields()` rejection escapes `onOk` as an unhandled promise rejection
`/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/components/connections/ReauthModal.tsx:25-39`

```js
const onOk = async () => {
  if (!connection) return;
  const { secret } = await form.validateFields();  // ← outside try/catch
  setSubmitting(true);
  try { ... } catch (err) { ... }
};
```

antd's `<Modal onOk>` wires `onOk` directly as the OK button's `onClick` (verified in `node_modules/antd/es/modal/components/NormalOkBtn.js`) and does **not** await/catch its returned promise. When the user clicks "Rotate credential" with an empty field, `form.validateFields()` rejects with an `{errorFields}` object that nothing catches → unhandled promise rejection.

I reproduced it by running the suite: the "does not call the API with an empty credential" test emits

```
⎯ Unhandled Rejection ⎯
Unknown Error: 'secret' is required
```

The tests still report green only because vitest doesn't fail on unhandled rejections by default — and vitest itself flags this as a potential source of false-positive tests. **Failure scenario:** any user who clicks Rotate before typing a credential triggers an unhandled rejection (console noise, error-tracking/Sentry noise, and a latent test reliability problem).

Fix: move `validateFields()` inside a guard, e.g.
```js
const onOk = async () => {
  if (!connection) return;
  let secret: string;
  try { ({ secret } = await form.validateFields()); } catch { return; }
  ...
};
```

Note: `ConnectionDrawer` does **not** have this bug — it submits via `form.submit()`, so `onFinish` only runs after validation passes; antd handles the validation rejection internally.

### Candidates verified clean (REFUTED / sound)

2. **Edit-mode prefill / create-after-edit stale state — sound.** `setDrawer({ open: false })` replaces the whole object, so `connection` becomes `undefined` on close; the next "Add" opens in create mode. `destroyOnHidden` is the correct antd v6 prop (deprecated alias is `destroyOnClose`, confirmed in `Drawer.d.ts`) and remounts the Form each open, so `Form.useWatch` re-attaches and fields reset cleanly. The effect re-seeds correctly when switching between two different connections (`connection` is in the dep array). Verified by the passing edit test (`Account` prefills to `acc1`).

3. **Create vs edit immutability — honored.** Edit `onFinish` forwards only `{name, config}`; `type`/`env` are never sent. `type = isEdit ? connection.type : watchedType` renders the right fields in edit regardless of the disabled Select. `auth_type`/`extraField` (e.g. Airflow basic→username) prefill correctly from `config`.

4. **Delete `modal.confirm` — correct pattern.** `onOk` rethrows after the error toast, which is the documented antd way to keep the dialog open; `actions.onChanged()` (reload) runs only after `await deleteConnection` resolves.

5. **`actions` object rebuilt each render — not a correctness bug.** Closures capture only stable state setters and the `useCallback`-stable `reload`; no stale data is closed over. Pure identity churn with no memoized consumers downstream.

6. **`api/connections.ts` verbs/paths/payloads — correct.** `PATCH /connections/:id` (`{name?, config?, secret?}`), `DELETE /connections/:id` (void/204), `POST /connections/:id/reauth {secret}`. All consistent with the create/test endpoints and the documented REST surface.

Relevant file for the fix: `/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/components/connections/ReauthModal.tsx`.

Here is my review.

## Overall verdict

This is a clean, well-judged PR. The generalization to `ConnectionDrawer` is the right call, naming is consistent with the existing codebase, and the tests assert behavior that matters. I found no bugs and nothing that blocks landing. Below are the honest answers per your five points — mostly "acceptable now, watch later," with one cheap cleanup worth doing in this PR.

---

### 1. The async-action-with-toast duplication — real, but file as follow-up (don't extract yet)

The `setSubmitting(true)` → `try { await X; message.success } catch { message.error } finally { setSubmitting(false) }` shape now appears in four places:

- `ConnectionDrawer.tsx:68-95` (`onFinish`)
- `ReauthModal.tsx:25-40` (`onOk`)
- `Connections.tsx:171-181` (`onTest`)
- `Connections.tsx:184-198` (`onDelete`, slightly different — uses modal `onOk` + rethrow)

A `useAsyncAction` hook returning `{ run, loading }` would collapse the first three cleanly. **But I'd file this, not do it now**, for two honest reasons:

- The error-message *prefix* differs per call (`Create/Update failed`, `Re-auth failed`, `Test failed`, `Delete failed`), and the success message differs, so the helper needs both passed in — it saves the `try/finally/useState` boilerplate (~5 lines each) but not the message strings. Real but modest payoff.
- `onDelete` is the odd one out (rethrow to keep the confirm modal open), so it wouldn't share the helper cleanly — meaning you'd get 3-of-4 unification, and the page would have two patterns side by side.

Concrete cost if left: each new mutating action (suites, check editor) re-derives the `submitting` state + try/finally. That's exactly the `useAsyncData` situation the codebase already solved once for fetches. The symmetry is the argument *for* extracting — but it's a Week-5 pre-suites task, not a this-PR blocker. **Recommendation: file an issue "extract `useAsyncAction` toast helper before suites page" and land this PR as-is.** Extracting it now under-specified (before you see the suites call sites) risks the wrong shape.

### 2. `AddConnectionDrawer` → `ConnectionDrawer` (create+edit) — right altitude, not over-branched

This is the correct shape. The `isEdit` branching is shallow and localized:

- `ConnectionDrawer.tsx:42` — `const isEdit = connection !== undefined;` single derivation.
- The branches are: title, button label, the submit call (`updateConnection` vs `createConnection`), two `disabled={isEdit}` props, and `showSecret={!isEdit}`. That's it — ~6 touchpoints, all one-liners, no nested conditionals.

The form, validation, type-fields rendering, and layout are fully shared — which is the whole point and what a split would duplicate. Splitting into `CreateDrawer`/`EditDrawer` would duplicate the entire `<Form>` body (the spec-driven fields, the Drawer chrome) to avoid 6 trivial ternaries. That's a worse trade. **Keep it merged.** One thing to watch as it grows: if a 3rd mode appears (e.g. "clone"), `isEdit: boolean` becomes a `mode` enum — but that's a YAGNI concern, not now.

Minor: `ConnectionDrawer.tsx:48` `type = isEdit ? connection.type : watchedType` is a clean way to freeze the type in edit mode while keeping the watch for create. Good.

### 3. Prop-drilling `actions` through `ConnectionsBody → ConnectionTypeSection → ConnectionCard` — acceptable, smell is borderline

It's threaded through 2 intermediate components that don't use it (`ConnectionsBody:101`, `ConnectionTypeSection:138` both just forward). That's the classic prop-drilling tell. **But it's acceptable here** because:

- Depth is only 3, and these are all private components in one ~250-line file — not a cross-module context.
- A `ConnectionsContext` would be more ceremony than the problem warrants at this size.

Concrete cost: when you add a 4th action, you don't touch the intermediates (the `actions` object absorbs it) — so the drilling cost is paid once and is now flat. That's actually the *reason* bundling them into one `ConnectionActions` object (vs. 3 separate props) was the right move. **Acceptable as-is.** If a 4th level of nesting appears, reach for context then.

### 4. Dead code / redundant state / cleverness — one cheap fix

**Worth fixing in this PR:**
- `ReauthModal.tsx:30` — `const { secret } = await form.validateFields();` is **outside** the `try`. If validation rejects (empty field), the rejection is unhandled. It happens to be harmless because antd swallows the `validateFields` rejection into the form UI, but it's inconsistent with `ConnectionDrawer` (which uses `onFinish`, so antd validates first) and relies on antd's promise being safely ignorable. Low cost, but a maintainer copying this into the suites modal might not realize the ordering matters. Minor — optional.

**Not dead, but worth noting:**
- `Connections.tsx:62-66` — the `actions` object is recreated every render. Harmless (the children aren't memoized), but if anyone later wraps `ConnectionCard` in `React.memo` for the wrap-grid, this silently defeats it. Not worth a `useMemo` now; just be aware.

No actual dead code. No redundant state. The `drawer: { open, connection? }` single-state-object (`Connections.tsx:63`) is a nice consolidation vs. two `useState`s. The comment at `:62` explaining `connection === undefined while open = create` is exactly the right level of inline doc — consistent with the codebase's commenting style.

Naming is consistent: `onSaved`/`onDone`/`onChanged` follow the existing `onCreated` convention, `ConnectionActions` mirrors the spec-driven type style. Good.

### 5. Test quality — solid, asserts behavior not implementation

The tests are genuinely good and not over-mocked:

- `ConnectionDrawer.test.tsx:140-165` (edit) asserts the **real** prefill-via-effect (`waitFor(... toHaveValue('acc1'))`), that the secret field is **absent**, and that `updateConnection` (PATCH) is called — not `createConnection`. The `expect(mockCreate).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` is the assertion that actually proves the branch. This is testing behavior that matters.
- It mocks only the two network functions and keeps the real `connectionFormSpec`/labels (`importOriginal` + spread) — so the spec-driven field rendering is exercised for real. That's the right mock boundary.
- `Connections.test.tsx:101-119` drives the **full** menu→confirm-modal→delete path through the DOM, including the nice disambiguation comment about both buttons being labelled "Delete" (`within(dialog)`). Not brittle — it goes through roles/labels, not test-ids or component internals.
- `ReauthModal.test.tsx` covers both the happy path and the empty-credential guard.

One small brittleness note, not worth changing: `ReauthModal.test.tsx:58` asserts the empty-credential case via `getAllByText('New credential').length > 0` — that's asserting "the label still renders" as a proxy for "validation blocked submit," which is indirect. The load-bearing assertion is the next line (`mockReauth not called`), which is correct. The label check is weak filler but harmless.

---

### Summary of recommended actions

| # | Item | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `useAsyncAction` toast helper (4th copy) | **File follow-up issue**, do before suites page — not in this PR |
| 2 | `ConnectionDrawer` create+edit merge | **Keep as-is** — correct altitude |
| 3 | `actions` prop-drilling (depth 3) | **Acceptable** — revisit only if a 4th level appears |
| 4 | `ReauthModal.tsx:30` validateFields outside try | Optional cheap tidy; move inside `try` or note it |
| 5 | Tests | **Good** — land as-is |

Net: clean PR, safe to land. The only thing I'd actively do is file the `useAsyncAction` issue so the pattern is extracted *before* it gets copied into the suites/check-editor pages (which the prompt flags as the real risk) rather than after the 6th copy.

1	import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from 'react';
2	
3	/** Three-state result of an async fetch. */
4	export type AsyncState<T> =
5	  | { status: 'loading' }
6	  | { status: 'ok'; data: T }
7	  | { status: 'error'; error: string };
8	
9	/**
10	 * Fetch on mount (and on `reload()`), with a cancelled-guard so a late
11	 * resolution after unmount doesn't set state, and rejection normalised to a
12	 * string `error`. Shared by the data pages (Home, Connections, …) so the
13	 * cancelled-effect dance lives in one place rather than being re-derived per page.
14	 *
15	 * `reload` re-runs the fetcher (e.g. after a mutation) while keeping the current
16	 * data visible until the refetch resolves — no flash back to the loading state.
17	 */
18	export function useAsyncData<T>(fetcher: () => Promise<T>): {
19	  state: AsyncState<T>;
20	  reload: () => void;
21	} {
22	  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<T>>({ status: 'loading' });
23	  const [nonce, setNonce] = useState(0);
24	
25	  useEffect(() => {
26	    let cancelled = false;
27	    fetcher()
28	      .then((data) => {
29	        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', data });
30	      })
31	      .catch((err: unknown) => {
32	        if (!cancelled) {
33	          setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
34	        }
35	      });
36	    return () => {
37	      cancelled = true;
38	    };
39	    // Re-run on mount and whenever `reload` bumps the nonce; the fetcher identity
40	    // is intentionally not a dependency.
41	    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
42	  }, [nonce]);
43	
44	  const reload = useCallback(() => setNonce((n) => n + 1), []);
45	  return { state, reload };
46	}
47

104	function ConnectionsBody({
105	  state,
106	  actions,
107	}: {
108	  state: AsyncState<Connection[]>;
109	  actions: ConnectionActions;
110	}) {
111	  if (state.status === 'loading') {
112	    return <Spin tip="Loading connections…" size="large" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;
113	  }
114	  if (state.status === 'error') {
115	    return (
116	      <Alert
117	        type="error"
118	        showIcon
119	        title="Failed to load connections"
120	        description={state.error}
121	        style={{ margin: 24 }}
122	      />
123	    );
124	  }
125	  const connections = state.data;
126	  if (connections.length === 0) {
127	    return <Empty description="No connections configured yet" />;
128	  }
129	  return (
130	    <>
131	      {groupByType(connections).map(([type, group]) => (
132	        <ConnectionTypeSection key={type} type={type} connections={group} actions={actions} />
133	      ))}
134	    </>
135	  );
136	}

138	function ConnectionTypeSection({
139	  type,
140	  connections,
141	  actions,
142	}: {
143	  type: ConnectionType;
144	  connections: Connection[];
145	  actions: ConnectionActions;
146	}) {
147	  return (
148	    <Flex vertical gap={12}>
149	      <Typography.Title level={5} style={{ margin: 0 }}>
150	        {CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[type]}
151	      </Typography.Title>
152	      <Flex wrap gap={12}>
153	        {connections.map((connection) => (
154	          <ConnectionCard key={connection.id} connection={connection} actions={actions} />
155	        ))}

161	function ConnectionCard({
162	  connection,
163	  actions,
164	}: {
165	  connection: Connection;
166	  actions: ConnectionActions;
167	}) {
168	  const { message, modal } = App.useApp();
169	  const [testing, setTesting] = useState(false);
170	
171	  const onTest = async () => {
172	    setTesting(true);
173	    try {
174	      const { ok } = await testConnection(connection.id);
175	      if (ok) message.success(`${connection.name}: connection OK`);
176	      else message.error(`${connection.name}: connection test failed`);
177	    } catch (err) {
178	      message.error(`${connection.name}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'test failed'}`);
179	    } finally {
180	      setTesting(false);
181	    }
182	  };
183	
184	  const onDelete = () => {
185	    modal.confirm({
186	      title: `Delete “${connection.name}”?`,
187	      content: 'This removes the connection and its stored credential.',
188	      okText: 'Delete',
189	      okType: 'danger',
190	      onOk: async () => {
191	        try {
192	          await deleteConnection(connection.id);
193	          message.success(`${connection.name} deleted`);
194	          actions.onChanged();
195	        } catch (err) {
196	          message.error(`Delete failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
197	          throw err; // keep the confirm modal open on failure
198	        }
199	      },
200	    });
201	  };
202	
203	  const menuItems = [
204	    { key: 'edit', label: 'Edit', onClick: () => actions.onEdit(connection) },
205	    { key: 'reauth', label: 'Re-authenticate', onClick: () => actions.onReauth(connection) },
206	    { type: 'divider' as const },
207	    { key: 'delete', label: 'Delete', danger: true, onClick: onDelete },
208	  ];
209	
210	  return (
211	    <Card size="small" style={{ minWidth: 280 }}>
212	      <Flex justify="space-between" align="center" gap={12}>
213	        <Flex vertical gap={6}>
214	          <Typography.Text strong>{connection.name}</Typography.Text>
215	          <Flex gap={8} align="center">
216	            <Tag color={ENV_COLORS[connection.env]}>{envLabel(connection.env)}</Tag>
217	            {connection.has_secret ? (

219	            ) : (

221	            )}
222	          </Flex>
223	        </Flex>
224	        <Flex gap={8} align="center">
225	          <Button size="small" loading={testing} onClick={onTest}>

227	          </Button>
228	          <Dropdown menu={{ items: menuItems }} trigger={['click']}>

232	              aria-label={`${connection.name} actions`}
233	            />
234	          </Dropdown>
235	        </Flex>

238	  );

import { Button, Flex, Layout, Menu, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';
import { Link, Navigate, Route, Routes, useLocation } from 'react-router-dom';

import { AuthGate } from './auth/AuthGate';
import { authMode } from './auth/config';
import { useCurrentUser } from './auth/useCurrentUser';
import { getMsalInstance } from './auth/msalInstance';
import { Connections } from './pages/Connections';
import { Home } from './pages/Home';

const { Header, Sider, Content } = Layout;

const NAV_ITEMS = [
  { key: '/connections', label: <Link to="/connections">Connections</Link> },
  { key: '/profile', label: <Link to="/profile">Profile</Link> },
];

export function App() {
  const location = useLocation();
  // Highlight the nav item whose path prefixes the current location.
  const selectedKeys = NAV_ITEMS.map((i) => i.key).filter((k) => location.pathname.startsWith(k));

  return (
    <Layout style={{ minHeight: '100vh' }}>
      <Header style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 16 }}>
        <Typography.Title level={4} style={{ color: '#fff', margin: 0, flex: 1 }}>
          DataQ
        </Typography.Title>
        <UserChip />
      </Header>
      <Layout>
        <Sider width={200} theme="light" breakpoint="lg" collapsedWidth={0}>
          <Menu
            mode="inline"
            selectedKeys={selectedKeys}
            items={NAV_ITEMS}
            style={{ height: '100%', borderInlineEnd: 0 }}
          />
        </Sider>
        <Content style={{ padding: 24 }}>
          <AuthGate>
            <Routes>
              <Route path="/" element={<Navigate to="/connections" replace />} />
              <Route path="/connections" element={<Connections />} />
              <Route path="/profile" element={<Home />} />
              <Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/connections" replace />} />
            </Routes>
          </AuthGate>
        </Content>
      </Layout>
    </Layout>
  );
}

function UserChip() {
  const user = useCurrentUser();
  if (!user) return null;

  const onLogout = () => {
    if (authMode !== 'real') return;
    const instance = getMsalInstance();
    void instance?.logoutRedirect({ account: instance.getAllAccounts()[0] });
  };

  return (
    <Flex align="center" gap={12}>
      {user.isDev && <Tag color="orange">DEV BYPASS</Tag>}
      <Typography.Text style={{ color: '#fff' }}>{user.name}</Typography.Text>
      {!user.isDev && (
        <Button size="small" onClick={onLogout}>
          Sign out
        </Button>
      )}
    </Flex>
  );
}

import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { App as AntApp, ConfigProvider } from 'antd';
import { BrowserRouter } from 'react-router-dom';

import { App } from './App';
import { CurrentUserProvider } from './auth/CurrentUserProvider';
import { MsalProvider } from './auth/MsalProvider';
import { getMsalInstance } from './auth/msalInstance';
import './styles.css';

const maybeRoot = document.getElementById('root');
if (!maybeRoot) {
  throw new Error('Root element #root not found in index.html');
}
const rootEl: HTMLElement = maybeRoot;

// MSAL lifecycle (issue #62):
//   1. .initialize() must complete before any MSAL API call (v5 requirement).
//   2. .handleRedirectPromise() must resolve before React renders so the
//      first paint reflects post-login state.
//   3. Errors surface to the console + a static page — fail loud during dev.
async function bootstrap() {
  const instance = getMsalInstance();
  if (instance) {
    await instance.initialize();
    await instance.handleRedirectPromise();
  }
  createRoot(rootEl).render(
    <StrictMode>
      <ConfigProvider>
        <AntApp>
          <MsalProvider>
            <CurrentUserProvider>
              <BrowserRouter>
                <App />
              </BrowserRouter>
            </CurrentUserProvider>
          </MsalProvider>
        </AntApp>
      </ConfigProvider>
    </StrictMode>,
  );
}

bootstrap().catch((err) => {
  console.error('MSAL bootstrap failed', err);
  rootEl.innerHTML =
    '<pre style="padding:24px;color:#a00">Authentication bootstrap failed. See console.</pre>';
});

"""Suite CRUD endpoints.

Thin HTTP layer over `suite_service`: validates request shapes, wires the
current user + db session, and maps models onto responses. All business logic
(connection validation, persistence) lives in the service. `connection_id` is
set at create and immutable thereafter (re-pointing would orphan child checks).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Annotated, Any, Literal

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from backend.app.core.auth import get_current_user
from backend.app.core.secrets import SecretStore, get_secret_store
from backend.app.db.models import Connection, User
from backend.app.db.session import get_db
from backend.app.services import profile_service as profile
from backend.app.services import suite_io_service as suite_io
from backend.app.services import suite_service as svc
from backend.app.services.suite_authz import require_permission

router = APIRouter(tags=["suites"])


class SuiteCreate(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=1024)
    connection_id: uuid.UUID


class SuiteUpdate(BaseModel):
    name: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=128)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=1024)


class SuiteRead(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    id: uuid.UUID
    name: str
    description: str | None
    connection_id: uuid.UUID
    created_by: uuid.UUID


@router.post(
    "/suites",
    response_model=SuiteRead,
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    summary="Create a suite",
)
def create_suite(
    payload: SuiteCreate,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> SuiteRead:
    suite = svc.create_suite(
        db,
        name=payload.name,
        description=payload.description,
        connection_id=payload.connection_id,
        created_by=current_user.id,
    )
    return SuiteRead.model_validate(suite)


@router.get("/suites", response_model=list[SuiteRead], summary="List suites")
def list_suites(
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
    connection_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
) -> list[SuiteRead]:
    # Scoped to suites the user owns or has a share on.
    suites = svc.list_suites(db, user_id=current_user.id, connection_id=connection_id)
    return [SuiteRead.model_validate(s) for s in suites]


@router.get("/suites/{suite_id}", response_model=SuiteRead, summary="Get a suite")
def get_suite(
    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> SuiteRead:
    suite = require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="view")
    return SuiteRead.model_validate(suite)


@router.patch("/suites/{suite_id}", response_model=SuiteRead, summary="Update a suite")
def update_suite(
    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
    payload: SuiteUpdate,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> SuiteRead:
    require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="edit")
    suite = svc.update_suite(db, suite_id, name=payload.name, description=payload.description)
    return SuiteRead.model_validate(suite)


@router.delete(
    "/suites/{suite_id}",
    status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT,
    summary="Delete a suite",
)
def delete_suite(
    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> None:
    require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="admin")
    svc.delete_suite(db, suite_id)


# ───────────────────────── export / import (portable documents) ─────

class CheckCreate(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=256)
    # v1 authors only 'expectation' (service enforces; reserved kinds 422).
    kind: str = "expectation"
    expectation_type: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128)
    config: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    warn_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    fail_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    critical_threshold: Decimal | None = None


class CheckUpdate(BaseModel):
    name: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=256)
    expectation_type: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=128)
    config: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    warn_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    fail_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    critical_threshold: Decimal | None = None

    id: uuid.UUID
    suite_id: uuid.UUID
    name: str
    kind: str
    expectation_type: str
    config: dict[str, Any]
    warn_threshold: float | None
    fail_threshold: float | None
    critical_threshold: float | None


@router.post(
    "/suites/{suite_id}/checks",
    response_model=CheckRead,
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,

)
def create_check(

    payload: CheckCreate,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],

) -> CheckRead:
    require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="edit")
    check = svc.create_check(
        db,
        suite_id=suite_id,
        name=payload.name,
        kind=payload.kind,
        expectation_type=payload.expectation_type,
        config=payload.config,
        warn_threshold=payload.warn_threshold,
        fail_threshold=payload.fail_threshold,
        critical_threshold=payload.critical_threshold,
    )
    return CheckRead.model_validate(check)

    "/suites/{suite_id}/checks",

) -> list[CheckRead]:

  "content": "import { App, Button, Drawer, Flex, Form, Input, Select } from 'antd';\nimport { useEffect } from 'react';\n\nimport {\n  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,\n  type Connection,\n  envLabel,\n} from '../../api/connections';\nimport { createSuite, type Suite, updateSuite } from '../../api/suites';\n\ninterface SuiteFormValues {\n  name: string;\n  description?: string;\n  connection_id: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Create or edit a suite. `suite === undefined` is create mode (connection is\n * chosen and then locked); editing exposes only name/description since\n * `connection_id` is immutable on the backend (re-pointing orphans child checks).\n */\nexport function SuiteDrawer({\n  open,\n  suite,\n  connections,\n  onClose,\n  onSaved,\n}: {\n  open: boolean;\n  suite?: Suite;\n  /** Available connections for the create-mode picker. */\n  connections: Connection[];\n  onClose: () => void;\n  onSaved: () => void;\n}) {\n  const { message } = App.useApp();\n  const [form] = Form.useForm<SuiteFormValues>();\n  const isEdit = suite !== undefined;\n\n  // Prefill on open/edit; reset to a blank form for create.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!open) return;\n    if (suite) {\n      form.setFieldsValue({\n        name: suite.name,\n        description: suite.description ?? undefined,\n        connection_id: suite.connection_id,\n      });\n    } else {\n      form.resetFields();\n    }\n  }, [open, suite, form]);\n\n  const onSubmit = async () => {\n    let values: SuiteFormValues;\n    try {\n      values = await form.validateFields();\n    } catch {\n      return; // validation errors render inline\n    }\n    try {\n      if (isEdit) {\n        await updateSuite(suite.id, {\n          name: values.name,\n          description: values.description ?? null,\n        });\n        message.success(`${values.name}: saved`);\n      } else {\n        await createSuite({\n          name: values.name,\n          description: values.description ?? null,\n          connection_id: values.connection_id,\n        });\n        message.success(`${values.name}: created`);\n      }\n      onSaved();\n    } catch (err) {\n      message.error(`Save failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Drawer\n      title={isEdit ? `Edit “${suite.name}”` : 'New suite'}\n      open={open}\n      onClose={onClose}\n      width={480}\n      destroyOnHidden\n      extra={\n        <Flex gap={8}>\n          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>\n          <Button type=\"primary\" onClick={onSubmit}>\n            {isEdit ? 'Save' : 'Create'}\n          </Button>\n        </Flex>\n      }\n    >\n      <Form form={form} layout=\"vertical\">\n        <Form.Item name=\"name\" label=\"Name\" rules={[{ required: true }]}>\n          <Input />\n        </Form.Item>\n        <Form.Item name=\"description\" label=\"Description (optional)\">\n          <Input.TextArea rows={3} />\n        </Form.Item>\n        <Form.Item\n          name=\"connection_id\"\n          label=\"Connection\"\n          rules={[{ required: true }]}\n          extra={isEdit ? 'The connection is fixed once a suite is created.' : undefined}\n        >\n          <Select\n            disabled={isEdit}\n            placeholder=\"Select a connection\"\n            options={connections.map((c) => ({\n              value: c.id,\n              label: `${c.name} · ${CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[c.type]} · ${envLabel(c.env)}`,\n            }))}\n          />\n        </Form.Item>\n      </Form>\n    </Drawer>\n  );\n}\n"
}

connState.data : [];\n\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical gap={24}>\n      <Flex justify=\"space-between\" align=\"center\" gap={12}>\n        <Typography.Title level={3} style={{ margin: 0 }}>\n          Suites\n        </Typography.Title>\n        <Button\n          type=\"primary\"\n          disabled={connections.length === 0}\n          onClick={() => setDrawer({ open: true })}\n        >\n          New suite\n        </Button>\n      </Flex>\n      <SuitesBody\n        state={state}\n        connections={connections}\n        selectedId={selectedId}\n        onSelect={setSelectedId}\n        onEdit={(suite) => setDrawer({ open: true, suite })}\n        onDeleted={() => {\n          setSelectedId(null);\n          reload();\n        }}\n      />\n      <SuiteDrawer\n        open={drawer.open}\n        suite={drawer.suite}\n        connections={connections}\n        onClose={() => setDrawer({ open: false })}\n        onSaved={() => {\n          setDrawer({ open: false });\n          reload();\n        }}\n      />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction SuitesBody({\n  state,\n  connections,\n  selectedId,\n  onSelect,\n  onEdit,\n  onDeleted,\n}: {\n  state: AsyncState<Suite[]>;\n  connections: Connection[];\n  selectedId: string | null;\n  onSelect: (id: string) => void;\n  onEdit: (suite: Suite) => void;\n  onDeleted: () => void;\n}) {\n  if (state.status === 'loading') {\n    return <Spin tip=\"Loading suites…\" size=\"large\" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;\n  }\n  if (state.status === 'error') {\n    return (\n      <Alert\n        type=\"error\"\n        showIcon\n        title=\"Failed to load suites\"\n        description={state.error}\n        style={{ margin: 24 }}\n      />\n    );\n  }\n  const suites = state.data;\n  if (suites.length === 0) {\n    return <Empty description=\"No suites yet — create one to start authoring checks.\" />;\n  }\n  const selected = suites.find((s) => s.id === selectedId) ?? null;\n\n  return (\n    <Flex gap={24} align=\"flex-start\">\n      <Card size=\"small\" style={{ width: 300, flexShrink: 0 }} styles={{ body: { padding: 0 } }}>\n        <List\n          dataSource={suites}\n          renderItem={(suite) => (\n            <List.Item\n              onClick={() => onSelect(suite.id)}\n              style={{\n                cursor: 'pointer',\n                padding: '12px 16px',\n                background: suite.id === selectedId ? 'rgba(22,119,255,0.08)' : undefined,\n              }}\n            >\n              <Typography.Text strong={suite.id === selectedId}>{suite.name}</Typography.Text>\n            </List.Item>\n          )}\n        />\n      </Card>\n      <div style={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 0 }}>\n        {selected ? (\n          <SuiteDetail\n            key={selected.id}\n            suite={selected}\n            connections={connections}\n            onEdit={() => onEdit(selected)}\n            onDeleted={onDeleted}\n          />\n        ) : (\n          <Empty description=\"Select a suite to view its checks.\" style={{ marginTop: 64 }} />\n        )}\n      </div>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction SuiteDetail({\n  suite,\n  connections,\n  onEdit,\n  onDeleted,\n}: {\n  suite: Suite;\n  connections: Connection[];\n  onEdit: () => void;\n  onDeleted: () => void;\n}) {\n  const { message, modal } = App.useApp();\n  // Remounted (keyed by suite.id) when the selection changes → checks refetch.\n  const { state } = useAsyncData(() => listChecks(suite.id));\n  const connection = connections.find((c) => c.id === suite.connection_id);\n\n  const onDelete = () => {\n    modal.confirm({\n      title: `Delete “${suite.name}”?`,\n      content: 'This removes the suite and all of its checks.',\n      okText: 'Delete',\n      okType: 'danger',\n      onOk: async () => {\n        try {\n          await deleteSuite(suite.id);\n          message.success(`${suite.name} deleted`);\n          onDeleted();\n        } catch (err) {\n          message.error(`Delete failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);\n          throw err; // keep the confirm modal open on failure\n        }\n      },\n    });\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical gap={16}>\n      <Flex justify=\"space-between\" align=\"flex-start\" gap={12}>\n        <Flex vertical gap={6}>\n          <Typography.Title level={4} style={{ margin: 0 }}>\n            {suite.name}\n          </Typography.Title>\n          {connection ? (\n            <Flex gap={8} align=\"center\">\n              <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\">\n                {connection.name} · {CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[connection.type]}\n              </Typography.Text>\n              <Tag color={ENV_COLORS[connection.env]}>{envLabel(connection.env)}</Tag>\n            </Flex>\n          ) : (\n            <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\">Connection {suite.connection_id}</Typography.Text>\n          )}\n        </Flex>\n        <Flex gap={8}>\n          <Button onClick={onEdit}>Edit</Button>\n          <Button danger onClick={onDelete}>\n            Delete\n          </Button>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n      {suite.description && <Typography.Paragraph>{suite.description}</Typography.Paragraph>}\n      <ChecksList state={state} />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction ChecksList({ state }: { state: AsyncState<Check[]> }) {\n  if (state.status === 'loading') {\n    return <Spin tip=\"Loading checks…\" />;\n  }\n  if (state.status === 'error') {\n    return <Alert type=\"error\" showIcon title=\"Failed to load checks\" description={state.error} />;\n  }\n  const checks = state.data;\n  return (\n    <Card size=\"small\" title={`Checks (${checks.length})`}>\n      {checks.length === 0 ? (\n        <Empty\n          image={Empty.PRESENTED_IMAGE_SIMPLE}\n          description=\"No checks yet — the check editor lands in the next slice.\"\n        />\n      ) : (\n        <List\n          dataSource={checks}\n          renderItem={(check) => (\n            <List.Item>\n              <Flex vertical gap={2}>\n                <Typography.Text strong>{check.name}</Typography.Text>\n                <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\" style={{ fontSize: 12 }}>\n                  {check.expectation_type}\n                </Typography.Text>\n              </Flex>\n            </List.Item>\n          )}\n        />\n      )}\n    </Card>\n  );\n}\n"
}

--- /dev/null
+++ b/frontend/src/api/suites.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
+import { api } from './client';
+
+/**
+ * Suites API — a suite is a named bundle of DQ checks bound to one connection.
+ * `connection_id` is set at create and immutable thereafter (re-pointing would
+ * orphan the child checks), mirroring the backend `suite_service` contract.
+ */
+
+/** Mirrors the backend `SuiteRead` schema. */
+export interface Suite {
+  id: string;
+  name: string;
+  description: string | null;
+  connection_id: string;
+  created_by: string;
+}
+
+/** Mirrors `SuiteCreate` — connection_id is required and immutable. */
+export interface SuiteCreate {
+  name: string;
+  description?: string | null;
+  connection_id: string;
+}
+
+/** Mirrors `SuiteUpdate` — only name/description are mutable. */
+export interface SuiteUpdate {
+  name?: string;
+  description?: string | null;
+}
+
+export async function listSuites(params?: { connection_id?: string }): Promise<Suite[]> {
+  const { data } = await api.get<Suite[]>('/suites', { params });
+  return data;
+}
+
+export async function getSuite(id: string): Promise<Suite> {
+  const { data } = await api.get<Suite>(`/suites/${id}`);
+  return data;
+}
+
+export async function createSuite(payload: SuiteCreate): Promise<Suite> {
+  const { data } = await api.post<Suite>('/suites', payload);
+  return data;
+}
+
+export async function updateSuite(id: string, payload: SuiteUpdate): Promise<Suite> {
+  const { data } = await api.patch<Suite>(`/suites/${id}`, payload);
+  return data;
+}
+
+export async function deleteSuite(id: string): Promise<void> {
+  await api.delete(`/suites/${id}`);
+}
+
+/** Mirrors the backend `CheckRead` schema (read-only here — editor is a later slice). */
+export interface Check {
+  id: string;
+  suite_id: string;
+  name: string;
+  kind: string;
+  expectation_type: string;
+  config: Record<string, unknown>;
+  warn_threshold: number | null;
+  fail_threshold: number | null;
+  critical_threshold: number | null;
+}
+
+export async function listChecks(suiteId: string): Promise<Check[]> {
+  const { data } = await api.get<Check[]>(`/suites/${suiteId}/checks`);
+  return data;
+}
diff --git a/frontend/src/components/suites/SuiteDrawer.tsx b/frontend/src/components/suites/SuiteDrawer.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..de5317c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/frontend/src/components/suites/SuiteDrawer.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,119 @@
+import { App, Button, Drawer, Flex, Form, Input, Select } from 'antd';
+import { useEffect } from 'react';
+
+import { CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS, type Connection, envLabel } from '../../api/connections';
+import { createSuite, type Suite, updateSuite } from '../../api/suites';
+
+interface SuiteFormValues {
+  name: string;
+  description?: string;
+  connection_id: string;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Create or edit a suite. `suite === undefined` is create mode (connection is
+ * chosen and then locked); editing exposes only name/description since
+ * `connection_id` is immutable on the backend (re-pointing orphans child checks).
+ */
+export function SuiteDrawer({
+  open,
+  suite,
+  connections,
+  onClose,
+  onSaved,
+}: {
+  open: boolean;
+  suite?: Suite;
+  /** Available connections for the create-mode picker. */
+  connections: Connection[];
+  onClose: () => void;
+  onSaved: () => void;
+}) {
+  const { message } = App.useApp();
+  const [form] = Form.useForm<SuiteFormValues>();
+  const isEdit = suite !== undefined;
+
+  // Prefill on open/edit; reset to a blank form for create.
+  useEffect(() => {
+    if (!open) return;
+    if (suite) {
+      form.setFieldsValue({
+        name: suite.name,
+        description: suite.description ?? undefined,
+        connection_id: suite.connection_id,
+      });
+    } else {
+      form.resetFields();
+    }
+  }, [open, suite, form]);
+
+  const onSubmit = async () => {
+    let values: SuiteFormValues;
+    try {
+      values = await form.validateFields();
+    } catch {
+      return; // validation errors render inline
+    }
+    try {
+      if (isEdit) {
+        await updateSuite(suite.id, {
+          name: values.name,
+          description: values.description ?? null,
+        });
+        message.success(`${values.name}: saved`);
+      } else {
+        await createSuite({
+          name: values.name,
+          description: values.description ?? null,
+          connection_id: values.connection_id,
+        });
+        message.success(`${values.name}: created`);
+      }
+      onSaved();
+    } catch (err) {
+      message.error(`Save failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
+    }
+  };
+
+  return (
+    <Drawer
+      title={isEdit ? `Edit “${suite.name}”` : 'New suite'}
+      open={open}
+      onClose={onClose}
+      width={480}
+      destroyOnHidden
+      extra={
+        <Flex gap={8}>
+          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>
+          <Button type="primary" onClick={onSubmit}>
+            {isEdit ? 'Save' : 'Create'}
+          </Button>
+        </Flex>
+      }
+    >
+      <Form form={form} layout="vertical">
+        <Form.Item name="name" label="Name" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
+          <Input />
+        </Form.Item>
+        <Form.Item name="description" label="Description (optional)">
+          <Input.TextArea rows={3} />
+        </Form.Item>
+        <Form.Item
+          name="connection_id"
+          label="Connection"
+          rules={[{ required: true }]}
+          extra={isEdit ? 'The connection is fixed once a suite is created.' : undefined}
+        >
+          <Select
+            disabled={isEdit}
+            placeholder="Select a connection"
+            options={connections.map((c) => ({
+              value: c.id,
+              label: `${c.name} · ${CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[c.type]} · ${envLabel(c.env)}`,
+            }))}
+          />
+        </Form.Item>
+      </Form>
+    </Drawer>
+  );
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,239 @@
+import { App, Alert, Button, Card, Empty, Flex, List, Spin, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';
+import { useState } from 'react';
+
+import {
+  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,
+  type Connection,
+  type ConnectionEnv,
+  envLabel,
+  listConnections,
+} from '../api/connections';
+import { type Check, deleteSuite, listChecks, listSuites, type Suite } from '../api/suites';
+import { SuiteDrawer } from '../components/suites/SuiteDrawer';
+import { type AsyncState, useAsyncData } from '../hooks/useAsyncData';
+
+const ENV_COLORS: Record<ConnectionEnv, string> = {
+  dev: 'blue',
+  qa: 'gold',
+  uat: 'purple',
+  prod: 'red',
+};
+
+export function Suites() {
+  const { state, reload } = useAsyncData(listSuites);
+  const { state: connState } = useAsyncData(listConnections);
+  const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<string | null>(null);
+  // `drawer.suite === undefined` while open = create mode; a suite = edit.
+  const [drawer, setDrawer] = useState<{ open: boolean; suite?: Suite }>({ open: false });
+
+  const connections = connState.status === 'ok' ? connState.data : [];
+
+  return (
+    <Flex vertical gap={24}>
+      <Flex justify="space-between" align="center" gap={12}>
+        <Typography.Title level={3} style={{ margin: 0 }}>
+          Suites
+        </Typography.Title>
+        <Button
+          type="primary"
+          disabled={connections.length === 0}
+          onClick={() => setDrawer({ open: true })}
+        >
+          New suite
+        </Button>
+      </Flex>
+      <SuitesBody
+        state={state}
+        connections={connections}
+        selectedId={selectedId}
+        onSelect={setSelectedId}
+        onEdit={(suite) => setDrawer({ open: true, suite })}
+        onDeleted={() => {
+          setSelectedId(null);
+          reload();
+        }}
+      />
+      <SuiteDrawer
+        open={drawer.open}
+        suite={drawer.suite}
+        connections={connections}
+        onClose={() => setDrawer({ open: false })}
+        onSaved={() => {
+          setDrawer({ open: false });
+          reload();
+        }}
+      />
+    </Flex>
+  );
+}
+
+function SuitesBody({
+  state,
+  connections,
+  selectedId,
+  onSelect,
+  onEdit,
+  onDeleted,
+}: {
+  state: AsyncState<Suite[]>;
+  connections: Connection[];
+  selectedId: string | null;
+  onSelect: (id: string) => void;
+  onEdit: (suite: Suite) => void;
+  onDeleted: () => void;
+}) {
+  if (state.status === 'loading') {
+    return <Spin tip="Loading suites…" size="large" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;
+  }
+  if (state.status === 'error') {
+    return (
+      <Alert
+        type="error"
+        showIcon
+        title="Failed to load suites"
+        description={state.error}
+        style={{ margin: 24 }}
+      />
+    );
+  }
+  const suites = state.data;
+  if (suites.length === 0) {
+    return <Empty description="No suites yet — create one to start authoring checks." />;
+  }
+  const selected = suites.find((s) => s.id === selectedId) ?? null;
+
+  return (
+    <Flex gap={24} align="flex-start">
+      <Card size="small" style={{ width: 300, flexShrink: 0 }} styles={{ body: { padding: 0 } }}>
+        <List
+          dataSource={suites}
+          renderItem={(suite) => (
+            <List.Item
+              onClick={() => onSelect(suite.id)}
+              style={{
+                cursor: 'pointer',
+                padding: '12px 16px',
+                background: suite.id === selectedId ? 'rgba(22,119,255,0.08)' : undefined,
+              }}
+            >
+              <Typography.Text strong={suite.id === selectedId}>{suite.name}</Typography.Text>
+            </List.Item>
+          )}
+        />
+      </Card>
+      <div style={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 0 }}>
+        {selected ? (
+          <SuiteDetail
+            key={selected.id}
+            suite={selected}
+            connections={connections}
+            onEdit={() => onEdit(selected)}
+            onDeleted={onDeleted}
+          />
+        ) : (
+          <Empty description="Select a suite to view its checks." style={{ marginTop: 64 }} />
+        )}
+      </div>
+    </Flex>
+  );
+}
+
+function SuiteDetail({
+  suite,
+  connections,
+  onEdit,
+  onDeleted,
+}: {
+  suite: Suite;
+  connections: Connection[];
+  onEdit: () => void;
+  onDeleted: () => void;
+}) {
+  const { message, modal } = App.useApp();
+  // Remounted (keyed by suite.id) when the selection changes → checks refetch.
+  const { state } = useAsyncData(() => listChecks(suite.id));
+  const connection = connections.find((c) => c.id === suite.connection_id);
+
+  const onDelete = () => {
+    modal.confirm({
+      title: `Delete “${suite.name}”?`,
+      content: 'This removes the suite and all of its checks.',
+      okText: 'Delete',
+      okType: 'danger',
+      onOk: async () => {
+        try {
+          await deleteSuite(suite.id);
+          message.success(`${suite.name} deleted`);
+          onDeleted();
+        } catch (err) {
+          message.error(`Delete failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
+          throw err; // keep the confirm modal open on failure
+        }
+      },
+    });
+  };
+
+  return (
+    <Flex vertical gap={16}>
+      <Flex justify="space-between" align="flex-start" gap={12}>
+        <Flex vertical gap={6}>
+          <Typography.Title level={4} style={{ margin: 0 }}>
+            {suite.name}
+          </Typography.Title>
+          {connection ? (
+            <Flex gap={8} align="center">
+              <Typography.Text type="secondary">
+                {connection.name} · {CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[connection.type]}
+              </Typography.Text>
+              <Tag color={ENV_COLORS[connection.env]}>{envLabel(connection.env)}</Tag>
+            </Flex>
+          ) : (
+            <Typography.Text type="secondary">Connection {suite.connection_id}</Typography.Text>
+          )}
+        </Flex>
+        <Flex gap={8}>
+          <Button onClick={onEdit}>Edit</Button>
+          <Button danger onClick={onDelete}>
+            Delete
+          </Button>
+        </Flex>
+      </Flex>
+      {suite.description && <Typography.Paragraph>{suite.description}</Typography.Paragraph>}
+      <ChecksList state={state} />
+    </Flex>
+  );
+}
+
+function ChecksList({ state }: { state: AsyncState<Check[]> }) {
+  if (state.status === 'loading') {
+    return <Spin tip="Loading checks…" />;
+  }
+  if (state.status === 'error') {
+    return <Alert type="error" showIcon title="Failed to load checks" description={state.error} />;
+  }
+  const checks = state.data;
+  return (
+    <Card size="small" title={`Checks (${checks.length})`}>
+      {checks.length === 0 ? (
+        <Empty
+          image={Empty.PRESENTED_IMAGE_SIMPLE}
+          description="No checks yet — the check editor lands in the next slice."
+        />
+      ) : (
+        <List
+          dataSource={checks}
+          renderItem={(check) => (
+            <List.Item>
+              <Flex vertical gap={2}>
+                <Typography.Text strong>{check.name}</Typography.Text>
+                <Typography.Text type="secondary" style={{ fontSize: 12 }}>
+                  {check.expectation_type}
+                </Typography.Text>
+              </Flex>
+            </List.Item>
+          )}
+        />
+      )}
+    </Card>
+  );
+}

Confirmed a real latent issue. Here's the triage.

## Dependabot triage — 10 open PRs

All 10 branches are **7 commits behind `main`** (opened 2026-06-08, before the recent merges), so each needs a rebase before merge.

### ✅ Safe — low-risk, CI green (8)
Minor/patch bumps, all 13 checks passing:

| PR | Bump | Type |
|----|------|------|
| #179 | azure-storage-blob 12.25→12.30 | pip, minor |
| #181 | fastmcp 3.4.1→3.4.2 | pip, patch |
| #182 | uvicorn 0.48→0.49 | pip, minor |
| #183 | opencensus-ext-azure 1.1.14→1.1.15 | pip, patch |
| #184 | @types/react 19.2.16→19.2.17 | npm dev, patch |
| #185 | react-router-dom 7.16→7.17 | npm, minor |
| #187 | @azure/msal-browser 5.11→5.12 | npm, minor |
| #188 | axios 1.16.1→1.17.0 | npm, minor |

### 🟡 Review — major, but dev-only & green (1)
- **#186 @types/node 22 → 25** (major). It's a `devDependency` (type stubs only, never bundled) and `tsc` passes, so low blast radius — but a 3-major jump. Worth a glance, not a blocker.

### 🔴 Hold — major runtime bump, **CI failing, surfaces a real bug** (1)
- **#180 databricks-sql-connector 3.7 → 4.2.** Backend tests fail at collection: `ImportError: Unable to find a usable engine; tried 'pyarrow', 'fastparquet'`.

  **Root cause (latent bug, not the bump's fault):** [flatfile.py:118](backend/app/datasources/flatfile.py#L118) calls `pd.read_parquet(raw, dtype_backend="pyarrow")`, but **`pyarrow` is nowhere in our requirements** — we've been relying on `databricks-sql-connector` 3.x pulling it in transitively. The 4.x connector dropped that transitive dep, so our Parquet flat-file support (and three test modules) breaks. We have an undeclared direct dependency.

## Recommendation
1. **File an issue** for the undeclared `pyarrow` dep, fix by adding it to `requirements.txt` (a defect per working-agreement — surfaces independent of the bump). That fix also unblocks #180.
2. **Merge the 8 safe bumps** (rebase each; npm/pip ones share lockfiles so they go one-at-a-time with Dependabot re-resolving between).
3. **#186** — merge with the safe batch, or hold for a closer look; your call.

@router.patch(
    "/suites/{suite_id}/checks/{check_id}",
    response_model=CheckRead,
    summary="Update a check",
)
def update_check(
    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
    check_id: uuid.UUID,
    payload: CheckUpdate,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> CheckRead:
    require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="edit")
    check = svc.update_check(
        db,
        suite_id,
        check_id,
        name=payload.name,
        expectation_type=payload.expectation_type,
        config=payload.config,
        warn_threshold=payload.warn_threshold,
        fail_threshold=payload.fail_threshold,
        critical_threshold=payload.critical_threshold,
    )
    return CheckRead.model_validate(check)


@router.delete(
    "/suites/{suite_id}/checks/{check_id}",
    status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT,
    summary="Delete a check",
)
def delete_check(
    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
    check_id: uuid.UUID,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> None:
    require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="edit")
    svc.delete_check(db, suite_id, check_id)


# ───────────────────────── dry-run (preview, no persistence) ────────


class CheckDryRunRequest(BaseModel):
    kind: str = "expectation"
    expectation_type: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128)
    config: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    warn_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    fail_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    critical_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    table: str = Field(min_length=1, description="Target table the check runs against")
    schema_: str | None = Field(default=None, alias="schema")


class CheckDryRunResult(BaseModel):
    status: str  # pass | warn | fail | critical (ADR 0005)
    metric_value: float | None
    observed_value: dict[str, Any] | None
    expected_value: dict[str, Any] | None


@router.post(
    "/suites/{suite_id}/checks/dryrun",
    response_model=CheckDryRunResult,
    summary="Dry-run a check against live data (no persistence)",
)
def dry_run_check(
    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
    payload: CheckDryRunRequest,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
    secret_store: Annotated[SecretStore, Depends(get_secret_store)],
) -> CheckDryRunResult:
    # sync def → threadpool; the datasource connect + GX run are blocking.
    # Authoring action → 'edit'. The suite's connection FK is RESTRICT, so it
    # always resolves.
    suite = require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="edit")
    connection = db.get(Connection, suite.connection_id)
    assert connection is not None
    outcome = dryrun.dry_run_check(
        connection,
        kind=payload.kind,
        expectation_type=payload.expectation_type,
        config=payload.config,
        warn_threshold=payload.warn_threshold,
        fail_threshold=payload.fail_threshold,
```

> AGENT

Clear picture: the backend maps `expectation_type` (snake_case) → GX class by title-casing and treats `config` as free-form GX kwargs — no server catalog. So the editor should drive a **curated frontend catalog** of common GX expectations with typed config fields (the same spec pattern as the connection forms). GX column expectations are datasource-agnostic in v1, so one catalog covers all 4.

I'll scope this PR to **check CRUD (catalog-driven editor)** and leave dry-run + profiler as the follow-up slice (keeps it reviewable, one functionality per PR). Let me branch and read the current API module.

column/table expectations are datasource-agnostic in v1 (all four\n * datasources run them through the shared `gx_runner`), so one catalog serves\n * every suite regardless of its connection type.\n */\n\nexport type ConfigFieldType = 'string' | 'number' | 'list';\n\nexport interface ConfigField {\n  /** Key in the GX `config` kwargs object. */\n  name: string;\n  label: string;\n  type: ConfigFieldType;\n  optional?: boolean;\n  help?: string;\n}\n\nexport interface ExpectationSpec {\n  /** snake_case GX expectation type sent to the backend. */\n  type: string;\n  label: string;\n  description: string;\n  fields: ConfigField[];\n}\n\nconst COLUMN: ConfigField = { name: 'column', label: 'Column', type: 'string' };\n\nexport const EXPECTATION_CATALOG: ExpectationSpec[] = [\n  {\n    type: 'expect_column_values_to_not_be_null',\n    label: 'Column values not null',\n    description: 'Every value in the column is non-null.',\n    fields: [COLUMN],\n  },\n  {\n    type: 'expect_column_values_to_be_unique',\n    label: 'Column values unique',\n    description: 'Values in the column are distinct (no duplicates).',\n    fields: [COLUMN],\n  },\n  {\n    type: 'expect_column_values_to_be_between',\n    label: 'Column values in range',\n    description: 'Numeric values fall within [min, max].',\n    fields: [\n      COLUMN,\n      { name: 'min_value', label: 'Minimum', type: 'number', optional: true },\n      { name: 'max_value', label: 'Maximum', type: 'number', optional: true },\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    type: 'expect_column_values_to_be_in_set',\n    label: 'Column values in set',\n    description: 'Every value is one of an allowed set.',\n    fields: [\n      COLUMN,\n      {\n        name: 'value_set',\n        label: 'Allowed values',\n        type: 'list',\n        help: 'Comma-separated list of permitted values.',\n      },\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    type: 'expect_column_value_lengths_to_be_between',\n    label: 'Column value lengths in range',\n    description: 'String lengths fall within [min, max].',\n    fields: [\n      COLUMN,\n      { name: 'min_value', label: 'Min length', type: 'number', optional: true },\n      { name: 'max_value', label: 'Max length', type: 'number', optional: true },\n    ],\n  },\n  {\n    type: 'expect_column_values_to_match_regex',\n    label: 'Column values match regex',\n    description: 'Table row count in range',\n    description: 'The table’s row count falls within [min, max].',\n    fields: [\n      { name: 'min_value', label: 'Minimum rows', type: 'number', optional: true },\n      { name: 'max_value', label: 'Maximum rows', type: 'number', optional: true },\n    ],\n  },\n];\n\n/** Lookup by expectation_type (for prefilling the editor in edit mode). */\nexport const EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE: Record<string, ExpectationSpec> = Object.fromEntries(\n  EXPECTATION_CATALOG.map((e) => [e.type, e]),\n);\n"
