The expectation Select drives\n * which config fields render (from EXPECTATION_CATALOG); the submitted `config`\n * is rebuilt from only the selected expectation's declared fields, so switching\n * types never leaks stale kwargs to the backend.\n */\nexport function CheckDrawer({\n  open,\n  suiteId,\n  check,\n  onClose,\n  onSaved,\n}: {\n  open: boolean;\n  suiteId: string;\n  /** undefined = create; a check = edit. */\n  check?: Check;\n  onClose: () => void;\n  onSaved: () => void;\n}) {\n  const { message } = App.useApp();\n  const [form] = Form.useForm();\n  const isEdit = check !== undefined;\n  const selectedType = Form.useWatch('expectation_type', form) as string | undefined;\n  const spec = selectedType ? EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[selectedType] : undefined;\n\n  // Prefill on open/edit; blank form for create.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!open) return;\n    if (check) {\n      form.setFieldsValue({\n        name: check.name,\n        expectation_type: check.expectation_type,\n        config: configToForm(EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[check.expectation_type], check.config),\n        warn_threshold: check.warn_threshold ?? undefined,\n        fail_threshold: check.fail_threshold ?? undefined,\n        critical_threshold: check.critical_threshold ?? undefined,\n      });\n    } else {\n      form.resetFields();\n    }\n  }, [open, check, form]);\n\n  const onSubmit = async () => {\n    let values: Record<string, unknown>;\n    try {\n      values = await form.validateFields();\n    } catch {\n      return; // inline validation errors\n    }\n    const activeSpec = EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[values.expectation_type as string];\n    const payload = {\n      name: values.name as string,\n      expectation_type: values.expectation_type as string,\n      config: formToConfig(activeSpec, (values.config ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>),\n      warn_threshold: numOrNull(values.warn_threshold),\n      fail_threshold: numOrNull(values.fail_threshold),\n      critical_threshold: numOrNull(values.critical_threshold),\n    };\n    try {\n      if (isEdit) {\n        await updateCheck(suiteId, check.id, payload);\n        message.success(`${payload.name}: saved`);\n      } else {\n        await createCheck(suiteId, payload);\n        message.success(`${payload.name}: created`);\n      }\n      onSaved();\n    } catch (err) {\n      message.error(`Save failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Drawer\n      title={isEdit ? `Edit “${check.name}”` : 'New check'}\n      open={open}\n      onClose={onClose}\n      width={520}\n      destroyOnHidden\n      extra={\n        <Flex gap={8}>\n          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>\n          <Button type=\"primary\" onClick={onSubmit}>\n            {isEdit ? 'Save' : 'Create'}\n          </Button>\n        </Flex>\n      }\n    >\n      <Form form={form} layout=\"vertical\">\n        <Form.Item name=\"name\" label=\"Name\" rules={[{ required: true }]}>\n          <Input placeholder=\"e.g. order_id not null\" />\n        </Form.Item>\n        <Form.Item name=\"expectation_type\" label=\"Expectation\" rules={[{ required: true }]}>\n          <Select\n            placeholder=\"Select an expectation\"\n            options={EXPECTATION_CATALOG.map((e) => ({ value: e.type, label: e.label }))}\n          />\n        </Form.Item>\n\n        {spec && (\n          <>\n            <Typography.Paragraph type=\"secondary\" style={{ marginTop: -8 }}>\n              {spec.description}\n            </Typography.Paragraph>\n            {spec.fields.map((field) => (\n              <ConfigFieldItem key={field.name} field={field} />\n            ))}\n          </>\n        )}\n\n        <Divider style={{ margin: '8px 0 16px' }}>Severity thresholds (optional)</Divider>\n        <Typography.Paragraph type=\"secondary\" style={{ marginTop: -8 }}>\n          Band the GX unexpected-% to warn / fail / critical (higher = worse). Leave blank for a\n          binary pass/fail.\n        </Typography.Paragraph>\n        <Flex gap={12}>\n          <Form.Item name=\"warn_threshold\" label=\"Warn ≥\" style={{ flex: 1 }}>\n            <InputNumber min={0} max={100} style={{ width: '100%' }} />\n          </Form.Item>\n          <Form.Item name=\"fail_threshold\" label=\"Fail ≥\" style={{ flex: 1 }}>\n            <InputNumber min={0} max={100} style={{ width: '100%' }} />\n          </Form.Item>\n          <Form.Item name=\"critical_threshold\" label=\"Critical ≥\" style={{ flex: 1 }}>\n            <InputNumber min={0} max={100} style={{ width: '100%' }} />\n          </Form.Item>\n        </Flex>\n      </Form>\n    </Drawer>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction ConfigFieldItem({ field }: { field: ConfigField }) {\n  const label = field.optional ? `${field.label} (optional)` : field.label;\n  const rules = field.optional ? undefined : [{ required: true }];\n  return (\n    <Form.Item name={['config', field.name]} label={label} rules={rules} extra={field.help}>\n      {field.type === 'number' ? (\n        <InputNumber style={{ width: '100%' }} />\n      ) : (\n        <Input placeholder={field.type === 'list' ? 'value1, value2, value3' : undefined} />\n      )}\n    </Form.Item>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction numOrNull(v: unknown): number | null {\n  return typeof v === 'number' ? v : null;\n}\n\n/** Build the GX `config` kwargs from only the selected expectation's fields. */\nfunction formToConfig(\n  spec: ExpectationSpec | undefined,\n  raw: Record<string, unknown>,\n): Record<string, unknown> {\n  const config: Record<string, unknown> = {};\n  if (!spec) return config;\n  for (const field of spec.fields) {\n    const value = raw[field.name];\n    if (value === undefined || value === null || value === '') continue;\n    if (field.type === 'list') {\n      const items = String(value)\n        .split(',')\n        .map((s) => s.trim())\n        .filter(Boolean);\n      if (items.length > 0) config[field.name] = items;\n    } else {\n      config[field.name] = value;\n    }\n  }\n  return config;\n}\n\n/** Inverse of formToConfig for edit-mode prefill (list array → comma string). */\nfunction configToForm(\n  spec: ExpectationSpec | undefined,\n  config: Record<string, unknown>,\n): Record<string, unknown> {\n  const form: Record<string, unknown> = {};\n  if (!spec) return form;\n  for (const field of spec.fields) {\n    const value = config[field.name];\n    if (value === undefined) continue;\n    form[field.name] = field.type === 'list' && Array.isArray(value) ? value.join(', ') : value;\n  }\n  return form;\n}\n"

I now have full context. Let me analyze the duplication and altitude concerns.

Key observations:

1. **Drawer scaffold duplication** — `ConnectionDrawer`, `SuiteDrawer`, `CheckDrawer` all repeat: `Drawer` + `Form` + `useEffect` prefill + `validateFields`/`onFinish` try/catch + `message.success`/`message.error` + `onSaved`. But they differ in field shape, edit-mode immutability rules, the form-typing approach (`onFinish` vs imperative `validateFields`), and config-marshalling. Notably the three already drifted: ConnectionDrawer uses `onFinish` + `submitting` state, the other two use imperative `onSubmit`. That drift is itself evidence that a premature shared scaffold would be fought against.

2. **`modal.confirm` delete pattern** — now 3x (ConnectionCard, SuiteDetail, ChecksList), nearly identical: title, okText Delete, okType danger, try/await delete/message.success/onChanged, catch message.error + `throw err`. This is the most mechanical, lowest-variance duplication — a strong helper candidate.

3. **`ConfigFieldItem` vs `ConfigTextField`** — same spec-driven `name={['config', field.name]}` idiom, diverging only by type-switch (number/list vs text-only). Parallel idiom, acceptable but worth noting.

4. **Catalog altitude / coupling risk** — field `name`s must equal GX kwarg names exactly with no compile-time check.

5. **`numOrNull` typing** — minor; `InputNumber` with `min/max` but `numOrNull` silently coerces non-number to null (a stale string would become null silently rather than erroring).

Let me note the error-string duplication too: `err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'` appears ~6 times.

## Summary

Reviewed `CheckDrawer.tsx`, `expectationCatalog.ts`, and `Suites.tsx` against the existing connection/suite drawer code. No correctness bugs that break the feature; findings are cleanup/altitude. Ranked by what a maintainer would actually act on:

1. **`modal.confirm` delete helper (highest value)** — verbatim 3x duplication (`Suites.tsx:171`, `Suites.tsx:252`, `Connections.tsx:177`), including the load-bearing `throw err`. A `useConfirmDelete` hook is a clean, low-risk extraction.

2. **Drawer scaffold — do NOT fully abstract.** The three drawers have already drifted (`onFinish`+`submitting` vs imperative `onSubmit`; `footer` vs `extra`) and have genuinely different field/immutability rules. A forced `<EntityDrawer>` would be fought. But two narrow wins exist: extract the repeated `err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'` formatter (~6 occurrences), and **align the missing submit loading-state** — only `ConnectionDrawer` guards against double-submit; `CheckDrawer`/`SuiteDrawer` don't.

3. **Catalog altitude is correct, coupling is the risk.** Frontend-owned catalog is the right call (backend is intentionally catalog-free, free-form GX kwargs). The real exposure: `ConfigField.name`/`ExpectationSpec.type` must match GX kwarg/class names exactly with zero compile-time check — fails only at worker run-time. Worth a contract test asserting the catalog resolves against the pinned GX version, given CLAUDE.md's explicit "GX API drifts across point releases" warning.

4. **`numOrNull` + loose `Form<Record<string,unknown>>` typing** — CheckDrawer is the weakest-typed of the three drawers; `numOrNull` silently coerces non-numbers to null. Fragile but not currently broken.

5. **`ConfigFieldItem` vs `ConfigTextField`** — same idiom, acceptable parallel duplication; flagged only for drift risk on the optional/label/rules boilerplate.

No files were modified (report-only).

To go from editing A to editing B, the user must close the drawer (only Edit buttons in the list trigger `onEdit`, and the drawer overlays). Actually no — the list is behind the drawer overlay; clicking another Edit isn't possible while open. So A→B direct switch isn't reachable without closing first. On close, `open` goes false; `destroyOnHidden` unmounts the form children. Reopening with B runs the effect with the new `check`. Because `formToConfig` scopes to B's spec, stale A config keys (if preserved in store) are filtered out on submit. **So no stale-field submission bug** — the `formToConfig` scoping is the effective guard, exactly as the doc comment claims.

However, there IS a residual prefill display bug worth noting: `setFieldsValue` merges; if A had `config.column = "x"` and B's type also has a `column` field but B's stored config has no column, `configToForm` returns `{}` for that key (skipped via `value === undefined`), and the merge leaves A's stale `column` visible in B's form. But on edit, B always comes from the backend with its own config, so `configToForm` returns B's actual values — overwriting. Only fields B *lacks* but A *had* could linger visually, but those get filtered by `formToConfig` on submit. Low severity (cosmetic prefill only). I'll note it but it's minor.

Notes on the items the prompt flagged that I verified are NOT bugs (for confidence):

- **0-is-valid concern (highest priority):** `formToConfig` uses a strict `value === ''` check (line 182), NOT a falsy check, so `min_value: 0`, `max_value: 0`, and row-count `0` survive correctly. `numOrNull` (line 170) uses `typeof v === 'number'`, so a threshold of `0` survives too. `configToForm` (line 205) skips only `=== undefined`, so prefilled `0` survives. **Correct on all three.**
- **Stale-field submission on type switch (concern 3/7):** `formToConfig` iterates only `activeSpec.fields`, so even though `setFieldsValue` merges and `validateFields()` (with antd's default `preserve:true`) returns stale keys, the payload's `config` is rebuilt from the new type's fields only. Stale kwargs from the old type are NOT submitted. The doc comment's claim holds.
- **Payload contract (concern 5):** Create payload (lines 74-81) has exactly `name, expectation_type, config, warn/fail/critical_threshold` — matches `CheckCreate`; omitting `kind` is correct (backend defaults to `"expectation"`). No extra/missing fields. Update omits `kind` correctly (immutable). Clearing a threshold sends `null`, correctly resetting it.
- **Two Delete buttons (concern 6):** Per-check Delete and suite Delete are separate components with distinct `onClick`/`modal.confirm` handlers — no runtime wiring confusion (only a potential test-selector ambiguity). Reload wiring after save/delete is correct (`onChanged={reload}`, `onSaved` closes + reloads).

The strongest finding is #1 (value_set delimiter-only input → silently dropped → late GX failure). Finding #2 is lower severity (prefill display) and is partially self-mitigating.

**PR #203 merged.** The catalog-driven check editor is on `main`.

## What shipped
- **`expectationCatalog.ts`** — curated GX expectations with typed config fields (the frontend owns this since the backend has no server catalog)
- **`CheckDrawer.tsx`** — expectation-driven dynamic config form; config rebuilt from only the active expectation's fields (no stale-kwarg leakage); optional warn/fail/critical thresholds; comma-list round-trip
- Suite detail wired with **Add check / Edit / Delete**; `createCheck`/`updateCheck`/`deleteCheck` API
- 41 frontend tests green

## Review-agent pass (spawned, not inline)
The agents **cleared** the highest-risk items (0-is-a-valid-value survives the strict `=== ''` guard; payload matches `CheckCreate`; no stale-kwarg submission). Three real fixes applied before merge:
- **value_set validator** — delimiter-only input (`","`) was passing `required` but saving an empty config that only failed later at GX run time → now rejected inline
- **edit prefill** — always `resetFields()` first (antd retains unmounted-field values across open/close)
- **double-submit guard** — added the `submitting` state CheckDrawer was missing

Deferred-but-filed (per the track-don't-drop rule): **#204** (consolidate the 3× `confirmDelete` / `errorMessage` / SuiteDrawer's missing submit guard) and **#205** (a contract test asserting catalog field names resolve against the pinned GX version — the one coupling with no compile-time check).

## Next slice
**Dry-run preview** (`POST /suites/{id}/checks/dryrun` — runs a check against live data, needs a target table) **+ the profiler panel**. That closes out the Week-4 check-authoring loop. Want me to start it?

## 1. #203 main CI failure — infrastructure, not code
The failed run on #203's merge commit (`7f5a6ae`) was the `Backend — tests` job **timing out pulling the Postgres service-container image from Docker Hub** (`registry-1.docker.io: Client.Timeout exceeded`, three retries all failing). A transient registry blip — nothing in #203's code.

It's already verified green: #206 (docs) branched off main *after* #203 merged, and its CI passed (`3c76819`) — that run included all of #203's code. Main HEAD is and has stayed green. No fix needed.

## 2. The open-issues list — you were right, I broke it
Two real faults in my #206 snapshot edit, now fixed in **#207 (merged)**:

- **#146 was listed as "closed" but was still open** on GitHub. Both its symptoms had actually shipped (worker runner-dispatch #165 + profiler registry), but the PRs said `(#146)` not `Fixes #146`, so it never auto-closed — leaving the doc internally contradictory (infra table said closed, snapshot said closed, GitHub said open). I've now **actually closed #146** on GitHub referencing both PRs.
- **I dropped the Week-1 carryover issues** (#168 token refresh, #169 real Key Vault, #170 prod-docs gate). That's what made it read infra/cleanup-heavy — it wasn't *only* infra (the frontend nits + governance were still there), but it was **incomplete**, which is the actual fault.

```
60	    onEdit: (connection) => setDrawer({ open: true, connection }),
61	    onReauth: setReauthing,
62	    onChanged: reload,
63	  };
64	
65	  return (
66	    <Flex vertical gap={24}>
67	      <Flex justify="space-between" align="center" gap={12}>
68	        <Typography.Title level={3} style={{ margin: 0 }}>
69	          Connections
70	        </Typography.Title>
71	        <Button type="primary" onClick={() => setDrawer({ open: true })}>
72	          Add connection
73	        </Button>
74	      </Flex>
75	      <ConnectionsBody state={state} actions={actions} />
76	      <ConnectionDrawer
77	        open={drawer.open}
78	        connection={drawer.connection}
79	        onClose={() => setDrawer({ open: false })}
80	        onSaved={() => {
81	          setDrawer({ open: false });
82	          reload();
83	        }}
84	      />
85	      <ReauthModal
86	        connection={reauthing}
87	        onClose={() => setReauthing(null)}
88	        onDone={() => {
89	          setReauthing(null);
90	          reload();
91	        }}
92	      />
93	    </Flex>
94	  );
95	}
96	
97	function ConnectionsBody({
98	  state,
99	  actions,
100	}: {
101	  state: AsyncState<Connection[]>;
102	  actions: ConnectionActions;
103	}) {
104	  if (state.status === 'loading') {
105	    return <Spin tip="Loading connections…" size="large" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;
106	  }
107	  if (state.status === 'error') {
108	    return (
109	      <Alert
110	        type="error"
111	        showIcon
112	        title="Failed to load connections"
113	        description={state.error}
114	        style={{ margin: 24 }}
115	      />
116	    );
117	  }
118	  const connections = state.data;
119	  if (connections.length === 0) {
120	    return <Empty description="No connections configured yet" />;
121	  }
122	  return (
123	    <>
124	      {groupByType(connections).map(([type, group]) => (
125	        <ConnectionTypeSection key={type} type={type} connections={group} actions={actions} />
126	      ))}
127	    </>
128	  );
129	}
130	
131	function ConnectionTypeSection({
132	  type,
133	  connections,
134	  actions,
135	}: {
136	  type: ConnectionType;
137	  connections: Connection[];
138	  actions: ConnectionActions;
139	}) {
140	  return (
141	    <Flex vertical gap={12}>
142	      <Typography.Title level={5} style={{ margin: 0 }}>
143	        {CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[type]}
144	      </Typography.Title>
145	      <Flex wrap gap={12}>
146	        {connections.map((connection) => (
147	          <ConnectionCard key={connection.id} connection={connection} actions={actions} />
148	        ))}
149	      </Flex>
150	    </Flex>
151	  );
152	}
153	
154	function ConnectionCard({
155	  connection,
156	  actions,
157	}: {
158	  connection: Connection;
159	  actions: ConnectionActions;
160	}) {
161	  const { message, modal } = App.useApp();
162	  const [testing, setTesting] = useState(false);
163	
164	  const onTest = async () => {
165	    setTesting(true);
166	    try {
167	      const { ok } = await testConnection(connection.id);
168	      if (ok) message.success(`${connection.name}: connection OK`);
169	      else message.error(`${connection.name}: connection test failed`);
170	    } catch (err) {
171	      message.error(`${connection.name}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'test failed'}`);
172	    } finally {
173	      setTesting(false);
174	    }
175	  };
176	
177	  const onDelete = () => {
178	    modal.confirm({
179	      title: `Delete “${connection.name}”?`,
180	      content: 'This removes the connection and its stored credential.',
181	      okText: 'Delete',
182	      okType: 'danger',
183	      onOk: async () => {
184	        try {
185	          await deleteConnection(connection.id);
186	          message.success(`${connection.name} deleted`);
187	          actions.onChanged();
188	        } catch (err) {
189	          message.error(`Delete failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
190	          throw err; // keep the confirm modal open on failure
191	        }
192	      },
193	    });
194	  };
195	
196	  const menuItems = [
197	    { key: 'edit', label: 'Edit', onClick: () => actions.onEdit(connection) },
198	    { key: 'reauth', label: 'Re-authenticate', onClick: () => actions.onReauth(connection) },
199	    { type: 'divider' as const },
200	    { key: 'delete', label: 'Delete', danger: true, onClick: onDelete },
201	  ];
202	
203	  return (
204	    <Card size="small" style={{ minWidth: 280 }}>
205	      <Flex justify="space-between" align="center" gap={12}>
206	        <Flex vertical gap={6}>
207	          <Typography.Text strong>{connection.name}</Typography.Text>
208	          <Flex gap={8} align="center">
209	            <Tag color={ENV_COLORS[connection.env]}>{envLabel(connection.env)}</Tag>
210	            {connection.has_secret ? (
211	              <Badge status="success" text="credential set" />
212	            ) : (
213	              <Badge status="warning" text="no credential" />
214	            )}
215	          </Flex>
216	        </Flex>
217	        <Flex gap={8} align="center">
218	          <Button size="small" loading={testing} onClick={onTest}>
219	            Test
220	          </Button>
221	          <Dropdown menu={{ items: menuItems }} trigger={['click']}>
222	            <Button
223	              size="small"
224	              icon={<MoreOutlined />}
225	              aria-label={`${connection.name} actions`}
226	            />
227	          </Dropdown>
228	        </Flex>
229	      </Flex>
230	    </Card>
231	  );
232	}
233	
```

Connections\n        </Typography.Title>\n        <Flex gap={8}>\n          <Button\n            loading={testingAll}\n            disabled={connections.length === 0}\n            onClick={testAll}\n          >\n            Test all\n          </Button>\n          <Button type=\"primary\" onClick={() => setDrawer({ open: true })}>\n            Add connection\n          </Button>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n      <ConnectionsBody state={state} actions={actions} health={health} />\n      <ConnectionDrawer\n        open={drawer.open}\n        connection={drawer.connection}\n        onClose={() onClose={() => setReauthing(null)}\n        onDone={() => {\n          setReauthing(null);\n          reload();\n        }}\n      />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction ConnectionsBody({\n  state,\n  actions,\n  health,\n}: {\n  state: AsyncState<Connection[]>;\n  actions: ConnectionActions;\n  health: Record<string, HealthState>;\n}) {\n  if (state.status === 'loading') {\n    return <Spin tip=\"Loading connections…\" size=\"large\" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;\n  }\n  if (state.status === 'error') {\n    return (\n      <Alert\n        type=\"error\"\n        showIcon\n  return <Empty description=\"No connections configured yet\" />;\n  }\n  return (\n    <>\n      {groupByType(connections).map(([type, group]) => (\n        <ConnectionTypeSection\n          key={type}\n          type={type}\n          connections={group}\n          actions={actions}\n          health={health}\n        />\n      ))}\n    </>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction ConnectionTypeSection({\n I have all the context. Let me analyze each scrutiny point carefully.

**Items 1-2 (concurrency, throw):** `setHealth` uses updater form — safe under concurrent `Promise.all`. `testOne` has try/catch covering `testConnection`; the only other code is two `setHealth` calls (synchronous, won't throw) and `.ok` destructure (inside try). So `testOne` never rejects → `Promise.all` never rejects → `testingAll` correctly resets. Both fine.

**Items 4/5/7 (stale health):** Tracing reload paths — `reload()` only bumps the nonce in `useAsyncData`, never touches the `health` map. So:
- **Item 7**: re-auth success → `onDone` → reload → health map untouched → `'failed'` badge + "Re-authenticate" link persist after a successful credential rotation. Real UX bug.
- **Item 5**: edit config → reload → stale `'ok'`/`'failed'` badge persists. Real but more minor.
- **Item 4**: deleted connection's entry lingers (unbounded growth, no wrong-badge since UUIDs). Minor.

**Item 6:** Switch covers all 4 union members. TS with no `default` — exhaustive, fine. `health` is never `undefined` (parent passes `?? 'idle'`). Fine.

Let me verify there's a duplicate re-auth action and confirm the `message` from `App.useApp()` in the card is still used (delete uses it). Both fine. Now confirming the most material finding — the failed badge persisting across re-auth is the strongest. Let me double check whether `testOne` is even reachable in a way that the stale-badge after edit applies (the card's local `testing` state was removed, good).

One more concrete check: item 3 stale closure on `connections` in `testAll` — `connections` is recomputed each render from `state`; `testAll` is recreated each render (not memoized), so the closure captures the latest render's `connections`. Between render and click it's current. Low/non-issue.

```
import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { App as AntApp, ConfigProvider } from 'antd';
import { BrowserRouter } from 'react-router-dom';

import { App } from './App';
import { CurrentUserProvider } from './auth/CurrentUserProvider';
import { MsalProvider } from './auth/MsalProvider';
import { getMsalInstance } from './auth/msalInstance';
import './styles.css';

const maybeRoot = document.getElementById('root');
if (!maybeRoot) {
  throw new Error('Root element #root not found in index.html');
}
const rootEl: HTMLElement = maybeRoot;

// MSAL lifecycle (issue #62):
//   1. .initialize() must complete before any MSAL API call (v5 requirement).
//   2. .handleRedirectPromise() must resolve before React renders so the
//      first paint reflects post-login state.
//   3. Errors surface to the console + a static page — fail loud during dev.
async function bootstrap() {
  const instance = getMsalInstance();
  if (instance) {
    await instance.initialize();
    await instance.handleRedirectPromise();
  }
  createRoot(rootEl).render(
    <StrictMode>
      <ConfigProvider>
        <AntApp>
          <MsalProvider>
            <CurrentUserProvider>
              <BrowserRouter>
                <App />
              </BrowserRouter>
            </CurrentUserProvider>
          </MsalProvider>
        </AntApp>
      </ConfigProvider>
    </StrictMode>,
  );
}

bootstrap().catch((err) => {
  console.error('MSAL bootstrap failed', err);
  rootEl.innerHTML =
    '<pre style="padding:24px;color:#a00">Authentication bootstrap failed. See console.</pre>';
});
```

> AGENT

`extra="forbid"` is genuinely blocked: `.env.example` mixes **compose-only vars** (`POSTGRES_USER/PASSWORD/DB`, consumed by the postgres container) with app vars, and Settings has no fields for them — flipping to `forbid` would crash the app on startup. That's exactly the precondition ("once compose-only vs app-only `.env` are split") and it isn't met. So I'll do the **two real frontend items** now (error boundary + code-splitting) and keep #3 deferred with a clear note.

```json
  "content": "import { Button, Result } from 'antd';\nimport { Component, type ErrorInfo, type ReactNode } from 'react';\n\ninterface Props {\n  children: ReactNode;\n}\n\ninterface State {\n  error: Error | null;\n}\n\n/**\n * Catches render-time errors anywhere in the app subtree and shows an antd\n * fallback instead of React's blank screen. (main.tsx's bootstrap `.catch`\n * only covers the pre-render MSAL bootstrap; this covers everything after the\n * first paint.) Error boundaries must be class components — there is no hook\n * equivalent for `getDerivedStateFromError`.\n */\nexport class ErrorBoundary extends Component<Props, State> {\n  state: State = { error: null };\n\n  static getDerivedStateFromError(error: Error): State {\n    return { error };\n  }\n\n  componentDidCatch(error: Error, info: ErrorInfo): void {\n    // Surfaced to the console (and, once wired, App Insights) — fail loud.\n    console.error('Unhandled render error', error, info.componentStack);\n  }\n\n  render(): ReactNode {\n    if (this.state.error) {\n      return (\n        <Result\n          status=\"error\"\n          title=\"Something went wrong\"\n          subTitle={this.state.error.message}\n          extra={\n            <Button type=\"primary\" onClick={() => window.location.reload()}>\n              Reload\n            </Button>\n          }\n        />\n      );\n    }\n    return this.props.children;\n  }\n}\n"
}
```

```
"""Idempotent dev-data seed (run by scripts/setup.sh, safe to re-run).

Gives a fresh local database a minimal baseline so the UI and API aren't empty
on first boot:

- the **dev-bypass user** (the same fixed identity `auth_dev_bypass` resolves
  every request to), so seeded rows are owned by the user you actually log in as
  locally; and
- the **probe Connection + Suite + Check**, reusing `ensure_probe_fixtures` so
  the seed never drifts from what the Week-1 probe endpoint expects.

Both steps get-or-create, so running this repeatedly is a no-op. Run as a module
(so `backend.*` imports resolve from the repo root):

    conda run -n dataq python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from backend.app.core.auth import (
    DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID,
    DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,
    DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,
    _upsert_user,
)
from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
from backend.app.db.session import get_session
from backend.app.services.probe import ensure_probe_fixtures


def seed() -> None:
    settings = get_settings()
    session = get_session()
    try:
        user = _upsert_user(
            session,
            aad_object_id=DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID,
            email=DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,
            display_name=DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,
        )
        connection, suite, checks = ensure_probe_fixtures(session, user=user, settings=settings)
        print(
            "Seeded dev data: "
            f"user={user.email} connection={connection.name} "
            f"suite={suite.name} checks={len(checks)}"
        )
    finally:
        session.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    seed()
```

            {\"column\": \"amount\", \"min_value\": 0, \"max_value\": 100000},\n                Decimal(\"1\"),\n                Decimal(\"5\"),\n                Decimal(\"10\"),\n            ),\n            (\n                \"status in set\",\n                \"expect_column_values_to_be_in_set\",\n                {\"column\": \"status\", \"value_set\": [\"new\", \"paid\", \"shipped\", \"cancelled\"]},\n                None,\n                None,\n                None,\n            ),\n        ],\n    ),\n    (\n        \"Customer files\",\n        \"s3-datalake\",\n        \"prod\",\n        \"Schema + volume checks on the daily customer export drops.\",\n        [\n            (\n                \"row count sane\",\n                \"expect_table_row_count_to_be_between\",\n                {\"min_value\": 1, \"max_value\": 5000000},\n                None,\n                None,\n                None,\n            ),\n            (\"email present\", \"expect_column_values_to_not_be_null\", {\"column\": \"email\"}, None, None, None),\n        ],\n    ),\n    (\n        \"Lakehouse events\",\n        \"uc-lakehouse\",\n        \"uat\",\n        \"Validity checks on the streaming events Delta table.\",\n        [\n            (\n                \"event_type in set\",\n                \"expect_column_values_to_be_in_set\",\n                {\"column\": \"event_type\", \"value_set\": [\"click\", \"view\", \"purchase\"]},\n                None,\n                None,\n                None,\n            ),\n        ],\n    ),\n]\n\n\ndef _get_or_create_connection(\n    session: Session,\n    *,\n    name: str,\n    conn_type: str,\n    env: str,\n    config: dict[str, Any],\n    secret: str,\n    owner: User,\n    secret_store: SecretStore,\n) -> Connection:\n    existing = session.scalar(\n        select(Connection).where(Connection.name == name, Connection.env == env)\n    )\n    if existing is not None:\n        return existing\n    return connection_service.create_connection(\n        session,\n        name=name,\n        conn_type=conn_type,\n        env=env,\n        config=config,\n        secret=secret,\n        created_by=owner.id,\n        secret_store=secret_store,\n    )\n\n\ndef _get_or_create_suite(\n    session: Session, *, name: str, connection: Connection, description: str, owner: User\n) -> Suite:\n    existing = session.scalar(\n        select(Suite).where(Suite.name == name, Suite.connection_id == connection.id)\n    )\n    if existing is not None:\n        return existing\n    return suite_service.create_suite(\n        session,\n        name=name,\n        description=description,\n        connection_id=connection.id,\n        created_by=owner.id,\n    )\n\n\ndef _ensure_check(\n    session: Session,\n    *,\n    suite: Suite,\n    name: str,\n    expectation_type: str,\n    config: dict[str, Any],\n    warn: Any,\n    fail: Any,\n    critical: Any,\n) -> None:\n    existing = session.scalar(\n        select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == suite.id, Check.name == name)\n    )\n    if existing is not None:\n        return\n    check_service.create_check(\n        session,\n        suite_id=suite.id,\n        name=name,\n        kind=\"expectation\",\n        expectation_type=expectation_type,\n        config=config,\n        warn_threshold=warn,\n        fail_threshold=fail,\n        critical_threshold=critical,\n    )\n\n\ndef seed_demo_data(session: Session, *, owner: User, secret_store: SecretStore) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Seed the representative dataset. Returns a count summary. Idempotent.\"\"\"\n    analyst = _upsert_user(\n        session, aad_object_id=ANALYST_OID, email=ANALYST_EMAIL, display_name=ANALYST_NAME\n    )\n\n    connections: dict[tuple[str, str], Connection] = {}\n    for name, conn_type, env, config, secret in _CONNECTIONS:\n        conn = _get_or_create_connection(\n            session,\n            name=name,\n            conn_type=conn_type,\n            env=env,\n            config=config,\n            secret=secret,\n            owner=owner,\n            secret_store=secret_store,\n        )\n        connections[(name, env)] = conn\n\n    suite_count = check_count = 0\n    first_suite: Suite | None = None\n    for suite_name, conn_name, env, description, checks in _SUITES:\n        suite = _get_or_create_suite(\n            session,\n            name=suite_name,\n            connection=connections[(conn_name, env)],\n            description=description,\n            owner=owner,\n        )\n        first_suite = first_suite or suite\n        suite_count += 1\n        for check_name, exp_type, config, warn, fail, critical in checks:\n            _ensure_check(\n                session,\n                suite=suite,\n                name=check_name,\n                expectation_type=exp_type,\n                config=config,\n                warn=warn,\n                fail=fail,\n                critical=critical,\n            )\n            check_count += 1\n\n    # Share the first suite with the analyst (idempotent: skip if already shared).\n    if first_suite is not None:\n        already = share_service.list_shares(session, first_suite.id, actor_id=owner.id)\n        if not any(s.user_id == analyst.id for s in already):\n            share_service.grant_share(\n                session,\n                first_suite.id,\n                actor_id=owner.id,\n                target_user_id=analyst.id,\n                permission=\"edit\",\n            )\n\n    session.commit()\n    return {\n        \"connections\": len(connections),\n        \"suites\": suite_count,\n        \"checks\": check_count,\n        \"shares\": 1,\n    }\n"
```json
}
```

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/scripts/e2e_smoke.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Full-stack API E2E smoke against a running DataQ stack (no mocks).\n\nDrives the **real** HTTP API the way the frontend does — dev-bypass auth, the\nseeded demo dataset — and asserts the read + authoring paths work end-to-end\n(HTTP → service → Postgres). Run it after `docker compose up` + the seed:\n\n    python -m backend.scripts.e2e_smoke                 # http://localhost:8000\n    DATAQ_API=http://localhost:8000 python -m backend.scripts.e2e_smoke\n\nWhat it verifies (exit 0 = all passed):\n  1. the six seeded connection types are listed (secrets never returned);\n  2. the demo suites + their checks are retrievable;\n  3. an authoring round-trip: create suite → add a check → read back → delete;\n  4. a dry-run *attempt* returns a structured result/error, not a crash\n     (live connectivity fails-soft without real datasource creds — expected).\n\nLive `test()`/runs against real Snowflake/S3/etc. are out of scope (no creds —\nthe documented deferred smoke); this proves the app layer, not the datasources.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport uuid\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport httpx\n\nAPI = os.environ.get(\"DATAQ_API\", \"http://localhost:8000\")\nBASE = f\"{API}/api/v1\"\n\n_passed = 0\n_failed = 0\n\n\ndef check(label: str, ok: bool, detail: str = \"\") -> None:\n    global _passed, _failed\n    mark = \"PASS\" if ok else \"FAIL\"\n    if ok:\n        _passed += 1\n    else:\n        _failed += 1\n    print(f\"[{mark}] {label}\" + (f\" — {detail}\" if detail else \"\"))\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    # Dev-bypass: no bearer needed when AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true + environment=dev.\n    client = httpx.Client(base_url=BASE, timeout=30.0)\n\n    # 1. Connections — six types present, no secret leaked.\n    r = client.get(\"/connections\")\n    conns: list[dict[str, Any]] = r.json() if r.status_code == 200 else []\n    types = {c[\"type\"] for c in conns}\n    expected_types = {\"snowflake\", \"s3\", \"adls_gen2\", \"unity_catalog\", \"adf\", \"airflow\"}\n    check(\"GET /connections returns 200\", r.status_code == 200, f\"status={r.status_code}\")\n    check(\n        \"all six connection types seeded\",\n        expected_types.issubset(types),\n        f\"missing={expected_types - types}\",\n    )\n    check(\n        \"secret is never returned on a connection\",\n        all(\"secret\" not in c and \"secret_ref\" not in c for c in conns),\n        \"a connection payload leaked a secret field\",\n    )\n\n    # 2. Suites + checks retrievable.\n    r = client.get(\"/suites\")\n    suites: list[dict[str, Any]] = r.json() if r.status_code == 200 else []\n    check(\"GET /suites returns the demo suites\", len(suites) >= 3, f\"count={len(suites)}\")\n    orders = next((s for s in suites if s[\"name\"] == \"Orders quality\"), None)\n    check(\"'Orders quality' suite present\", orders is not None)\n    if orders is not None:\n        r = client.get(f\"/suites/{orders['id']}/checks\")\n        checks = r.json() if r.status_code == 200 else []\n        names = {c[\"name\"] for c in checks}\n        check(\n            \"'Orders quality' has its seeded checks\",\n            {\"order_id not null\", \"amount in range\"}.issubset(names),\n            f\"got={sorted(names)}\",\n        )\n        amount = next((c for c in checks if c[\"name\"] == \"amount in range\"), None)\n        check(\n            \"severity thresholds round-trip on a check\",\n            amount is not None and amount[\"fail_threshold\"] == 5,\n            f\"check={amount}\",\n        )\n\n    # 3. Authoring round-trip: create suite → add check → read → delete.\n    conn_id = conns[0][\"id\"] if conns else None\n    if conn_id is not None:\n        name = f\"e2e-smoke-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}\"\n        r = client.post(\"/suites\", json={\"name\": name, \"connection_id\": conn_id})\n        check(\"POST /suites creates a suite\", r.status_code == 201, f\"status={r.status_code}\")\n        sid = r.json()[\"id\"] if r.status_code == 201 else None\n        if sid:\n            r = client.post(\n                f\"/suites/{sid}/checks\",\n                json={\n                    \"name\": \"smoke not null\",\n                    \"expectation_type\": \"expect_column_values_to_not_be_null\",\n                    \"config\": {\"column\": \"id\"},\n                },\n            )\n            check(\"POST a check into the suite\", r.status_code == 201, f\"status={r.status_code}\")\n            r = client.get(f\"/suites/{sid}/checks\")\n            check(\"the new check reads back\", r.status_code == 200 and len(r.json()) == 1)\n\n            # 4. Dry-run attempt: structured outcome, not a 500 crash.\n            r = client.post(\n                f\"/suites/{sid}/checks/dryrun\",\n                json={\n                    \"expectation_type\": \"expect_column_values_to_not_be_null\",\n                    \"config\": {\"column\": \"id\"},\n                    \"table\": \"ORDERS\",\n                    \"schema\": \"PUBLIC\",\n                },\n            )\n            check(\n                \"dry-run returns a structured result/error (fails-soft, no crash)\",\n                r.status_code in (200, 422, 502),\n                f\"status={r.status_code}\",\n            )\n\n            r = client.delete(f\"/suites/{sid}\")\n            check(\"DELETE the smoke suite cleans up\", r.status_code == 204, f\"status={r.status_code}\")\n\n    print(f\"\\n{_passed} passed, {_failed} failed\")\n    return 1 if _failed else 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n"
}
```

```
# Leave empty + set AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true for local dev without a real tenant.
AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true

# SECRET_STORE=env (redis mode reads Redis, not these env vars).
# backend AZURE_* vars and AUTH_DEV_BYPASS so the SPA and the API agree on the
VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true
=== api service command + ports ===
  api:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    env_file:
      - path: .env
        required: false
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: *database-url
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
      # Shared across api + worker so a credential the API writes at runtime is
      # readable by connection-driven worker runs (#86). Dev only — plaintext in
      # Redis. NOTE: in redis mode KV_SECRET_* env vars are NOT consulted (that's
      # `env` mode); set SECRET_STORE=env if you rely on env-provided creds.
      SECRET_STORE: ${SECRET_STORE:-redis}
    volumes:
      # Bind-mount source for hot reload; the conda env in the image is untouched.
      - ./backend:/workspace/backend
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  worker:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile
    restart: unless-stopped
    # -B runs celery-beat embedded in the worker (the #171 orchestration polling
    # schedule). Fine for the single-worker dev stack; prod runs a separate beat.
    command: celery -A backend.app.worker.celery_app worker -B --loglevel=INFO
    env_file:
      - path: .env
        required: false
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: *database-url
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
      # Must match the api service so secrets the API writes are visible here (#86).
      SECRET_STORE: ${SECRET_STORE:-redis}
    volumes:
      - ./backend:/workspace/backend
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  # React/Vite dev server. corepack pins pnpm from package.json's packageManager.
  # node_modules is an anonymous volume so the host's (possibly macOS-built) copy
  # doesn't clobber the container's. pnpm's ~300MB content-addressable store is
  # relocated to /pnpm-store (OUTSIDE the ./frontend bind) and held in its own
  # volume — so nothing leaks into, or creates an empty mountpoint under, the host
  # working tree. The browser loads from localhost:3000 and the Vite proxy forwards
  # /api + /mcp to the api service over the compose network.
```

Share path: the seed checks `list_shares` for existing membership before granting, and `grant_share` itself has a UNIQUE-violation guard → idempotent. But note: the seed's `_SUITES[0]` is "Orders quality" → `first_suite`. The probe suite is also owned by the same owner, but `first_suite` is the demo's first suite, fine.

One subtle idempotency concern on shares: `list_shares` requires `actor_id` to have `view` — owner has it. Fine.

Now item 2 — half-seeded on partial failure. Each `create_*` commits internally. If, say, the 4th connection raises (e.g. SecretWriteError → 502), connections 1–3 are already committed. Re-run resumes via get-or-create. This is self-healing for connections/suites/checks (get-or-create), so on dev it's actually fine. The only non-idempotent-safe gap would be a partial that leaves something that *collides* on re-run — but all paths are SELECT-guarded. So item 2 is low severity/acceptable.

Let me quickly confirm item 4 — no secret logged. The seed prints only counts; `create_connection` logs type/env only; SecretStore.set isn't logging the value. Fine.

Summary of the two real findings (both stem from `conns[0]`):

1. **`conns[0]` is the Airflow connection** — `GET /connections` is `created_at DESC` and `airflow-dags` is seeded last, so the authoring round-trip creates a suite bound to an orchestration provider, which `create_suite` does not block (it only checks the FK, not `connection.type`). This silently green-lights a state the architecture forbids (CLAUDE.md §4/§11).

2. **The dry-run assertion is a near-no-op** — because the suite is on an Airflow connection, `dryrun_service` short-circuits with `DryRunUnsupportedError` (422) before touching any runner. `_SUPPORTED_TYPES = {"snowflake"}`. So the smoke's "fails-soft, no crash" claim is never tested on a real datasource path; the broad `200/422/502` accept would hide a genuine Snowflake dry-run 500.

Both are fixed together by selecting a datasource connection (e.g. the snowflake one) instead of `conns[0]` for the round-trip. Idempotency (item 1) is otherwise **correct**: connection get-or-create is keyed on `(name, env)` matching the real `uq_connections_name_env` constraint, the two `snowflake-analytics` rows differ by env so no collision, `probe-snowflake-dev` ≠ `snowflake-analytics` so no probe clash, and suite/check/share paths are all SELECT-guarded (with `grant_share` additionally guarded by the unique constraint). Item 2 is low-severity/acceptable. Items 4 and 5 are non-issues (no secret logged; global counters fine for a script).

## 1. Frontend coverage: **80.3% lines** (76.7% branch, 70% funcs)

- **Rich seed** (`demo_data.py`) — all six connection types, 3 suites with varied checks + severity thresholds, a cross-user share, seeded through the real service layer (idempotent).
- **API E2E** (`e2e_smoke.py`) — ran against the **live stack**, no mocks: **12/12 pass** (six types listed · secret never leaked · thresholds round-trip · create→check→dry-run→delete · dry-run fails soft as 502).

Along the way I hit two real things:

Fixed the smoke (now exercises the real Snowflake fail-soft) and **filed #212** for the backend validation gap.

**The stack is still running** — open **http://localhost:3000** to click through the seeded data. Tear down with `docker compose down` (add `-v` to also wipe the DB).

```
=== auth/config.ts (how dev bypass is decided) ===
/**
 * Auth configuration sourced from VITE_* env vars at build time.
 *
 * Mode is computed once at module load:
 * - 'real'         — VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID + VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID set.
 *                    MSAL handles redirect-flow login + token acquisition.
 * - 'dev_bypass'   — DEV build + VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true + Azure vars empty.
 *                    No MSAL; renders a fixed dev user. Mirrors backend behaviour.
 * - 'unconfigured' — anything else. AuthGate shows a setup-needed banner.
 */

export type AuthMode = 'real' | 'dev_bypass' | 'unconfigured';

const tenantId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID;
const spaClientId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID;
const apiClientId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID;
const apiScope = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE || 'user_impersonation';
const devBypass = import.meta.env.VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS === 'true';

export const authConfig = {
  tenantId,
  spaClientId,
  apiClientId,
  apiScope,
  apiScopeUri: apiClientId ? `api://${apiClientId}/${apiScope}` : undefined,
} as const;

export const authMode: AuthMode = (() => {
  if (tenantId && spaClientId) return 'real';
  if (import.meta.env.DEV && devBypass) return 'dev_bypass';
  return 'unconfigured';
})();

export const DEV_USER = {
  name: 'Dev Bypass User',
  username: 'dev-bypass@dataq.local',
  homeAccountId: 'dev-bypass',
  isDev: true as const,
};

=== frontend service env in compose ===
  frontend:
    image: node:20-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    working_dir: /app
    command: sh -c "corepack enable && pnpm config set store-dir /pnpm-store && pnpm install && pnpm dev --host"
    environment:
      VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET: http://api:8000
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./frontend:/app
      - /app/node_modules
      - pnpm-store:/pnpm-store
    depends_on:
      - api

volumes:
  postgres_data:
=== is VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS actually in the frontend container env? ===
VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=
VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID=
```

> AGENT

Answered by the code: **no — there's no schedule option for checks/suites yet.** It's a **Week-5** feature (not started).

## How checks run today
There are exactly two trigger paths, neither time-based:
1. **On-demand** — manual dispatch (the probe endpoint / direct `run_suite`).
2. **Event-driven** — `trigger_bindings`: a suite runs when a bound ADF/Airflow **pipeline succeeds** ([orchestration_service.py](backend/app/services/orchestration_service.py)). Failures alert but don't trigger.

There's **no** `schedules`/`cron` table, no per-suite cron API, and no UI to manage them.

## What *is* already in place
Celery **Beat is running** — but it drives one fixed *system* job, not user schedules: `poll-orchestration-runs` every 10 min (the #171 ADF/Airflow polling) in [celery_app.py:56](backend/app/worker/celery_app.py#L56). So the scheduling *infrastructure* exists; what's missing is the user-facing layer.

## What's planned (Week 5 — "scheduling operational")
From the roadmap / [progress.md](docs/progress.md):
- **Scheduled runs table — create, pause, delete cron schedules** (⬜ Execution UI)
- plus the async run UI (run-now, live progress, cancel)

Building it means: a `schedules` table (`suite_id`, cron expr, enabled, env) → an API → a beat entry that reads schedules from the DB (e.g. a DB-backed beat scheduler or a dispatcher task that checks due schedules each minute) → the UI to manage them. The beat process is already wired, so it's an additive build, not new infra.

So: **on-demand + on-pipeline-success now; cron schedules are the Week-5 slice.** Want me to pull scheduling forward as the next piece (it pairs naturally with the dry-run/profiler UI and the async-run UI), or keep to the planned order?

Also — #214 merged, so a hard-refresh of localhost:3000 now gets you into the seeded app under dev-bypass.

Both are answered clearly by the code — and the short version is **planned, not abandoned**, but with one important design correction.

## 1. Run button — not built yet (Week 5)
There's **no manual run trigger** anywhere in the UI, and there isn't even a general backend endpoint for it yet. The *only* thing that dispatches a suite run today is the dev probe — [probe.py:74](backend/app/api/v1/probe.py#L74) (`run_suite.delay`). There's no `POST /suites/{id}/run`, and `frontend/src/api/` has no runs module.

This is the **Week-5 "Execution UI"** slice (all ⬜ in [progress.md](docs/progress.md)):
- Run-now panel · live run-progress (check-by-check) · cancel · recent-runs table

So: **not implemented, planned for Week 5.**

## 2. Binding a pipeline/DAG — partly built, but it's a *suite*-level concept, not a check field
Your instinct is right that it's missing from the UI — but it would **never** go in the *check* editor. The binding is **suite ↔ pipeline**, provider-agnostic: `trigger_bindings` = (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`) → **`suite_id`** ([trigger_bindings.py](backend/app/api/v1/trigger_bindings.py)). When the bound ADF pipeline / Airflow DAG **succeeds**, the *whole suite* runs (all its checks). There's no per-check binding by design (CLAUDE.md §4: orchestration providers are never a datasource/check field).

State of it:
- **Backend CRUD: done** (#172, merged) — you can create/list/delete bindings via the API.
- **UI: not built** — there's no "Triggers" panel on a suite yet. That's the missing piece you noticed (just in the wrong place — it belongs on the suite, not the check).
- **End-to-end execution is still gated**: even when a pipeline succeeds, [orchestration_service.py:230](backend/app/services/orchestration_service.py#L230) creates the queued `Run` but logs `suite_dispatch_deferred` instead of firing it.

## The real blocker behind both: checks don't carry a target table
A check today doesn't store *what table/path it runs against* — the dry-run passes `table` in the request body. Until a check (or suite) carries its target, neither a manual "Run" nor a pipeline-triggered run can actually execute a real suite. That's the load-bearing gap, and it's why dispatch is gated.

## So, in order, the missing pieces are:
1. **Target table/path on checks** (modeling gap — unblocks all real runs)
2. **Manual run + run-progress UI** (Week-5 Execution UI) ← your "Run button"
3. **Suite Triggers panel** (UI over the existing `trigger_bindings` API) ← your "bind a pipeline/DAG"

All planned for Week 5; none abandoned. Given you've now spotted the target-table gap as the thing blocking real execution, **I'd suggest tackling #1 next** (it's the prerequisite for everything run-related) — ahead of the dry-run/profiler UI polish. Want me to scope the target-table modeling, or stay on the current Week-4 UI track?

## Done — summary

**1. Switched secret scanning gitleaks → betterleaks** (verified legitimate first: it's from the gitleaks creator, backed by Aikido, an explicit drop-in replacement — not a typosquat). Latest release `v1.4.1` (2026-06-06). Changes:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [.pre-commit-config.yaml](.pre-commit-config.yaml#L45) | hook → `betterleaks/betterleaks` `rev: v1.4.1`, id `betterleaks` |
| [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml#L164) | CI job now runs the pinned container `ghcr.io/betterleaks/betterleaks:v1.4.1` |
| [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#L59), [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md#L147), [CLAUDE.md:306](CLAUDE.md#L306), [ADR 0013](docs/adr/0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md#L47) | prose references updated |

**One thing to flag:** betterleaks has **no official GitHub Action** (unlike `gitleaks-action@v3`), so I couldn't do a one-line `uses:` swap in CI. I pinned the official Docker image and run `git /repo --redact --verbose` — as a gitleaks drop-in it exits nonzero on findings, which fails the job. If you'd rather install the binary directly instead of pulling a container, say so.

I haven't run `pre-commit autoupdate`/install (it builds the Go hook) or committed anything — let me know if you want either.

**2. GitHub Secret Scanning Push Protection: ❌ disabled.**

In fact native **secret scanning itself is disabled** too. The repo is **public**, so both are free. They're a server-side net (catches what bypasses the client-side hook — e.g. `--no-verify`, or pushes from machines without pre-commit installed), so worth enabling alongside betterleaks rather than instead of it. I can turn both on via:

```
gh api -X PATCH repos/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ \
  -f 'security_and_analysis[secret_scanning][status]=enabled' \
  -f 'security_and_analysis[secret_scanning_push_protection][status]=enabled'
```

> AGENT

Review complete. The diff is mostly a clean mechanical swap (docs + config). One real risk in the CI job survived verification:

```json
[
  {
    "file": ".github/workflows/ci.yml",
    "line": 178,
    "summary": "Dockerized git scan may fail with 'detected dubious ownership' because the container runs as root (uid 0) while actions/checkout writes files as the runner user (uid 1001).",
    "failure_scenario": "If betterleaks shells out to git (rather than using a pure-Go git impl), git's safe.directory check fires on the uid mismatch between /repo's owner and root → 'fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository at /repo', the scan aborts, and the job either errors or — worse — exits 0 without scanning anything, silently disabling the merge gate."
  }
]
```

**My take:** This is the one thing worth confirming before relying on the gate. The gitleaks-action handled checkout/ownership internally; a raw `docker run` doesn't. Two ways to harden it, both cheap:

- Add `-e GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 -e GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.directory -e GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/repo` to the `docker run`, **or**
- Run betterleaks via its pre-commit hook in CI instead (reuses the config we already pinned), sidestepping the container entirely.

Everything else (pre-commit hook coordinates, doc references) is correct.

```
Based on the search results, here's what I found about pre-commit's golang language support:

## Go Installation Behavior

As of version 3.0.0, pre-commit will bootstrap Go if it is not present. This represents an important change—previously you were required to have Go already installed on your system.

However, the behavior varies depending on your pre-commit version:

- **Pre-commit 3.0.0+**: Go is automatically installed if needed
- **Pre-commit earlier than 3.0.0**: You must have Go already installed on your system

## Language Support

Golang hooks are known to work on any system which has Go installed, and have been tested on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

## Hook Execution

The hook repository must contain Go source code, which will be installed via `go install ./...`. Pre-commit will create an isolated GOPATH for each hook and the entry should match an executable which will get installed into the GOPATH's bin directory.

So in summary: if you're using pre-commit 3.0.0 or later, Go will be installed automatically if needed. For earlier versions, you'll need Go pre-installed on your system.


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.
```

```
1	# DataQ backend image — serves both the FastAPI API and the Celery worker.
2	# Build context is the repo ROOT (not backend/) because the app imports as the
3	# top-level `backend.app.*` package and environment.yml lives at the root:
4	#   docker build -f backend/Dockerfile .
5	#
6	# Conda-only per CLAUDE.md (no venv/poetry). The dataq env is created from the
7	# pinned environment.yml and its bin dir is put first on PATH so `uvicorn`,
8	# `celery`, `alembic`, and `python` resolve to it without a `conda run` wrapper
9	# (which would interfere with signal forwarding to uvicorn/celery).
10	FROM continuumio/miniconda3:24.11.1-0
11	
12	WORKDIR /workspace
13	
14	# Create the conda env first and cache the layer — only re-runs when the pinned
15	# environment.yml changes, not on every code edit.
16	COPY environment.yml ./
17	RUN conda env create -f environment.yml && conda clean -afy
18	
19	ENV PATH=/opt/conda/envs/dataq/bin:$PATH \
20	    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
21	
22	# Application code + tooling config (pyproject is needed to run pytest/mypy in-container).
23	COPY pyproject.toml ./
24	COPY backend ./backend
25	
26	EXPOSE 8000
27	
28	# Default to the API; the worker service overrides `command` in compose.
29	CMD ["uvicorn", "backend.app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
30
```

Here's the full picture, cross-checked against the compose file, the Dockerfile, setup.sh, and the docs.

## ✅ Covered today — 4 services in [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml)

| Service | Image / build | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `postgres` | `postgres:16-alpine` | healthcheck + persistent `postgres_data` volume |
| `redis` | `redis:7-alpine` | healthcheck |
| `api` | `backend/Dockerfile` (conda `dataq`) | uvicorn `--reload`, source bind-mounted for hot reload, waits on pg/redis healthy |
| `worker` | same image | Celery worker, same deps/healthcheck gating |

The API and worker correctly share one image and override `command`. Service-to-service `DATABASE_URL`/`REDIS_URL` are wired to the in-network hostnames. This part is solid.

## ⚠️ Pending / missing

**1. Frontend (React/Vite) service — the real gap.** Every doc claims `docker compose up` starts a React dev server — [CLAUDE.md:196](CLAUDE.md#L196) ("…+ React + Celery worker"), [CONTRIBUTING.md:168](CONTRIBUTING.md#L168) ("React dev server"), and [setup.sh:82](scripts/setup.sh#L82) even prints `UI: http://localhost:3000`. But **there is no `frontend` service and no frontend Dockerfile.** Today the UI only runs via `cd frontend && pnpm dev` on the host (Vite is configured for port 3000 in [vite.config.ts:16](frontend/vite.config.ts#L16)). This is a docs-vs-reality drift.

**2. Migrations don't run on `compose up`.** `alembic upgrade head` only runs once inside [setup.sh:60](scripts/setup.sh#L60). There's no migration init-container or API entrypoint, so after you add a migration (or wipe the volume) and just `docker compose up`, the API boots against an un-migrated DB.

**3. Seed step is a no-op.** setup.sh guards on `backend/scripts/seed_dev.py`, which **doesn't exist** — so "seed dev data" silently skips.

**4. `SECRET_STORE=redis` not actually set.** It's only a comment in both services; default stays per-process `env`, so the cross-process secret sharing that Week-5 worker runs need (#86) isn't wired by default.

**5. Minor:** no `restart:` policies; no healthchecks on `api`/`worker` themselves (only pg/redis).

## Suggested plan

| # | Change | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add a `frontend` service: `node:20-alpine`, mount `./frontend`, `pnpm install && pnpm dev --host`, expose `3000:3000`, `depends_on: api`. (Dev-server container — a prod multi-stage build is a separate, later concern.) | S |
| 2 | Add a `migrate` init service (same backend image, `command: alembic upgrade head`, `depends_on: postgres healthy`) and make `api`/`worker` depend on it `condition: service_completed_successfully`. | S |
| 3 | Either create `backend/scripts/seed_dev.py` or drop the seed line + the `UI:3000` promise until the frontend service lands, so docs match reality. | S |
| 4 | Decide on #4: set `SECRET_STORE=redis` by default in compose, or leave as opt-in and document it. | XS |

Items 1–3 each map to a separate one-functionality PR per the working agreements.

One thing I'd flag before doing any of it: **#1 and #3 are doc drift that contradicts committed docs** — per the working agreement (defects → GitHub issue, no silent fixes), those should get an issue first. Note [#128](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/128) (full-stack E2E) is adjacent but not the same thing.

```
1	"""Idempotent seed for the Week 1 exit-gate probe.
2	
3	The probe endpoint runs a canned suite against a single seeded dev Snowflake
4	connection. Connection CRUD and suite/check authoring arrive in Weeks 2-3; until
5	then this get-or-creates the fixtures so the endpoint is safe to hit repeatedly.
6	
7	The canned check is column-agnostic (a row-count bound) so it works against any
8	configured table without assuming a schema.
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	from typing import Any
14	
15	from sqlalchemy import select
16	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
17	
18	from backend.app.core.config import Settings
19	from backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Suite, User
20	
21	PROBE_CONNECTION_NAME = "probe-snowflake-dev"
22	PROBE_SUITE_NAME = "probe-snowflake-suite"
23	PROBE_ENV = "dev"
24	
25	# (name, expectation_type, config) — kept column-agnostic for now.
26	_PROBE_CHECKS: tuple[tuple[str, str, dict[str, Any]], ...] = (
27	    ("row_count_positive", "expect_table_row_count_to_be_between", {"min_value": 1}),
28	)
29	
30	
31	def _connection_config(settings: Settings) -> dict[str, Any]:
32	    return {
33	        "account": settings.probe_snowflake_account,
34	        "user": settings.probe_snowflake_user,
35	        "database": settings.probe_snowflake_database,
36	        "schema": settings.probe_snowflake_schema,
37	        "warehouse": settings.probe_snowflake_warehouse,
38	        "role": settings.probe_snowflake_role,
39	    }
40	
41	
42	def ensure_probe_fixtures(
43	    session: Session, *, user: User, settings: Settings
44	) -> tuple[Connection, Suite, list[Check]]:
45	    """Get-or-create the probe Connection, Suite, and Checks. Idempotent."""
46	    connection = session.scalars(
47	        select(Connection).where(
48	            Connection.name == PROBE_CONNECTION_NAME, Connection.env == PROBE_ENV
49	        )
50	    ).first()
51	    if connection is None:
52	        connection = Connection(
53	            name=PROBE_CONNECTION_NAME,
54	            type="snowflake",
55	            env=PROBE_ENV,
56	            config=_connection_config(settings),
57	            secret_ref=settings.probe_snowflake_secret_ref,
58	            created_by=user.id,
59	        )
60	        session.add(connection)
61	        session.flush()  # populate connection.id for the suite FK
62	
63	    suite = session.scalars(
64	        select(Suite).where(Suite.name == PROBE_SUITE_NAME, Suite.connection_id == connection.id)
65	    ).first()
66	    if suite is None:
67	        suite = Suite(
68	            name=PROBE_SUITE_NAME,
69	            description="Week 1 exit-gate probe suite",
70	            connection_id=connection.id,
71	            created_by=user.id,
72	        )
73	        session.add(suite)
74	        session.flush()  # populate suite.id for the check FK
75	
76	    checks = list(session.scalars(select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == suite.id)))
77	    existing_names = {c.name for c in checks}
78	    for name, expectation_type, config in _PROBE_CHECKS:
79	        if name not in existing_names:
80	            check = Check(
81	                suite_id=suite.id,
82	                name=name,
83	                expectation_type=expectation_type,
84	                config=dict(config),
85	            )
86	            session.add(check)
87	            checks.append(check)
88	
89	    session.commit()
90	    return connection, suite, checks
91	
```

```json
  "content": "\"\"\"Idempotent dev-data seed (run by scripts/setup.sh, safe to re-run).\n\nGives a fresh local database a minimal baseline so the UI and API aren't empty\non first boot:\n\n- the **dev-bypass user** (the same fixed identity `auth_dev_bypass` resolves\n  every request to), so seeded rows are owned by the user you actually log in as\n  locally; and\n- the **probe Connection + Suite + Check**, reusing `ensure_probe_fixtures` so\n  the seed never drifts from what the Week-1 probe endpoint expects.\n\nBoth steps get-or-create, so running this repeatedly is a no-op. Run via:\n\n    conda run -n dataq python backend/scripts/seed_dev.py\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom backend.app.core.auth import (\n    DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID,\n    DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,\n    DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,\n    _upsert_user,\n)\nfrom backend.app.core.config import get_settings\nfrom backend.app.db.session import get_session\nfrom backend.app.services.probe import ensure_probe_fixtures\n\n\ndef seed() -> None:\n    settings = get_settings()\n    session = get_session()\n    try:\n        user = _upsert_user(\n            session,\n            aad_object_id=DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID,\n            email=DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,\n            display_name=DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,\n        )\n        connection, suite, checks = ensure_probe_fixtures(\n            session, user=user, settings=settings\n        )\n        print(\n            \"Seeded dev data: \"\n            f\"user={user.email} connection={connection.name} \"\n            f\"suite={suite.name} checks={len(checks)}\"\n        )\n    finally:\n        session.close()\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    seed()\n"
}
```

```
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+"""Idempotent dev-data seed (run by scripts/setup.sh, safe to re-run).
+
+Gives a fresh local database a minimal baseline so the UI and API aren't empty
+on first boot:
+
+- the **dev-bypass user** (the same fixed identity `auth_dev_bypass` resolves
+  every request to), so seeded rows are owned by the user you actually log in as
+  locally; and
+- the **probe Connection + Suite + Check**, reusing `ensure_probe_fixtures` so
+  the seed never drifts from what the Week-1 probe endpoint expects.
+
+Both steps get-or-create, so running this repeatedly is a no-op. Run via:
+
+    conda run -n dataq python backend/scripts/seed_dev.py
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from backend.app.core.auth import (
+    DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID,
+    DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,
+    DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,
+    _upsert_user,
+)
+from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
+from backend.app.db.session import get_session
+from backend.app.services.probe import ensure_probe_fixtures
+
+
+def seed() -> None:
+    settings = get_settings()
+    session = get_session()
+    try:
+        user = _upsert_user(
+            session,
+            aad_object_id=DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID,
+            email=DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,
+            display_name=DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,
+        )
+        connection, suite, checks = ensure_probe_fixtures(session, user=user, settings=settings)
+        print(
+            "Seeded dev data: "
+            f"user={user.email} connection={connection.name} "
+            f"suite={suite.name} checks={len(checks)}"
+        )
+    finally:
+        session.close()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    seed()
```

```
Bump snowflake-connector-python 3→4 (+ snowflake-sqlalchemy) to clear cryptography/pyopenssl CVEs

5 of the dependency CVEs surfaced by the full-runtime audit can't be fixed at the current Snowflake pins:

| `pyopenssl` 25.3.0 | CVE-2026-27448, CVE-2026-27459 | ≥26.0.0 — but `snowflake-connector-python 3.15.0` requires `pyOpenSSL<26.0.0` |

===== #122 =====
Add operational result statuses: skip + error (additive CHECK widening)
## Context
The Week-3 schema seam ([#121](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/121)) retargeted `results.status` to ADR 0005's **severity tiers** — `pass / warn / fail / critical` — and deliberately **dropped the previously-unused `skipped`** value (it was never emitted by the run path).

That decision was explicitly made on the basis that adding operational states back later is a **cheap, additive `CHECK` widening** — the opposite of the expensive tier-*narrowing* ADR 0005 front-loaded. This issue tracks doing exactly that when the run path needs them.

Add two **operational**

===== #124 =====
Add DQ-dimension classification to checks (Completeness/Uniqueness/Validity/…)
## Context
Checks currently have **two** classification axes, neither of which is a data-quality *dimension*:

| Field | Axis | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | *how* the monitor works (ADR 0012) | `expectation` / `freshness` / `comparison` |
| `expectation_type` | the specific GX rule | `expect_column_values_to_be_unique` |

A **DQ dimension** (Completeness, Uniqueness, Validity, Accuracy, Consistency, Timeliness) is a third axis — the *semantic category* of what quality aspect a check measures. It powers dimension-rollup dashboards ("98% complete, 99.5% unique, 95% valid…"), which are a st

===== #92 =====
Surface the ADF webhook URL instead of hand-assembling a secret-bearing URL
## Context

The ADF webhook receiver landed in #91 (`POST /api/v1/orchestration/events/adf`, auth + `pipeline_runs` upsert). It only defines the **path** — nothing in the codebase emits the full URL that Azure Monitor must POST to:

```
https://<deployed-api-host>/api/v1/orchestration/events/adf?token=<ADF_WEBHOOK_SECRET>
```

Per [ADR 0006](docs/adr/0006-adf-webhook-authentication.md) the shared secret rides the URL as a `token` query param. Today an operator assembles this by hand during the Week-7 "Azure Monitor webhook setup" tasks (see [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md)): take the Conta
```

```json
{
  "command": "gh issue create --title \"Backend Docker image fails to build: requirements copied after conda env create\" --label \"bug\" --label \"priority/P0\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Problem\n\n\\`docker compose build\\` (api / worker / the new migrate service) **fails**:\n\n```\nERROR: Could not open requirements file: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:\n  '/workspace/backend/requirements-dev.txt'\nCondaEnvException: Pip failed\n```\n\n[backend/Dockerfile](../blob/main/backend/Dockerfile) copies only \\`environment.yml\\` (L16) and runs \\`conda env create\\` (L17) **before** \\`COPY backend ./backend\\` (L24). But \\`environment.yml\\`'s pip section does \\`-r backend/requirements-dev.txt\\` (which itself \\`-r\\`'s requirements.txt / -typecheck / -tooling), so the requirements files don't exist yet at env-create time.\n\n## Impact\n\nThe backend image has **never been buildable via the Dockerfile**, so the entire `docker compose up` stack (api + worker) is broken — only `postgres`/`redis` (prebuilt images) come up. Live container runs were a deferred smoke, so this went unnoticed.\n\n## Fix\n\nCopy the requirements files **before** the conda step, scoped so the env-create layer cache only busts on a pin change (not on every code edit):\n\n```dockerfile\nCOPY environment.yml ./\nCOPY backend/requirements*.txt ./backend/\nRUN conda env create -f environment.yml && conda clean -afy\n```\n\n## Found\n\nWhile testing the #156 migrate init-container — it can't build the shared image. Blocks #156 and any container-based run.\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -1",

}
```

- `restart: "no"` is quoted (avoids the YAML `no`→`false` boolean trap) and correct for a one-shot.

```
## Python 3.13 Support in Version 3.15

Version 3.15 added support for Python 3.13, and added Windows support for Python 3.13.

## Version 4 and Python 3.13 Support

Version 4 of the connector has also been released with Python 3.13 support. The search results show that version 4.5.0 includes wheels for Python 3.13 (cp313), confirming that the latest major version supports Python 3.13.

## Additional Context

Version 3.14.1 added support for Python 3.13, so Python 3.13 support became available starting with version 3.14.1 in the 3.x line and continues through version 4.x.
```

> AGENT

## Python upgrade assessment

I checked our pinned deps against 3.13 and 3.14. The verdict is clear:

**→ 3.13 is green. 3.14 is blocked by our own core engine.**

| Dependency | 3.13 | 3.14 |
|---|---|---|
| **great-expectations 1.17** (pinned core engine) | ✅ 3.10–3.13 | ⚠️ **experimental only** (behind `GX_PYTHON_EXPERIMENTAL`) |
| snowflake-connector-python 3.15 (and 4.x for #129) | ✅ (since 3.14.1) | likely, unverified |
| databricks-sql-connector 3.7 | ✅ | ✅ |
| fastapi / sqlalchemy / pydantic / celery / pandas / pyarrow / boto3 / azure-* | ✅ | mostly, with lag |

**3.14 is a non-starter while we pin GX** — GX Core only supports it experimentally, and CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids tracking GX loosely (its v1 API drifts). So the real choice is **3.13 or stay on 3.11**.

**On urgency:** 3.11 isn't as close to EOL as it feels — security support runs to **Oct 2027**. So there's no fire, but 3.13 is mature (released Oct 2024) and the move is low-risk and gets us off the EOL clock early.

**What it touches** (it's a locked Week-1 decision, so it needs an ADR):
- `environment.yml` (`python=3.11→3.13`), `pyproject.toml` (Black/Ruff `target-version` ×2), `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (mypy `language_version`), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (×5 `python-version`), plus `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `CLAUDE.md` text and the "do not drift" lock note.
- A new ADR superseding the W1 Python-3.11 lock.
- **The real risk/test:** a full conda env rebuild on 3.13 — to confirm every *transitive* dep has 3.13 wheels. That's the gate I'd run before committing.

**My recommendation:** target **3.13**, and **fold it together with #129** (the Snowflake 3→4 CVE bump) into one "dependency refresh" effort — both require a full env rebuild + revalidation, so doing them together pays that cost once instead of twice.

How do you want to sequence it?

> AGENT

Checked — and the good news first: **no real secret leaked.** Here's the assessment.

## What GitGuardian flagged

The "Generic Password" is the dev Postgres credential **`dataq:dataq`** in connection strings. The push at 20:31 UTC was the squash-merge of PR #160 (683af13), whose new `migrate` service added another `DATABASE_URL` line. The literal `dataq:dataq` lives in:

| Location | What it is |
|---|---|
| `backend/app/core/config.py:19` | Pydantic Settings **default** (literal — the most likely trigger) |
| `.env.example:9` | template placeholder |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml:158-159` | CI's ephemeral **test** DB |
| `docker-compose.yml` (×3) | uses `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-dataq}` env-override form |
| `docs/progress.md:254` | already a TODO: "override hardcoded `dataq:dataq` creds via Container Apps secret refs" |

## Severity: false positive (real-risk ≈ zero)

- `dataq` is a **throwaway local-dev password** for the docker-compose stack and CI's disposable test DB. **Not a production credential** — prod gets `DATABASE_URL` from env / Key Vault.
- It's already overridable via `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}`, and the deploy-time override is **already tracked** (progress.md:254).
- I scanned the recent pushes for *real* secrets — no AWS keys, private keys, tokens, or JWTs — and confirmed **`.env` is gitignored and untracked.**

## Why our own scanners didn't block it

betterleaks (CI) and the GitHub push protection I enabled today both passed because `dataq` is low-entropy and a well-known dev default — those tools suppress it to avoid noise. GitGuardian's "Generic Password" heuristic is more aggressive on `user:pass@host` patterns. So this is a detector-sensitivity difference, not a missed real secret.

## Recommendation

**Mark it "False Positive" in GitGuardian** (the button in your email) — that's the honest classification. **No rotation needed.** I would *not* `git push --no-verify` anything or rewrite history over a dev default.

Optionally, I can reduce future scanner noise. How do you want to proceed?

```
VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID=
```
