  "content": "\"\"\"Unit tests for run_target.resolve_target / validate_target (#215).\n\nPure functions — no DB, no datasource. Covers each datasource's required field,\nthe targetless / wrong-datasource error paths, and that a flat-file path rides\nthe runner's `table` slot (the table-shaped CheckRunner contract).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom backend.app.services.run_target import (\n    SuiteTargetInvalidError,\n    resolve_target,\n    validate_target,\n)\n\n\ndef test_snowflake_resolves_table_and_optional_schema() -> None:\n    r = resolve_target(\"snowflake\", {\"table\": \"ORDERS\", \"schema\": \"SALES\"})\n    assert (r.table, r.schema, r.catalog) == (\"ORDERS\", \"SALES\", None)\n\n\ndef test_snowflake_schema_optional() -> None:\n    r = resolve_target(\"snowflake\", {\"table\": \"ORDERS\"})\n    assert (r.table, r.schema, r.catalog) == (\"ORDERS\", None, None)\n\n\ndef test_unity_catalog_requires_catalog_and_table() -> None:\n    r = resolve_target(\"unity_catalog\", {\"catalog\": \"main\", \"schema\": \"sales\", \"table\": \"orders\"})\n    assert (r.table, r.schema, r.catalog) == (\"orders\", \"sales\", \"main\")\n\n\ndef test_unity_catalog_missing_catalog_raises() -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(SuiteTargetInvalidError):\n        resolve_target(\"unity_catalog\", {\"table\": \"orders\"})\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"conn_type\", [\"adls_gen2\", \"s3\"])\ndef test_flatfile_path_rides_table_slot(conn_type: str) -> None:\n    # The CheckRunner interface is table-shaped; the file path is the `table`.\n    r = resolve_target(conn_type, {\"path\": \"data/orders.csv\"})\n    assert (r.table, r.schema, r.catalog) == (\"data/orders.csv\", None, None)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"conn_type\", [\"adls_gen2\", \"s3\"])\ndef test_flatfile_missing_path_raises(conn_type: str) -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(SuiteTargetInvalidError):\n        resolve_target(conn_type, {\"table\": \"orders\"})  # SQL field, wrong datasource\n\n\ndef test_snowflake_missing_table_raises() -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(SuiteTargetInvalidError):\n        resolve_target(\"snowflake\", {\"schema\": \"SALES\"})\n\n\ndef test_blank_table_is_rejected() -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(SuiteTargetInvalidError):\n        resolve_target(\"snowflake\", {\"table\": \"   \"})\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"target\", [None, {}])\ndef test_targetless_suite_raises(target: dict[str, str] | None) -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(SuiteTargetInvalidError):\n        resolve_target(\"snowflake\", target)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"conn_type\", [\"adf\", \"airflow\"])\ndef test_orchestration_types_have_no_run_path(conn_type: str) -> None:\n    # ADF / Airflow are orchestration providers, never suite datasources.\n    with pytest.raises(SuiteTargetInvalidError):\n        resolve_target(conn_type, {\"table\": \"x\"})\n\n\ndef test_validate_target_is_resolve_without_return() -> None:\n    validate_target(\"snowflake\", {\"table\": \"ORDERS\"})  # no raise\n    with pytest.raises(SuiteTargetInvalidError):\n        validate_target(\"snowflake\", {\"schema\": \"SALES\"})\n"
}

106:**Week 2 total: 15 / 19** _(ADF webhook receiver: endpoint+auth, payload parse, secret config, REST `fetch_run_detail` enrichment; upsert+correlate 🟡 — trigger-on-success skeleton landed, run_suite dispatch gated to Week 3; polling → Week 5. **Airflow group complete (3/3)** — HMAC receiver + connection adapter + DAG callback snippet, so the producer↔receiver loop is closed end-to-end. Remaining W2 tail: connection re-auth endpoint + `secret_ref` nullability note; the rest are Week-3/5 GX run-path tasks)_
118:- [x] ✅ API: check dry-run endpoint — validate against live data, return preview result — `POST /suites/{id}/checks/dryrun` (`dryrun_service`): runs **one ad-hoc check** against the suite's connection synchronously and returns a preview (severity `status` + `metric_value` + sanitized `observed/expected`) **without persisting** any Run/Result. Reuses the severity derivation (ADR 0005/0016) + JSON sanitiser. `require_permission` **edit** (authoring); table passed in the body (checks don't carry a target table yet). v1 → 422: non-`expectation` kind, non-Snowflake connection (runner dispatch generalises Week 5); execution failure → 502 (adapter exception never echoed). No `sample_failures` in the preview (PII; follow-up). 7 TestClient tests (mocked runner); `dryrun_service` + `checks.py` 100%
124:- [x] ✅ Post-processing in GX result handler — derive `warn` / `fail` / `critical` from observed value (PR-C) — `services/severity.py` (`extract_metric` + `derive_status`), wired into `run_service._build_result`. Thresholds band the GX **unexpected-%** as `metric_value` (higher=worse, ordered, unset-tier skipped); thresholds-as-policy override GX `success`; binary fallback when no thresholds / no metric. **Settled in [ADR 0016](adr/0016-severity-derivation-semantics.md)** (incl. A→B reversibility: raw `observed_value` retained → switch is additive `direction` column + backfill, never destructive). `duration_ms` stays NULL (per-check timing not separable from GX's suite-level `validate()`). 16 unit + 1 integration test; both modules 100%
125:- [x] ✅ Update check CRUD + run result response schemas with threshold fields + status values — check-CRUD thresholds (PR-B2) + result response now carries `status` (`pass`/`warn`/`fail`/`critical`) + `metric_value` (probe `CheckResultResponse`, PR-C)
134:- [x] ✅ Column profiler endpoint (Snowflake) — nulls, distinct count, min / max, top values — `profile_service` + `POST /suites/{id}/profile` (require_permission **edit**, suite-scoped so the connection is access-gated). Reads-only, persists nothing: one aggregate query (row count + null/distinct/min/max per column) + one top-N-values query per column, then `assemble_profile`. **SQL-injection-safe** — queries are built with the **SQLAlchemy Core expression language** (`select`/`table`/`column`, dialect-quoted) so there's no raw-string SQL sink (no S608/B608/CodeQL `py/sql-injection`); identifiers are additionally allowlist-validated (`validate_identifier`, strict `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$`) as defence-in-depth + a clean early 422, and `top_n` is `int()`-coerced. v1 → 422: non-Snowflake type (dispatch generalises Week 5), bad identifier, no schema; execution failure → 502 (adapter exception never echoed). min/max/top-values NaN-sanitised. 28 tests (22 pure: identifier allowlist incl. injection strings, compiled-SQL builders, assembly, div-by-zero, NaN; 6 endpoint via fake conn: stats, injection-422, unsupported-type-422, 502, edit-gated, no-schema-422); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 90% (live `_open_connection` is the deferred warehouse seam)
143:- [x] ✅ UC table check path — UC table → GX DataFrame datasource → run suite — `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` (`datasources/unity_catalog.py`): reads the target table from the Databricks SQL Warehouse into a pandas DataFrame (`pd.read_sql_table` via the databricks SQLAlchemy dialect — reflection quotes identifiers, so no hand-built SQL) and runs the suite's GX expectations against GX's **pandas DataFrame asset** — the "GX DataFrame datasource" shape (§5), the same shape Databricks Labs DQX consumes, so v1.1 swaps GX→DQX behind this one interface. Reuses the shared `gx_runner` (`run_expectations` + result mapping) exactly like the flat-file runner; the `catalog` is pinned in the connection URL (`build_databricks_url`, now shared with the column profiler — no duplication) so the 2-level `schema.table` resolves to `catalog.schema.table`. Because GX runs **in-process on the DataFrame**, the run path is unit-tested with a canned frame (real GX execution); only the reflect+read (`_read_table`) is the deferred-smoke seam. `build_unity_catalog_runner` mirrors `build_snowflake_runner` (raw config + resolved PAT, not the ORM). 14 tests; `unity_catalog` 91% (only `_read_table` uncovered). _Connection-type → runner dispatch is the Week-5 `run_suite` wiring._

I now have a thorough understanding. Let me finalize my candidate findings. The strongest concrete ones:

1. **`update_suite` cannot clear a target** — `target=None` means "unchanged". A suite with a wrong/stale target can never be reset to NULL via PATCH. Concrete but documented as intentional.

2. **`_trigger_suites` orphans runs on crash** between commit (line 219) and `delay` — and the docstring explicitly says poll won't re-dispatch. Pre-existing seam but newly load-bearing now that dispatch is ungated.

3. **`SuiteTarget` accepts conflicting/mixed fields** (both `table` and `path`), and `resolve_target` silently ignores the wrong-datasource field — e.g. a snowflake suite with `{"table":"T","path":"x.csv"}` is accepted, path silently dropped.

4. **Migration has no `server_default`** — fine since nullable. Not a bug.

Let me check one more concrete issue: in `_trigger_suites`, the broker-failure `except Exception` calls `session.commit()` but does NOT `session.refresh(run)` — actually runs were refreshed at 221. The bigger issue: if `delay` raises, the exception could leave `run.status="failed"` but the *first* successful delays already happened — those runs are correctly queued. No corruption.

Let me reconsider the **most defensible real bug**: the autouse `stub_run_dispatch` fixture stubs `tasks.run_suite.delay` with `lambda run_id:`. But `_trigger_suites` does a *lazy import* `from backend.app.worker.tasks import run_suite`. Since it imports the same module object `tasks.run_suite`, the monkeypatch on the attribute holds. Good — no test bug.

Final concrete bug worth flagging: **probe `target` overwrites a manually-set target on every call.** `ensure_probe_fixtures` sets `suite.target = target` unconditionally (line 83), so if `probe_snowflake_table` is unset, it resets a previously-runnable probe suite's target back to NULL every call. Concrete regression.

1	"""Celery application for DataQ's async execution backbone.
2	
3	GX suite runs are dispatched from FastAPI and executed here so the request
4	thread returns immediately (run created as ``queued``, worker drives it to
5	``running`` → ``succeeded``/``failed``).
6	
7	The CLAUDE.md observability rule requires ``request_id`` correlation to flow
8	FastAPI → Celery → GX. We carry it on the task message headers: the caller
9	injects the active request_id on publish, and the worker restores it into the
10	same ``request_id_var`` ContextVar the structlog processor chain reads from, so
11	worker log lines correlate with the request that triggered them.
12	"""
13	
14	from typing import Any
15	
16	from celery import Celery
17	from celery.signals import (
18	    before_task_publish,
19	    setup_logging,
20	    task_postrun,
21	    task_prerun,
22	)
23	
24	from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
25	from backend.app.core.logging import configure_logging, request_id_var
26	
27	# Message-header key carrying the originating request_id across the broker.
28	REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "request_id"
29	# Attribute on task.request where prerun stashes the ContextVar reset handle
30	# for postrun. Deliberately avoids the word "token" so it isn't mistaken for a
31	# secret by Bandit / Ruff (B105 / S105).
32	_REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR = "_dataq_request_id_reset"
33	
34	
35	def create_celery_app() -> Celery:
36	    settings = get_settings()
37	    app = Celery(
38	        "dataq",
39	        broker=settings.redis_url,
40	        backend=settings.redis_url,
41	    )
42	    app.conf.update(
43	        task_serializer="json",
44	        result_serializer="json",
45	        accept_content=["json"],
46	        timezone="UTC",
47	        enable_utc=True,
48	        # Surface a 'started' state so the run-status read-back can distinguish
49	        # queued from running without waiting for completion.
50	        task_track_started=True,
51	        # Celery-beat schedule. The orchestration polling fallback (#171) runs
52	        # every 10 min as the success channel for runs that produced no webhook;
53	        # the task looks back further than the interval so nothing slips the gap.
54	        # Beat runs embedded in the dev worker (`worker -B`); prod uses a separate
55	        # beat process.
56	        beat_schedule={
57	            "poll-orchestration-runs": {
58	                "task": "poll_orchestration_runs",
59	                "schedule": 600.0,  # 10 minutes
60	            },
61	        },
62	    )
63	    # Register task modules on worker boot (looks for backend.app.worker.tasks).
64	    app.autodiscover_tasks(["backend.app.worker"])
65	    return app
66	
67	
68	celery_app = create_celery_app()
69	
70	
71	@setup_logging.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
72	def _configure_celery_logging(**_kwargs: Any) -> None:
73	    """Disable Celery's default logging and route worker logs through structlog.
74	
75	    Connecting any receiver to ``setup_logging`` tells Celery not to configure
76	    logging itself, so our JSON + PII-redacting processor chain stays in force
77	    inside the worker exactly as it is in the API.
78	    """
79	    configure_logging()
80	
81	
82	@before_task_publish.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
83	def _inject_request_id(headers: dict[str, Any] | None = None, **_kwargs: Any) -> None:
84	    """Caller side (FastAPI): stamp the active request_id onto task headers."""
85	    if headers is None:
86	        return
87	    rid = request_id_var.get()
88	    if rid is not None:
89	        headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = rid
90	
91	
92	@task_prerun.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
93	def _restore_request_id(task: Any = None, **_kwargs: Any) -> None:
94	    """Worker side: restore request_id from the message into the ContextVar.
95	
96	    Custom headers added in ``before_task_publish`` are exposed as attributes on
97	    ``task.request`` under the protocol-v2 message format. We stash the reset
98	    token on ``task.request`` so ``task_postrun`` can restore the *prior* value
99	    rather than blindly clearing — under ``task_always_eager`` these signals run
100	    in the caller's context, so a blanket reset would drop the request_id for
101	    the rest of the request handler.
102	    """
103	    rid = getattr(task.request, REQUEST_ID_HEADER, None) if task is not None else None
104	    if rid and task is not None:
105	        token = request_id_var.set(rid)
106	        setattr(task.request, _REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR, token)
107	
108	
109	@task_postrun.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
110	def _clear_request_id(task: Any = None, **_kwargs: Any) -> None:
111	    """Worker side: restore the ContextVar to its pre-task value.
112	
113	    Only resets when ``task_prerun`` actually set it (token present), mirroring
114	    the ``reset(token)`` pattern used by ``request_id_middleware`` in main.py.
115	    """
116	    token = getattr(task.request, _REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR, None) if task is not None else None
117	    if token is not None:
118	        request_id_var.reset(token)
119

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/services/run_dispatch.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Dispatch a persisted `Run` to the Celery worker — the one place that publishes.\n\nPublishes ``run_suite`` **by name** via ``celery_app.send_task`` rather than\nimporting the task object. That decoupling is deliberate: ``worker.tasks``\nimports service modules (e.g. ``orchestration_service``), so a service importing\n``worker.tasks`` back would be a cyclic import (CodeQL `py/cyclic-import`). By\nname there is no import edge service → worker, and the broker resolves the task\non the worker side. The ``before_task_publish`` signal still fires, so the\n``request_id`` correlation header is carried exactly as for ``.delay``.\n\nRaises on a broker/publish failure; the caller owns the policy for a stuck run\n(the probe endpoint surfaces 503; the pipeline-trigger path marks the run\n``failed`` so it isn't left ``queued``).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport uuid\n\nfrom backend.app.worker.celery_app import celery_app\n\n_RUN_SUITE_TASK = \"run_suite\"\n\n\ndef dispatch_run(run_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Publish the ``run_suite`` task for ``run_id``. Raises if the broker is down.\"\"\"\n    celery_app.send_task(_RUN_SUITE_TASK, args=[str(run_id)])\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Unit test for run_dispatch.dispatch_run — publishes run_suite by name.\n\nNo broker: celery_app.send_task is spied. Asserts the task is published by its\nregistered name with the run id as the sole arg, and that a publish failure\npropagates (callers own the stuck-run policy).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport uuid\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom backend.app.services import run_dispatch\n\n\ndef test_dispatch_run_sends_task_by_name(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    calls: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []\n    monkeypatch.setattr(\n        run_dispatch.celery_app,\n        \"send_task\",\n        lambda name, args: calls.append((name, args)),\n    )\n    run_id = uuid.uuid4()\n\n    run_dispatch.dispatch_run(run_id)\n\n    # Published by registered name (decoupled from worker.tasks — no import edge),\n    # with the run id stringified for JSON serialisation.\n    assert calls == [(\"run_suite\", [str(run_id)])]\n\n\ndef test_dispatch_run_propagates_broker_failure(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    def _boom(name: str, args: Any) -> None:\n        raise RuntimeError(\"broker unreachable\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(run_dispatch.celery_app, \"send_task\", _boom)\n\n    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):\n        run_dispatch.dispatch_run(uuid.uuid4())\n"

> AGENT

Confirmed RCA: the 503 hit PyPI's `/pypi/.../json` metadata endpoint that pip-audit uses to resolve the requirements file — so it aborts regardless of vulnerability service, and the CI step has **no retry**, making the CVE gate flaky on any transient PyPI/OSV 5xx.

The proper fix (not a bypass): wrap the audit in a bounded retry with backoff. This is safe — a *real* CVE fails every attempt and still blocks the merge; only transient service errors are absorbed.

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01RzSE6VexjfNgtFqqtwpeot
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/.github/workflows/ci.yml",
  "old_string": "      - name: pip-audit (full runtime + test surface)\n        # Synchronous CVE gate over the entire runtime + test dependency tree\n        # (single source: requirements-dev.txt) + transitive deps, against the\n        # PyPI/OSV advisory DB. Complements the Dependabot alerts (full graph,\n        # async) with a fail-fast merge check.\n        #\n        # The 5 ignored advisories are cryptography + pyOpenSSL CVEs blocked by\n        # snowflake-connector-python<4 / snowflake-sqlalchemy<4 — a deliberate\n        # major datasource bump tracked in #129 (the deadline for removing these).\n        run: |\n          pip-audit -r backend/requirements-dev.txt \\\n            --ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-36 \\\n            --ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-35 \\\n            --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-26007 \\\n            --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-27448 \\\n            --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-27459",
  "new_string": "      - name: pip-audit (full runtime + test surface)\n        # Synchronous CVE gate over the entire runtime + test dependency tree\n        # (single source: requirements-dev.txt) + transitive deps, against the\n        # PyPI/OSV advisory DB. Complements the Dependabot alerts (full graph,\n        # async) with a fail-fast merge check.\n        #\n        # The 5 ignored advisories are cryptography + pyOpenSSL CVEs blocked by\n        # snowflake-connector-python<4 / snowflake-sqlalchemy<4 — a deliberate\n        # major datasource bump tracked in #129 (the deadline for removing these).\n        #\n        # Bounded retry: pip-audit resolves the requirements file via PyPI's\n        # per-package JSON endpoint, so a single transient PyPI/OSV 5xx (e.g.\n        # \"503 Backend is unhealthy\") aborts the whole audit and flakes the gate.\n        # Retrying with backoff absorbs that *without* masking real findings — a\n        # genuine CVE fails every attempt and still blocks (90s worst-case backoff).\n        run: |\n          audit() {\n            pip-audit -r backend/requirements-dev.txt \\\n              --ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-36 \\\n              --ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-35 \\\n              --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-26007 \\\n              --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-27448 \\\n              --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-27459\n          }\n          for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do\n            if audit; then\n              exit 0\n            fi\n            if [ \"$attempt\" -lt 4 ]; then\n              echo \"::warning::pip-audit attempt $attempt failed (likely a transient PyPI/OSV 5xx) — retrying in $((attempt * 15))s\"\n              sleep $((attempt * 15))\n            fi\n          done\n          echo \"::error::pip-audit failed after 4 attempts — a real CVE or a persistent PyPI/OSV outage (see log above)\"\n          exit 1"
}

- **Per-suite run target** — `Suite.target` (datasource-shaped JSONB), resolved per connection type by `run_target.resolve_target` to the runner's `(table, schema, catalog)`. Migration `b1f2c3d4e5a6`, tested up/down.
- **Dispatch ungated** — pipeline-success now actually fires `run_suite`; the worker resolves the target from the suite (targetless → clean `failed`).

**Three issues hit along the way — each RCA'd and fixed properly, none bypassed:**

1. **CodeQL cyclic import** (blocked merge via the review-thread-resolution ruleset). My lazy import only dodged the runtime error. Fixed at the right depth: extracted `run_dispatch.dispatch_run` that publishes by task *name* via `celery_app.send_task`, eliminating the service→worker import edge. This also collapsed the duplicated broker-failure dispatch pattern the review flagged. Both CodeQL threads auto-resolved on the clean commit.

2. **pip-audit failure** — RCA: transient PyPI `503 Backend is unhealthy` on the metadata endpoint pip-audit uses to resolve the requirements file; a single 5xx aborted the whole audit because the step had no retry. Fixed with bounded retry+backoff that absorbs transient 5xx **without masking real CVEs** (a genuine finding fails all 4 attempts and still blocks). Logic unit-tested.

3. **Dev-DB drift** (caught during cleanup) — the local `dataq` DB had only `alembic_version` stamped at head with zero real tables, so the compose `migrate` step was a silent no-op. Reconciled with `stamp base` → `upgrade head` → reseed; verified `suites.target` present and seed runs clean.

**Verification:** 558 backend tests pass; black/ruff/mypy/bandit clean; multi-agent review (7 angles) run with 2 findings fixed in-PR; all 14 CI checks green before squash-merge.

PR-C0b (run-trigger + `runs.py` read endpoints) and PR-C1 (Results page + ADR 0018) remain **not started** — ready when you are. Note: the shared `dispatch_run` helper that PR-C0b needed already exists now, so that part's done.

import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path';

const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));

// Proxy target for /api and /mcp. Defaults to localhost:8000 for host-side dev
// (`pnpm dev`); the docker-compose frontend service overrides it to the in-network
// api hostname (http://api:8000), since `localhost` inside the container is the
// frontend container itself.
const apiProxyTarget = process.env.VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET || 'http://localhost:8000';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  resolve: {
    alias: {
      '@': resolve(__dirname, 'src'),
    },
  },
  server: {
    port: 3000,
    proxy: {
      '/api': apiProxyTarget,
      '/mcp': apiProxyTarget,
    },
  },
  build: {
    rollupOptions: {
      output: {
        // Split the heavy, rarely-changing vendors into their own long-cache
        // chunks so the app chunk stays small and an app change doesn't bust the
        // whole vendor bundle. Routes are additionally lazy-split (App.tsx).
        manualChunks(id: string) {
          if (!id.includes('node_modules')) return undefined;
          if (id.includes('/antd/') || id.includes('@ant-design/')) return 'antd';
          if (id.includes('@azure/')) return 'msal';
          if (
            id.includes('/react/') ||
            id.includes('/react-dom/') ||
            id.includes('/react-router') ||
            id.includes('/scheduler/')
          ) {
            return 'react';
          }
          return 'vendor';
        },
      },
    },
  },
  test: {
    globals: true,
    environment: 'jsdom',
    setupFiles: ['./tests/setup.ts'],
    coverage: {
      provider: 'v8',
      reporter: ['text', 'lcov'],
      thresholds: {
        lines: 0, // raised to 80 in Week 8
      },
    },
  },
});

import '@testing-library/jest-dom';

// antd's responsive components (Descriptions, Card, …) call window.matchMedia,
// which jsdom does not implement. Provide a no-op stub so they render in tests.
if (!window.matchMedia) {
  window.matchMedia = (query: string): MediaQueryList =>
    ({
      matches: false,
      media: query,
      onchange: null,
      addListener: () => {},
      removeListener: () => {},
      addEventListener: () => {},
      removeEventListener: () => {},
      dispatchEvent: () => false,
    }) as MediaQueryList;
}

// antd's Select/virtual-list (rc-virtual-list) uses ResizeObserver, absent in
// jsdom. A no-op stub lets dropdown options render in tests.
if (!window.ResizeObserver) {
  window.ResizeObserver = class {
    observe(): void {}
    unobserve(): void {}
    disconnect(): void {}
  };
}

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # ── Backend ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  backend-lint:
    name: Backend — lint & format
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install lint tools
        run: pip install -r backend/requirements-tooling.txt

      - name: Black (format check)
        run: black --check backend/

      - name: Ruff (lint)
        run: ruff check backend/

      - name: Typecheck-deps in sync
        # Guard the pre-commit mypy hook against backend/requirements-typecheck.txt
        # (Dependabot bumps the requirements file but bypasses the local hook —
        # this catches the drift in CI, which previously slipped through).
        run: python scripts/check-typecheck-deps.py

  backend-types:
    name: Backend — type check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install type-check deps
        # mypy from the tooling file; the typed subset it checks against.
        run: |
          pip install -r backend/requirements-tooling.txt
          pip install -r backend/requirements-typecheck.txt

      - name: mypy
        run: mypy backend/app/

  backend-sast:
    name: Backend — SAST (Bandit)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install Bandit
        run: pip install -r backend/requirements-tooling.txt

      - name: Bandit
        run: bandit -c pyproject.toml -r backend/app/

  backend-audit:
    name: Backend — dependency audit (pip-audit)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install pip-audit
        run: pip install pip-audit==2.10.0

      - name: pip-audit (full runtime + test surface)
        # Synchronous CVE gate over the entire runtime + test dependency tree
        # (single source: requirements-dev.txt) + transitive deps, against the
        # PyPI/OSV advisory DB. Complements the Dependabot alerts (full graph,
        # async) with a fail-fast merge check.
        #
        # The 5 ignored advisories are cryptography + pyOpenSSL CVEs blocked by
        # snowflake-connector-python<4 / snowflake-sqlalchemy<4 — a deliberate
        # major datasource bump tracked in #129 (the deadline for removing these).
        run: |
          pip-audit -r backend/requirements-dev.txt \
            --ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-36 \
            --ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-35 \
            --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-26007 \
            --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-27448 \
            --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-27459

  backend-test:
    name: Backend — tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ephemeral Postgres for DB-backed integration tests (seed/run/endpoint).
    # Matches the compose image; gen_random_uuid() is built in to PG16.
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: dataq
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: dataq
          POSTGRES_DB: dataq_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U dataq"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 10
      # Redis broker for the real-broker E2E (dispatch -> worker round-trip).
      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install test deps
        # Single source of truth: runtime + typed subset + test toolchain, all
        # from backend/requirements-dev.txt. pip upgraded for PYSEC-2026-196.
        run: |
          python -m pip install -U pip
          pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt

      - name: pytest
        # TEST_DATABASE_URL enables the db_session fixture; DATABASE_URL + REDIS_URL
        # enable the real-broker E2E. All DB/broker tests skip when unset (e.g. a
        # contributor running pytest without the services).
        env:
          TEST_DATABASE_URL: REDACTED
          DATABASE_URL: REDACTED
          REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0
        run: pytest backend/tests/

  # ── Secret scanning ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  secrets:
    name: Secret scanning (betterleaks)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # Betterleaks has no official GitHub Action; run the official pinned
      # container image. Drop-in gitleaks replacement: nonzero exit on findings
      # fails the job. safe.directory env is required because the container runs
      # as root while checkout writes files as the runner user — without it git
      # aborts with "detected dubious ownership".
      - name: Run betterleaks
        run: |
          docker run --rm \
            -e GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
            -e GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.directory \
            -e GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/repo \
            -v "$PWD:/repo" -w /repo \
            ghcr.io/betterleaks/betterleaks:v1.4.1 \
            git /repo --redact --verbose

  # ── Frontend ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  frontend-lint:
    name: Frontend — lint & format
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
        with:
          version: 9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "20"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Prettier (format check)
        run: pnpm format:check

      - name: ESLint
        run: pnpm lint

      - name: TypeScript
        run: pnpm typecheck

  frontend-test:
    name: Frontend — tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
        with:
          version: 9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "20"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Vitest
        run: pnpm test

  frontend-audit:
    name: Frontend — dependency audit (pnpm audit)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
        with:
          version: 9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "20"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: pnpm audit (high+)
        # Fails on high/critical advisories in the dependency tree; lower
        # severities are reported but don't block (avoid noise from unfixable
        # transitive dev-tool advisories). Pairs with Dependabot alerts (async).
        run: pnpm audit --audit-level=high

  # ── CodeQL SAST ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  codeql:
    name: CodeQL analysis
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      security-events: write
      actions: read
      contents: read
    strategy:
      matrix:
        language: [python, javascript-typescript]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
        with:
          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
          config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml

      - uses: github/codeql-action/autobuild@v4

      - uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4
```

import { Button, Flex, Layout, Menu, Spin, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';
import { lazy, Suspense } from 'react';
import { Link, Navigate, Route, Routes, useLocation } from 'react-router-dom';

import { AuthGate } from './auth/AuthGate';
import { authMode } from './auth/config';
import { useCurrentUser } from './auth/useCurrentUser';
import { getMsalInstance } from './auth/msalInstance';

// Route components are code-split so the initial bundle doesn't ship every page
// (and antd-heavy pages only load on navigation). Named exports → map to default.
const Connections = lazy(() =>
  import('./pages/Connections').then((m) => ({ default: m.Connections })),
);
const Suites = lazy(() => import('./pages/Suites').then((m) => ({ default: m.Suites })));
const Home = lazy(() => import('./pages/Home').then((m) => ({ default: m.Home })));

const { Header, Sider, Content } = Layout;

const NAV_ITEMS = [
  { key: '/connections', label: <Link to="/connections">Connections</Link> },
  { key: '/suites', label: <Link to="/suites">Suites</Link> },
  { key: '/profile', label: <Link to="/profile">Profile</Link> },
];

export function App() {
  const location = useLocation();
  // Highlight the nav item whose path prefixes the current location.
  const selectedKeys = NAV_ITEMS.map((i) => i.key).filter((k) => location.pathname.startsWith(k));

  return (
    <Layout style={{ minHeight: '100vh' }}>
      <Header style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 16 }}>
        <Typography.Title level={4} style={{ color: '#fff', margin: 0, flex: 1 }}>
          DataQ
        </Typography.Title>
        <UserChip />
      </Header>
      <Layout>
        <Sider width={200} theme="light" breakpoint="lg" collapsedWidth={0}>
          <Menu
            mode="inline"
            selectedKeys={selectedKeys}
            items={NAV_ITEMS}
            style={{ height: '100%', borderInlineEnd: 0 }}
          />
        </Sider>
        <Content style={{ padding: 24 }}>
          <AuthGate>
            <Suspense fallback={<Spin size="large" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />}>
              <Routes>
                <Route path="/" element={<Navigate to="/connections" replace />} />
                <Route path="/connections" element={<Connections />} />
                <Route path="/suites" element={<Suites />} />
                <Route path="/profile" element={<Home />} />
                <Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/connections" replace />} />
              </Routes>
            </Suspense>
          </AuthGate>
        </Content>
      </Layout>
    </Layout>
  );
}

function UserChip() {
  const user = useCurrentUser();
  if (!user) return null;

  const onLogout = () => {
    if (authMode !== 'real') return;
    const instance = getMsalInstance();
    void instance?.logoutRedirect({ account: instance.getAllAccounts()[0] });
  };

  return (
    <Flex align="center" gap={12}>
      {user.isDev && <Tag color="orange">DEV BYPASS</Tag>}
      <Typography.Text style={{ color: '#fff' }}>{user.name}</Typography.Text>
      {!user.isDev && (
        <Button size="small" onClick={onLogout}>
          Sign out
        </Button>
      )}
    </Flex>
  );
}
===MAIN===
import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { App as AntApp, ConfigProvider } from 'antd';
import { BrowserRouter } from 'react-router-dom';

import { App } from './App';
import { CurrentUserProvider } from './auth/CurrentUserProvider';
import { MsalProvider } from './auth/MsalProvider';
import { getMsalInstance } from './auth/msalInstance';
import { ErrorBoundary } from './components/ErrorBoundary';
import './styles.css';

const maybeRoot = document.getElementById('root');
if (!maybeRoot) {
  throw new Error('Root element #root not found in index.html');
}
const rootEl: HTMLElement = maybeRoot;

// MSAL lifecycle (issue #62):
//   1. .initialize() must complete before any MSAL API call (v5 requirement).
//   2. .handleRedirectPromise() must resolve before React renders so the
//      first paint reflects post-login state.
//   3. Errors surface to the console + a static page — fail loud during dev.
async function bootstrap() {
  const instance = getMsalInstance();
  if (instance) {
    await instance.initialize();
    await instance.handleRedirectPromise();
  }
  createRoot(rootEl).render(
    <StrictMode>
      <ConfigProvider>
        <AntApp>
          <ErrorBoundary>
            <MsalProvider>
              <CurrentUserProvider>
                <BrowserRouter>
                  <App />
                </BrowserRouter>
              </CurrentUserProvider>
            </MsalProvider>
          </ErrorBoundary>
        </AntApp>
      </ConfigProvider>
    </StrictMode>,
  );
}

bootstrap().catch((err) => {
  console.error('MSAL bootstrap failed', err);
  rootEl.innerHTML =
    '<pre style="padding:24px;color:#a00">Authentication bootstrap failed. See console.</pre>';
});

function ConnectionsBody({
  state,
  actions,
  health,
}: {
  state: AsyncState<Connection[]>;
  actions: ConnectionActions;
  health: Record<string, HealthState>;
}) {
  if (state.status === 'loading') {
    return <Spin tip="Loading connections…" size="large" style={{ marginTop: 80 }} />;
  }
  if (state.status === 'error') {
    return (
      <Alert
        type="error"
        showIcon
        title="Failed to load connections"
        description={state.error}
        style={{ margin: 24 }}
      />
    );
  }
  const connections = state.data;
  if (connections.length === 0) {
    return <Empty description="No connections configured yet" />;
  }
  return (
    <>
      {groupByType(connections).map(([type, group]) => (
        <ConnectionTypeSection
          key={type}
          type={type}
          connections={group}
          actions={actions}
          health={health}
        />
      ))}
    </>
  );
}

function ConnectionTypeSection({
  type,
  connections,
  actions,
  health,
}: {
  type: ConnectionType;
  connections: Connection[];
  actions: ConnectionActions;
  health: Record<string, HealthState>;
}) {
  return (
    <Flex vertical gap={12}>
      <Typography.Title level={5} style={{ margin: 0 }}>
        {CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[type]}
      </Typography.Title>
      <Flex wrap gap={12}>
        {connections.map((connection) => (
          <ConnectionCard
            key={connection.id}
            connection={connection}
            actions={actions}
            health={health[connection.id] ?? 'idle'}
          />
        ))}
      </Flex>
    </Flex>
  );
}

function ChecksList({
  suiteId,
  state,
  onAdd,
  onEdit,
  onChanged,
}: {
  suiteId: string;
  state: AsyncState<Check[]>;
  onAdd: () => void;
  onEdit: (check: Check) => void;
  onChanged: () => void;
}) {
  const { message, modal } = App.useApp();

  const onDelete = (check: Check) => {
    modal.confirm({
      title: `Delete “${check.name}”?`,
      okText: 'Delete',
      okType: 'danger',
      onOk: async () => {
        try {
          await deleteCheck(suiteId, check.id);
          message.success(`${check.name} deleted`);
          onChanged();
        } catch (err) {
          message.error(`Delete failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
          throw err; // keep the confirm modal open on failure
        }
      },
    });
  };

  if (state.status === 'loading') {
    return <Spin tip="Loading checks…" />;
  }
  if (state.status === 'error') {
    return <Alert type="error" showIcon title="Failed to load checks" description={state.error} />;
  }
  const checks = state.data;
  return (
    <Card
      size="small"
      title={`Checks (${checks.length})`}
      extra={
        <Button type="primary" size="small" onClick={onAdd}>
          Add check
        </Button>
      }
    >
      {checks.length === 0 ? (
        <Empty
          image={Empty.PRESENTED_IMAGE_SIMPLE}
          description="No checks yet — add one to start."
        />
      ) : (
        <List
          dataSource={checks}
          renderItem={(check) => (
            <List.Item
              actions={[
                <Button key="edit" type="link" size="small" onClick={() => onEdit(check)}>
                  Edit
                </Button>,
                <Button
                  key="delete"
                  type="link"
                  size="small"
                  danger
                  onClick={() => onDelete(check)}
                >
                  Delete
                </Button>,
              ]}
            >
              <Flex vertical gap={2}>
                <Typography.Text strong>{check.name}</Typography.Text>
                <Typography.Text type="secondary" style={{ fontSize: 12 }}>
                  {check.expectation_type}
                </Typography.Text>
              </Flex>
            </List.Item>
          )}
        />

        <Form.Item name="name" label="Name" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
          <Input />
        </Form.Item>
        <Form.Item name="description" label="Description (optional)">
          <Input.TextArea rows={3} />
        </Form.Item>
        <Form.Item
          name="connection_id"
          label="Connection"
          rules={[{ required: true }]}
          extra={isEdit ? 'The connection is fixed once a suite is created.' : undefined}
        >
          <Select
            disabled={isEdit}
            placeholder="Select a connection"
            options={connections.map((c) => ({
              value: c.id,
              label: `${c.name} · ${CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[c.type]} · ${envLabel(c.env)}`,
            }))}
          />
        </Form.Item>
      </Form>
    </Drawer>

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/e2e/suites.spec.ts",
  "content": "import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test';\n\n// Seeded suite + checks (backend/scripts/demo_data.py) read through the real API,\n// then a full browser authoring round-trip (create → verify → delete) that\n// mirrors the httpx API smoke but through the React UI a user actually drives.\ntest.describe('Suites page', () => {\n  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.goto('/suites');\n    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Suites', level: 3 })).toBeVisible();\n  });\n\n  test('selecting a seeded suite shows its checks', async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.getByText('Orders quality').click();\n\n    // Detail panel renders the suite title (h4) and its seeded checks.\n    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Orders quality', level: 4 })).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(page.getByText('order_id not null')).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(page.getByText('amount in range')).toBeVisible();\n    // The expectation type is surfaced under each check name.\n    await expect(page.getByText('expect_column_values_to_not_be_null').first()).toBeVisible();\n  });\n\n  test('create a suite, see it in the list, then delete it', async ({ page }) => {\n    const name = `e2e suite ${Date.now()}`;\n\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'New suite' }).click();\n    const drawer = page.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'New suite' });\n    await drawer.getByLabel('Name').fill(name);\n\n    // antd Select: open, pick the first option (any seeded connection).\n    await drawer.getByLabel('Connection').click();\n    await page.getByRole('option').first().click();\n\n    await drawer.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create' }).click();\n    await expect(drawer).toBeHidden();\n\n    // The new suite appears in the left list; select it.\n    const item = page.getByText(name, { exact: true });\n    await expect(item).toBeVisible();\n    await item.click();\n    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name, level: 4 })).toBeVisible();\n\n    // Delete it via the detail action → confirm modal → row disappears.\n    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' }).click();\n    const confirm = page.getByRole('dialog').filter({ hasText: 'Delete' });\n    await confirm.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByText(name, { exact: true })).toBeHidden();\n  });\n});\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/e2e/README.md",
  "content": "# Browser E2E (Playwright)\n\nDrives the **real app in a browser** under dev-bypass auth against the seeded\ndemo dataset — the other half of the full-stack smoke (#128). The httpx API\nsmoke (`backend/scripts/e2e_smoke.py`) proves `HTTP → service → DB`; this proves\nthe React UI a user actually clicks: `browser → Vite proxy → api → DB`.\n\n> Live `test()`/runs against real Snowflake/S3/etc. stay out of scope (no creds\n> locally — the documented deferred smoke). The connectivity tests here\n> **fail-soft**; the specs assert the health/error path renders, not that a real\n> datasource is reachable.\n\n## Run it locally\n\n1. Bring up the stack and seed the demo data:\n\n   ```bash\n   docker compose up -d            # postgres + redis + api + worker + frontend\n   conda run -n dataq python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev\n   ```\n\n2. Install browsers once, then run:\n\n   ```bash\n   cd frontend\n   pnpm install\n   pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium\n   pnpm e2e            # headless\n   pnpm e2e:ui         # Playwright UI mode (watch/debug)\n   ```\n\nThe config (`playwright.config.ts`) targets `E2E_BASE_URL` (default\n`http://localhost:3000`) and **reuses** the already-running compose/`pnpm dev`\nserver on :3000. Point it elsewhere with `E2E_BASE_URL=… pnpm e2e`.\n\n## In CI\n\nThe `frontend-e2e` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` spins up Postgres + Redis,\npip-installs the backend, runs migrations, seeds the demo data, launches\n`uvicorn` on :8000, then lets Playwright start its own Vite dev server on :3000\n(`VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET=http://localhost:8000`) and run the specs. No Azure /\nreal datasource credentials are involved — dev-bypass only.\n"
}

  "new_string": "      - name: Vitest\n        run: pnpm test\n\n  frontend-e2e:\n    name: Frontend — browser E2E (Playwright)\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    # Full-stack browser smoke (#128): real API + seeded demo data + dev-bypass,\n    # driven through the React UI. Mirrors the compose stack — Postgres + Redis\n    # services, the backend on :8000, Playwright starts its own Vite dev server.\n    # No Azure / datasource creds: connectivity fails-soft, the UI paths are real.\n    services:\n      postgres:\n        image: postgres:16-alpine\n        env:\n          POSTGRES_USER: dataq\n          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: dataq\n          POSTGRES_DB: dataq_e2e\n        ports:\n          - 5432:5432\n        options: >-\n          --health-cmd \"pg_isready -U dataq\"\n          --health-interval 5s\n          --health-timeout 3s\n          --health-retries 10\n      redis:\n        image: redis:7-alpine\n        ports:\n          - 6379:6379\n        options: >-\n          --health-cmd \"redis-cli ping\"\n          --health-interval 5s\n          --health-timeout 3s\n          --health-retries 10\n    env:\n      DATABASE_URL: REDACTED\n      REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0\n      # api + seed must share the secret store so secrets the seed writes are\n      # readable by the api (compose parity). dev-bypass removes the auth wall.\n      SECRET_STORE: redis\n      AUTH_DEV_BYPASS: \"true\"\n      ENVIRONMENT: dev\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v6\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6\n        with:\n          python-version: \"3.13\"\n          cache: pip\n\n      - name: Install backend\n        run: |\n          python -m pip install -U pip\n          pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt\n\n      - name: Run migrations + seed demo data\n        # alembic.ini's script_location is relative to backend/ (compose parity).\n        run: |\n          (cd backend && alembic upgrade head)\n          python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev\n\n      - name: Launch the API\n        # Background uvicorn, then block until it serves before Playwright starts.\n        run: |\n          uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 &\n          for i in $(seq 1 30); do\n            if curl -sf http://localhost:8000/api/v1/connections >/dev/null; then\n              echo \"api up\"; exit 0\n            fi\n            sleep 2\n          done\n          echo \"api did not come up\"; exit 1\n\n      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6\n        with:\n          version: 9\n\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6\n        with:\n          node-version: \"20\"\n\n      - name: Install frontend\n        working-directory: frontend\n        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile\n\n      - name: Install Playwright browser\n        working-directory: frontend\n        run: pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium\n\n      - name: Playwright E2E\n        working-directory: frontend\n        # CI=true → Playwright starts its own Vite dev server (proxying to the\n        # api on :8000) and applies forbidOnly + flaky-retries.\n        env:\n          VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET: http://localhost:8000\n        run: pnpm e2e\n\n      - name: Upload Playwright report\n        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}\n        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4\n        with:\n          name: playwright-report\n          path: frontend/playwright-report/\n          retention-days: 7\n\n  frontend-audit:"
}

  secretLabel: string;

  multilineSecret?: boolean;

  extraField?: TextField;
}

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# GX-Cloud-style UI redesign: classified pages for Connections, Checks, and a Results surface

## Context

The Week-4 UI works but everything happens in **sidebar drawers** with **flat lists**:
`ConnectionDrawer` spec-drives all 6 connection types with no visible
datasource-vs-orchestration split, and `CheckDrawer` exposes a flat 7-item
`EXPECTATION_CATALOG` with no categorisation. There is also **no results/runs
surface at all** — `Run`/`Result`/`PipelineRun` models and `run_service` exist,
but no REST API lists them and there's no manual-run path.

Goal: model the UI on GX Cloud — dedicated **full-page create flows** that
**classify** what you're creating (data sources vs orchestration; checks by
type), plus an **in-app results / past-runs page**. Confirmed decisions:

1. **Results = in-app React page** (runs table + run detail + metric trend).
   Grafana is **deferred** as an optional post-v1 ops add-on (recorded in an
   ADR), never the per-suite authz path — reading Postgres directly would bypass
   suite-level sharing + PII redaction.
2. **Full-page create, drawer edit** — new routed pages for *create*; keep the
   existing drawers/modals for *edit* + re-auth (no churn to working paths).
3. **Sequence**: connections + checks redesign **now** (frontend; backends
   ready). Results page **after** the Week-5 run-enablement backend.

Domain nouns stay ours (Connections / Suites / Checks / Results) — we model GX
Cloud's *shape*, not its vocabulary. The check-category seam aligns with the
monitor-kind discriminator (ADR 0012): categories map toward `check.kind`, so
future freshness/volume monitors slot into the same picker.

---

## Phase A — Connections: dedicated, classified create page (frontend-only)

**Classification source of truth.** Add to `frontend/src/api/connections.ts`
next to `CONNECTION_TYPES`/`CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS`:
```ts
export const CONNECTION_KIND: Record<ConnectionType, 'datasource' | 'orchestration'> = {
  snowflake: 'datasource', adls_gen2: 'datasource', s3: 'datasource',
  unity_catalog: 'datasource', adf: 'orchestration', airflow: 'orchestration',
};
```
Derive `DATASOURCE_TYPES` / `ORCHESTRATION_TYPES` from it (single source — no
hardcoded lists elsewhere).

**New page** `frontend/src/pages/ConnectionNew.tsx`, route `/connections/new`:
- Step 1 — two labelled sections **Data sources** and **Orchestration**, each a
  card grid of its types (GX-Cloud picker). Reuse `CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS`.
- Step 2 — per-type form: **reuse the existing spec-driven fields**
  (`ConnectionTypeFields.tsx` + `connectionFormSpec.ts` +
  `initialConfigForType`) plus name/env/secret, submit via `createConnection`.
- Success → `navigate('/connections')`.

**Refactor `ConnectionDrawer.tsx`** to keep *edit* only; extract the shared inner
form so both the new page and the edit drawer render the same fields (most of
this already lives in `ConnectionTypeFields`).

**`frontend/src/pages/Connections.tsx`**: render the list under the two top-level
sections (Data sources / Orchestration), each still grouping by type
(`groupByType` reused within a section). Change **Add connection** to
`navigate('/connections/new')`. Keep `ReauthModal` + edit drawer + health page.

**`App.tsx`**: add the lazy `/connections/new` route.

## Phase B — Checks: dedicated, classified create page (frontend-only)

**Add `category`** to each entry in
`frontend/src/components/checks/expectationCatalog.ts`:
- **Column values** — not_null, unique, between, in_set, value_lengths_between, match_regex
- **Table shape** — table_row_count_to_be_between
- (optional) reserved, disabled categories **Freshness / Volume / Schema drift**
  rendered greyed "coming in v1.x" to surface the ADR-0012 monitor-kind roadmap.

**New page** `frontend/src/pages/CheckNew.tsx`, route
`/suites/:suiteId/checks/new`:
- Step 1 category picker → Step 2 expectation picker within category → Step 3
  config + thresholds. **Reuse** `CheckDrawer`'s existing `formToConfig`,
  `parseList`, list-validator, and dynamic field rendering (extract them into a
  shared `CheckFields` module so page + edit-drawer share logic).
- Natural home for the **#215 target table/path** field once that backend lands.

**Make suite selection a route** to preserve context across the check-editor
round-trip: `/suites` (none selected) + `/suites/:suiteId` (detail). The
two-panel layout stays; selecting a row navigates. "Add check" →
`/suites/:suiteId/checks/new`; back/save returns to `/suites/:suiteId`. Keep
`CheckDrawer` for *edit*.

## Phase C — Results & past runs page (Week-5-gated; backend first)

**Backend (new, Week 5)** — these are the run-enablement gaps already tracked:
- `#215` check **target table/path** modeling (the gate for any real run).
- Manual run: `POST /suites/{id}/run` (the #2 gap) → `run_service` dispatch.
- New `backend/app/api/v1/runs.py`:
  - `GET /runs?suite_id=&status=&limit=` → `RunRead` list
  - `GET /runs/{run_id}` → run + joined `Result`s (severity, `metric_value`,
    `observed_value`, redacted sample rows, `duration_ms`)
  - `GET /pipeline_runs?provider=&...` → orchestration monitoring feed
  Read-model schemas mirror `Run`/`Result`/`PipelineRun` in
  `backend/app/db/models.py`; reuse `run_service`. Enforce **suite-level
  sharing** in the query (same authz as suites) — this is exactly why Grafana
  isn't the path.

**Frontend** `frontend/src/pages/Results.tsx`, route `/results`:
- Runs table: suite, status, health score, started_at, duration. Filters.
- Run detail (drawer or `/results/:runId`): per-check rows — name, expectation,
  severity tag, observed/metric value, pass/fail, sample rows.
- Optional first-cut: per-check **metric_value sparkline** over recent runs
  (the column was designed SQL-aggregatable for exactly this — ADR 0012).
- Pipeline-runs tab reading `/pipeline_runs`.
- **Logs**: run detail deep-links to App Insights via `request_id`; the
  structured run record renders in-app. No Grafana.

**ADR** `docs/adr/0018-results-surface-and-grafana-deferral.md`: in-app results =
primary (suite-scoped authz, GX-Cloud parity); Grafana = optional post-v1 ops
dashboard (read-only reporting role + DB grants), additive only.

## IA / nav

`App.tsx` sidebar → **Connections · Suites · Results · Profile**. Add the lazy
`/results` route. Keep nav prefix-match (#192).

---

## Sequencing (one PR per slice, docs folded in per standing directive)

1. **PR-A1** Connection classification + `/connections/new` page + sectioned list.
2. **PR-A2** Connections drawer refactor to edit-only (if not folded into A1).
3. **PR-B1** Suite-selection-as-route + check categories.
4. **PR-B2** `/suites/:suiteId/checks/new` page (+ #215 target field when ready).
5. **PR-C0** (Week 5) backend: #215, `POST /suites/{id}/run`, `runs.py` endpoints.
6. **PR-C1** Results page + ADR 0018.

Each frontend PR: vitest unit + a Playwright spec for the new flow; each backend
PR: pytest. Update `docs/progress.md` + CLAUDE.md §13 in-PR.

## Verification

- **Unit**: `cd frontend && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test`;
  backend `pytest backend/tests/` (Phase C).
- **E2E** against the running compose stack + seed: extend
  `frontend/e2e/` — `connections.spec.ts` (pick Data sources → Snowflake →
  create → appears in list), a new `checks.spec.ts` (category → expectation →
  create → appears under the suite), and (Phase C) `results.spec.ts` (run a
  suite → run shows in the table → open detail). Backend API smoke:
  `backend/scripts/e2e_smoke.py` gains a run-trigger + `/runs` read assertion.
- **Manual**: `docker compose up` + `seed_dev`, click each new flow at
  localhost:3000 under dev-bypass.

```

1	import { App, Button, Drawer, Flex, Form, Input, Select } from 'antd';
2	import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
3	
4	import {
5	  CONNECTION_ENVS,
6	  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,
7	  CONNECTION_TYPES,
8	  type Connection,
9	  type ConnectionCreate,
10	  type ConnectionType,
11	  createConnection,
12	  envLabel,
13	  updateConnection,
14	} from '../../api/connections';
15	import { ConnectionTypeFields } from './ConnectionTypeFields';
16	import { initialConfigForType } from './connectionFormSpec';
17	
18	interface FormValues {
19	  name: string;
20	  type: ConnectionType;
21	  env: ConnectionCreate['env'];
22	  config?: Record<string, unknown>;
23	  secret?: string;
24	}
25	
26	/**
27	 * Create or edit a connection. In edit mode (`connection` present), type + env
28	 * are immutable (the backend `ConnectionUpdate` rejects them) and the secret is
29	 * omitted — credential rotation is the separate Re-auth flow.
30	 */
31	export function ConnectionDrawer({
32	  open,
33	  onClose,
34	  onSaved,
35	  connection,
36	}: {
37	  open: boolean;
38	  onClose: () => void;
39	  /** Called after a successful create or update (so the list can refresh). */
40	  onSaved: () => void;
41	  connection?: Connection;
42	}) {
43	  const isEdit = connection !== undefined;
44	  const { message } = App.useApp();
45	  const [form] = Form.useForm<FormValues>();
46	  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
47	  const watchedType = Form.useWatch('type', form) as ConnectionType | undefined;
48	  const type = isEdit ? connection.type : watchedType;
49	
50	  // Prefill when opening in edit mode (the Drawer's destroyOnHidden remounts the
51	  // form each open, so this re-seeds for whichever connection is being edited).
52	  useEffect(() => {
53	    if (open && connection) {
54	      form.setFieldsValue({
55	        name: connection.name,
56	        type: connection.type,
57	        env: connection.env,
58	        config: connection.config,
59	      });
60	    }
61	  }, [open, connection, form]);
62	
63	  // Switching type (create only) invalidates the previous config fields.
64	  const onTypeChange = (next: ConnectionType) => {
65	    form.setFieldsValue({ config: initialConfigForType(next), secret: undefined });
66	  };
67	
68	  const onFinish = async (values: FormValues) => {
69	    setSubmitting(true);
70	    try {
71	      if (isEdit) {
72	        await updateConnection(connection.id, {
73	          name: values.name,
74	          config: values.config ?? {},
75	        });
76	        message.success(`Connection “${values.name}” updated`);
77	      } else {
78	        await createConnection({
79	          name: values.name,
80	          type: values.type,
81	          env: values.env,
82	          config: values.config ?? {},
83	          secret: values.secret || undefined,
84	        });
85	        message.success(`Connection “${values.name}” created`);
86	      }
87	      form.resetFields();
88	      onSaved();
89	    } catch (err) {
90	      message.error(
91	        `${isEdit ? 'Update' : 'Create'} failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`,
92	      );
93	    } finally {
94	      setSubmitting(false);
95	    }
96	  };
97	
98	  return (
99	    <Drawer
100	      title={isEdit ? 'Edit connection' : 'Add connection'}
101	      open={open}
102	      onClose={onClose}
103	      width={520}
104	      destroyOnHidden
105	      footer={
106	        <Flex justify="end" gap={8}>
107	          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>
108	          <Button type="primary" loading={submitting} onClick={() => form.submit()}>
109	            {isEdit ? 'Save' : 'Create'}
110	          </Button>
111	        </Flex>
112	      }
113	    >
114	      <Form form={form} layout="vertical" onFinish={onFinish} requiredMark="optional">
115	        <Form.Item name="name" label="Name" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
116	          <Input />
117	        </Form.Item>
118	        <Form.Item name="env" label="Environment" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
119	          <Select
120	            disabled={isEdit}
121	            options={CONNECTION_ENVS.map((e) => ({ value: e, label: envLabel(e) }))}
122	            placeholder="Select an environment"
123	          />
124	        </Form.Item>
125	        <Form.Item name="type" label="Type" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
126	          <Select
127	            disabled={isEdit}
128	            placeholder="Select a connection type"
129	            onChange={onTypeChange}
130	            options={CONNECTION_TYPES.map((t) => ({ value: t, label: CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[t] }))}
131	          />
132	        </Form.Item>
133	        {type && <ConnectionTypeFields type={type} form={form} showSecret={!isEdit} />}
134	      </Form>
135	    </Drawer>
136	  );
137	}
138

1	import { Form, Input, Select, type FormInstance } from 'antd';
2	
3	import type { ConnectionType } from '../../api/connections';
4	import { CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS, type TextField } from './connectionFormSpec';
5	
6	/**
7	 * Renders the type-specific config + secret form fields from CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS.
8	 * Config fields are namespaced under `config` (name={['config','account']}) so the
9	 * drawer submits `config` as one object; the write-only credential is `secret`.
10	 */
11	
12	const requiredRule = [{ required: true }];
13	
14	function ConfigTextField({ field }: { field: TextField }) {
15	  return (
16	    <Form.Item
17	      name={['config', field.name]}
18	      label={field.optional ? `${field.label} (optional)` : field.label}
19	      rules={field.optional ? undefined : requiredRule}
20	    >
21	      <Input />
22	    </Form.Item>
23	  );
24	}
25	
26	function SecretField({ label, multiline = false }: { label: string; multiline?: boolean }) {
27	  return (
28	    <Form.Item name="secret" label={label} rules={requiredRule}>
29	      {multiline ? (
30	        <Input.TextArea rows={4} autoComplete="off" />
31	      ) : (
32	        <Input.Password autoComplete="off" />
33	      )}
34	    </Form.Item>
35	  );
36	}
37	
38	export function ConnectionTypeFields({
39	  type,
40	  form,
41	  showSecret = true,
42	}: {
43	  type: ConnectionType;
44	  form: FormInstance;
45	  /** Edit mode omits the secret — credential rotation is the Re-auth flow. */
46	  showSecret?: boolean;
47	}) {
48	  const spec = CONNECTION_FORM_SPECS[type];
49	  const authType = Form.useWatch(['config', 'auth_type'], form) as string | undefined;
50	  const activeAuth = spec.auth?.find((a) => a.value === authType) ?? spec.auth?.[0];
51	
52	  return (
53	    <>
54	      {spec.textFields.map((f) => (
55	        <ConfigTextField key={f.name} field={f} />
56	      ))}
57	
58	      {spec.auth && (
59	        <Form.Item name={['config', 'auth_type']} label="Auth type" rules={requiredRule}>
60	          <Select options={spec.auth.map((a) => ({ value: a.value, label: a.label }))} />
61	        </Form.Item>
62	      )}
63	
64	      {activeAuth?.extraField && <ConfigTextField field={activeAuth.extraField} />}
65	
66	      {showSecret &&
67	        (activeAuth ? (
68	          <SecretField label={activeAuth.secretLabel} multiline={activeAuth.multilineSecret} />
69	        ) : (
70	          spec.secretLabel && <SecretField label={spec.secretLabel} />
71	        ))}
72	    </>
73	  );
74	}
75

1	import { api } from './client';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Connections API — the six configurable connection types (CLAUDE.md §4).
5	 * ADF + Airflow are orchestration providers, not datasources, but they are
6	 * still `connections` rows and managed through the same CRUD surface.
7	 */
8	
9	export const CONNECTION_TYPES = [
10	  'snowflake',
11	  'adls_gen2',
12	  's3',
13	  'unity_catalog',
14	  'adf',
15	  'airflow',
16	] as const;
17	export type ConnectionType = (typeof CONNECTION_TYPES)[number];
18	
19	export const CONNECTION_ENVS = ['dev', 'qa', 'uat', 'prod'] as const;
20	export type ConnectionEnv = (typeof CONNECTION_ENVS)[number];
21	
22	/** Display label for an env (single source for the list page + the drawer). */
23	export const envLabel = (env: ConnectionEnv): string => env.toUpperCase();
24	
25	/** Tag color per env — shared by every page that renders an env badge. */
26	export const ENV_COLORS: Record<ConnectionEnv, string> = {
27	  dev: 'blue',
28	  qa: 'gold',
29	  uat: 'purple',
30	  prod: 'red',
31	};
32	
33	/** Mirrors the backend `ConnectionRead` schema (secret is never returned). */
34	export interface Connection {
35	  id: string;
36	  name: string;
37	  type: ConnectionType;
38	  env: ConnectionEnv;
39	  config: Record<string, unknown>;
40	  has_secret: boolean;
41	  created_by: string;
42	}
43	
44	/** Human-readable labels for the connection types, for grouping + display. */
45	export const CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS: Record<ConnectionType, string> = {
46	  snowflake: 'Snowflake',
47	  adls_gen2: 'ADLS Gen2',
48	  s3: 'AWS S3',
49	  unity_catalog: 'Unity Catalog',
50	  adf: 'Azure Data Factory',
51	  airflow: 'Airflow',
52	};
53	
54	export async function listConnections(params?: {
55	  type?: ConnectionType;
56	  env?: ConnectionEnv;
57	}): Promise<Connection[]> {
58	  const { data } = await api.get<Connection[]>('/connections', { params });
59	  return data;
60	}
61	
62	/** Live connectivity test — a green result means the credential authenticates. */
63	export async function testConnection(id: string): Promise<{ ok: boolean }> {
64	  const { data } = await api.post<{ ok: boolean }>(`/connections/${id}/test`);
65	  return data;
66	}
67	
68	/** Mirrors the backend `ConnectionCreate` schema (secret is write-only). */
69	export interface ConnectionCreate {
70	  name: string;
71	  type: ConnectionType;
72	  env: ConnectionEnv;
73	  config: Record<string, unknown>;
74	  secret?: string;
75	}
76	
77	export async function createConnection(payload: ConnectionCreate): Promise<Connection> {
78	  const { data } = await api.post<Connection>('/connections', payload);
79	  return data;
80	}
81	
82	/** Mirrors the backend `ConnectionUpdate` schema — type/env are immutable. */
83	export interface ConnectionUpdate {
84	  name?: string;
85	  config?: Record<string, unknown>;
86	  secret?: string;
87	}
88	
89	export async function updateConnection(id: string, payload: ConnectionUpdate): Promise<Connection> {
90	  const { data } = await api.patch<Connection>(`/connections/${id}`, payload);
91	  return data;
92	}
93	
94	export async function deleteConnection(id: string): Promise<void> {
95	  await api.delete(`/connections/${id}`);
96	}
97	
98	/** Rotate the credential and verify it in one step (bad credential → error). */
99	export async function reauthConnection(id: string, secret: string): Promise<{ ok: boolean }> {
100	  const { data } = await api.post<{ ok: boolean }>(`/connections/${id}/reauth`, { secret });
101	  return data;
102	}

1	import { MoreOutlined } from '@ant-design/icons';
2	import {
3	  Alert,
4	  App,
5	  Badge,
6	  Button,
7	  Card,
8	  Dropdown,
9	  Empty,
10	  Flex,
11	  Spin,
12	  Tag,
13	  Typography,
14	} from 'antd';
15	import { useCallback, useState } from 'react';
16	
17	import {
18	  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,
19	  CONNECTION_TYPES,
20	  type Connection,
21	  type ConnectionType,
22	  deleteConnection,
23	  ENV_COLORS,
24	  envLabel,
25	  listConnections,
26	  testConnection,
27	} from '../api/connections';
28	import { ConnectionDrawer } from '../components/connections/ConnectionDrawer';
29	import { ReauthModal } from '../components/connections/ReauthModal';
30	import { type AsyncState, useAsyncData } from '../hooks/useAsyncData';
31	
32	/** Live connectivity state for a card — the health-page badge. */
33	type HealthState = 'idle' | 'testing' | 'ok' | 'failed';
34	
35	/** Per-card actions, threaded from the page so they can mutate shared state. */
36	interface ConnectionActions {
37	  onEdit: (connection: Connection) => void;
38	  onReauth: (connection: Connection) => void;
39	  onChanged: () => void;
40	  /** Run a connectivity test and reflect the result on the card's health badge. */
41	  onTest: (connection: Connection) => Promise<boolean>;
42	  /** Drop a connection's stale health entry (after delete / edit / re-auth). */
43	  onClearHealth: (id: string) => void;
44	}
45	
46	/** Group connections by type in one pass, preserving canonical type order. */
47	function groupByType(connections: Connection[]): [ConnectionType, Connection[]][] {
48	  const byType = new Map<ConnectionType, Connection[]>();
49	  for (const c of connections) {
50	    const group = byType.get(c.type);
51	    if (group) group.push(c);
52	    else byType.set(c.type, [c]);
53	  }
54	  return CONNECTION_TYPES.filter((type) => byType.has(type)).map((type) => [
55	    type,
56	    byType.get(type) as Connection[],
57	  ]);
58	}
59	
60	export function Connections() {
61	  const { message } = App.useApp();
62	  const { state, reload } = useAsyncData(listConnections);
63	  // `drawer.connection === undefined` while open = create mode; a connection = edit.
64	  const [drawer, setDrawer] = useState<{ open: boolean; connection?: Connection }>({ open: false });
65	  const [reauthing, setReauthing] = useState<Connection | null>(null);
66	  // Per-connection live connectivity status (the bulk health view).
67	  const [health, setHealth] = useState<Record<string, HealthState>>({});
68	  const [testingAll, setTestingAll] = useState(false);
69	
70	  const testOne = useCallback(async (connection: Connection): Promise<boolean> => {
71	    setHealth((h) => ({ ...h, [connection.id]: 'testing' }));
72	    try {
73	      const { ok } = await testConnection(connection.id);
74	      setHealth((h) => ({ ...h, [connection.id]: ok ? 'ok' : 'failed' }));
75	      return ok;
76	    } catch {
77	      setHealth((h) => ({ ...h, [connection.id]: 'failed' }));
78	      return false;
79	    }
80	  }, []);
81	
82	  // Drop a stale health result when the connection changes underneath it —
83	  // after a re-auth, an edit, or a delete the prior pass/fail no longer holds,
84	  // so the badge returns to idle until re-tested (and the map can't leak).
85	  const clearHealth = useCallback((id: string) => {
86	    setHealth((h) =>
87	      id in h ? Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(h).filter(([key]) => key !== id)) : h,
88	    );
89	  }, []);
90	
91	  const connections = state.status === 'ok' ? state.data : [];
92	
93	  const testAll = async () => {
94	    setTestingAll(true);
95	    const results = await Promise.all(connections.map(testOne));
96	    setTestingAll(false);
97	    const failed = results.filter((ok) => !ok).length;
98	    if (failed === 0) message.success(`All ${results.length} connections healthy`);
99	    else message.warning(`${failed} of ${results.length} connections unreachable`);
100	  };

154	  health,
155	}: {
156	  state: AsyncState<Connection[]>;
157	  actions: ConnectionActions;

159	}) {

162	  }

164	    return (

175	  if (connections.length === 0) {

132	          if (drawer.connection) clearHealth(drawer.connection.id);
133	          setDrawer({ open: false });
134	          reload();
135	        }}
136	      />
137	      <ReauthModal
138	        connection={reauthing}
139	        onClose={() => setReauthing(null)}
140	        onDone={() => {
141	          // Credential rotated → the old unreachable verdict no longer holds.
142	          if (reauthing) clearHealth(reauthing.id);
143	          setReauthing(null);
144	          reload();
145	        }}
146	      />

(\n        <Form form={form} layout=\"vertical\" onFinish={onFinish} requiredMark=\"optional\">\n          <Form.Item name=\"name\" label=\"Name\" rules={[{ required: true }]}>\n            <Input />\n          </Form.Item>\n          <Form.Item name=\"env\" label=\"Environment\" rules={[{ required: true }]}>\n            <Select\n              options={CONNECTION_ENVS.map((e) => ({ value: e, label: envLabel(e) }))}\n              placeholder=\"Select an environment\"\n            />\n          </Form.Item>\n          <ConnectionTypeFields type={type} form={form} />\n          <Flex justify=\"end\" gap={8}>\n            <Button onClick={() => setType(undefined)}>Back</Button>\n            <Button type=\"primary\" htmlType=\"submit\" loading={submitting}>\n              Create\n            </Button>\n          </Flex>\n        </Form>\n      ) : (\n        <Flex vertical gap={24}>\n          <TypeSection kind=\"datasource\" types={DATASOURCE_TYPES} onPick={onPick} />\n          <TypeSection kind=\"orchestration\" types={ORCHESTRATION_TYPES} onPick={onPick} />\n        </Flex>\n      )}\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction TypeSection({\n  kind,\n  types,\n  onPick,\n}: {\n  kind: ConnectionKind;\n  types: ConnectionType[];\n  onPick: (type: ConnectionType) => void;\n}) {\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical gap={12}>\n      <Typography.Title level={5} style={{ margin: 0 }}>\n        {CONNECTION_KIND_LABELS[kind]}\n      </Typography.Title>\n      <Flex wrap gap={12}>\n        {types.map((type) => (\n          <Card\n            key={type}\n            hoverable\n            size=\"small\"\n            style={{ minWidth: 200 }}\n            onClick={() => onPick(type)}\n          >\n            <Typography.Text strong>{CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[type]}</Typography.Text>\n          </Card>\n        ))}\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n"

> AGENT

**Node 20** is the project standard, pinned in three places:

- [frontend/package.json](frontend/package.json#L?) — `engines.node: ">=20"`, `packageManager: pnpm@9.15.4`
- [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml) — every `actions/setup-node@v6` uses `node-version: "20"`
- [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml#L124) — the frontend service runs `node:20-alpine`

(My local host happens to have Node 26, but nothing in the project depends on that — CI and the compose stack are the source of truth at 20.)

One thing worth flagging that surfaced in the last CI run: a GitHub-Actions deprecation warning — *"Node.js 20 actions are deprecated… forced to Node.js 24 by June 16th, 2026"*. That's about the **runtime GitHub uses to execute JS-based actions** (e.g. `actions/upload-artifact@v4`), **not our app's Node 20** — they're unrelated. No action needed now, but when we bump runner action versions later it'll resolve itself.

Want me to continue with **PR-A2** (trim `ConnectionDrawer` to edit-only)? I've marked it in progress.
