=== ConnectionDrawer.test.tsx ===
import { App as AntApp } from 'antd';
import { render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

import { type Connection, createConnection, updateConnection } from '../../src/api/connections';
import { ConnectionDrawer } from '../../src/components/connections/ConnectionDrawer';

vi.mock('../../src/api/connections', async (importOriginal) => {
  const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import('../../src/api/connections')>();
  return { ...actual, createConnection: vi.fn(), updateConnection: vi.fn() };
});

const mockCreate = vi.mocked(createConnection);
const mockUpdate = vi.mocked(updateConnection);

function renderDrawer(props: Partial<Parameters<typeof ConnectionDrawer>[0]> = {}) {
  return render(
    <AntApp>
      <ConnectionDrawer open onClose={vi.fn()} onSaved={vi.fn()} {...props} />
    </AntApp>,
  );
}

// antd Select renders options in a portal; pick by visible option text.
async function selectOption(
  user: ReturnType<typeof userEvent.setup>,
  label: string,
  option: string,
) {
  const field = screen.getByLabelText(label);
  await user.click(field);
  const opt = await screen.findByText(option, { selector: '.ant-select-item-option-content' });
  await user.click(opt);
}

afterEach(() => {
  vi.clearAllMocks();
});

describe('ConnectionDrawer — create', () => {
  it('shows type-specific fields after picking a type (Snowflake)', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderDrawer();

    await selectOption(user, 'Type', 'Snowflake');

    expect(await screen.findByLabelText('Account')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByLabelText('Warehouse')).toBeInTheDocument();
    // Snowflake defaults to password auth → a Password secret field.
    expect(screen.getByLabelText('Password')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('swaps the secret field to a PEM textarea for Snowflake key-pair auth', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderDrawer();

    await selectOption(user, 'Type', 'Snowflake');
    await selectOption(user, 'Auth type', 'Key pair (RSA)');

    expect(await screen.findByLabelText('Private key (PEM)')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(
      screen.queryByLabelText('Password', { selector: 'input,textarea' }),
    ).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('shows S3 access-key fields with no auth toggle (IAM role deferred in v1)', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderDrawer();

    await selectOption(user, 'Type', 'AWS S3');

    expect(await screen.findByLabelText('Access key ID')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByLabelText('Secret access key')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByLabelText('Auth type')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('submits the assembled payload and calls onSaved', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onSaved = vi.fn();
    mockCreate.mockResolvedValue({
      id: 'c1',
      name: 'uc-dev',
      type: 'unity_catalog',
      env: 'dev',
      config: { workspace_url: 'https://w', warehouse_id: 'wh1' },
      has_secret: true,
      created_by: 'u1',
    });
    renderDrawer({ onSaved });

    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText('Name'), 'uc-dev');
    await selectOption(user, 'Environment', 'DEV');
    await selectOption(user, 'Type', 'Unity Catalog');
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText('Workspace URL'), 'https://w');
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText('Warehouse ID'), 'wh1');
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText('Personal access token (PAT)'), 'pat-xyz');

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create' }));

    await waitFor(() => expect(mockCreate).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1));
    expect(mockCreate).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      name: 'uc-dev',
      type: 'unity_catalog',
      env: 'dev',
      config: { workspace_url: 'https://w', warehouse_id: 'wh1' },
      secret: 'pat-xyz',
    });
    expect(onSaved).toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('does not submit when required fields are missing', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderDrawer();

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create' }));

    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getAllByText('Name').length).toBeGreaterThan(0));
    expect(mockCreate).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});

describe('ConnectionDrawer — edit', () => {
  const existing: Connection = {
    id: 'c1',
    name: 'sf-dev',
    type: 'snowflake',
    env: 'dev',
    config: {
      account: 'acc1',
      user: 'svc',
      database: 'DB',
      schema: 'SC',
      warehouse: 'WH',
      auth_type: 'password',
    },
    has_secret: true,
    created_by: 'u1',
  };

  it('prefills config, omits the secret field, and submits an update via PATCH', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onSaved = vi.fn();
    mockUpdate.mockResolvedValue({ ...existing, name: 'sf-dev-2' });
    renderDrawer({ connection: existing, onSaved });

    // Prefilled name + config (effect-driven, so wait for it).
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByLabelText('Account')).toHaveValue('acc1'));
    expect(screen.getByLabelText('Name')).toHaveValue('sf-dev');
    // Edit mode omits the secret — rotation is the Re-auth flow.
    expect(screen.queryByLabelText('Password')).not.toBeInTheDocument();

    await user.clear(screen.getByLabelText('Name'));
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText('Name'), 'sf-dev-2');
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }));

    await waitFor(() => expect(mockUpdate).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1));
    expect(mockUpdate).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      'c1',
      expect.objectContaining({
        name: 'sf-dev-2',
        config: expect.objectContaining({ account: 'acc1', auth_type: 'password' }),
      }),
    );
    expect(mockCreate).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(onSaved).toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/components/connections/ConnectionDrawer.tsx",
  "content": "import { App, Button, Drawer, Flex, Form, Input, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';\nimport { useEffect, useState } from 'react';\n\nimport {\n  CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS,\n  type Connection,\n  type ConnectionCreate,\n  ENV_COLORS,\n  envLabel,\n  updateConnection,\n} from '../../api/connections';\nimport { ConnectionTypeFields } from './ConnectionTypeFields';\n\ninterface FormValues {\n  name: string;\n  config?: Record<string, unknown>;\n}\n\n/**\n * Edit an existing connection. Type + env are immutable (the backend\n * `ConnectionUpdate` rejects them) and shown read-only; the secret is omitted —\n * credential rotation is the separate Re-auth flow. Creating a connection is a\n * dedicated page (`/connections/new`), not this drawer.\n */\nexport function ConnectionDrawer({\n  open,\n  onClose,\n  onSaved,\n  connection,\n}: {\n  open: boolean;\n  onClose: () => void;\n  /** Called after a successful update (so the list can refresh). */\n  onSaved: () => void;\n  connection?: Connection;\n}) {\n  const { message } = App.useApp();\n  const [form] = Form.useForm<FormValues>();\n  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);\n\n  // Prefill when opening (destroyOnHidden remounts the form each open, so this\n  // re-seeds for whichever connection is being edited).\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (open && connection) {\n      form.setFieldsValue({ name: connection.name, config: connection.config });\n    }\n  }, [open, connection, form]);\n\n  const onFinish = async (values: FormValues) => {\n    if (!connection) return;\n    setSubmitting(true);\n    try {\n      await updateConnection(connection.id, {\n        name: values.name,\n        config: values.config ?? {},\n      });\n      message.success(`Connection “${values.name}” updated`);\n      form.resetFields();\n      onSaved();\n    } catch (err) {\n      message.error(`Update failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);\n    } finally {\n      setSubmitting(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Drawer\n      title=\"Edit connection\"\n      open={open}\n      onClose={onClose}\n      width={520}\n      destroyOnHidden\n      footer={\n        <Flex justify=\"end\" gap={8}>\n          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>\n          <Button type=\"primary\" loading={submitting} onClick={() => form.submit()}>\n            Save\n          </Button>\n        </Flex>\n      }\n    >\n      {connection && (\n        <Form form={form} layout=\"vertical\" onFinish={onFinish} requiredMark=\"optional\">\n          <Form.Item name=\"name\" label=\"Name\" rules={[{ required: true }]}>\n            <Input />\n          </Form.Item>\n          {/* Type + env are fixed once a connection is created — show, don't edit. */}\n          <Form.Item label=\"Type\">\n            <Typography.Text>{CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[connection.type]}</Typography.Text>\n          </Form.Item>\n          <Form.Item label=\"Environment\">\n            <Tag color={ENV_COLORS[connection.env]}>{envLabel(connection.env)}</Tag>\n          </Form.Item>\n          <ConnectionTypeFields type={connection.type} form={form} showSecret={false} />\n        </Form>\n      )}\n    </Drawer>\n  );\n}\n\n// Re-exported for callers that only need the create payload shape.\nexport type { ConnectionCreate };\n"
}

1	/**
2	 * Curated catalog of GX expectations the check editor exposes in v1.
3	 *
4	 * The backend treats `expectation_type` as a snake_case string (title-cased to a
5	 * GX expectation class) and `config` as free-form GX kwargs — there is no server
6	 * catalog. This file is the frontend's single source of truth for which
7	 * expectations are offered and what typed config each needs, the same spec-driven
8	 * idiom as `connectionFormSpec.ts`.
9	 *
10	 * GX column/table expectations are datasource-agnostic in v1 (all four
11	 * datasources run them through the shared `gx_runner`), so one catalog serves
12	 * every suite regardless of its connection type.
13	 */
14	
15	export type ConfigFieldType = 'string' | 'number' | 'list';
16	
17	export interface ConfigField {
18	  /** Key in the GX `config` kwargs object. */
19	  name: string;
20	  label: string;
21	  type: ConfigFieldType;
22	  optional?: boolean;
23	  help?: string;
24	}
25	
26	export interface ExpectationSpec {
27	  /** snake_case GX expectation type sent to the backend. */
28	  type: string;
29	  label: string;
30	  description: string;
31	  fields: ConfigField[];
32	}
33	
34	const COLUMN: ConfigField = { name: 'column', label: 'Column', type: 'string' };
35	
36	export const EXPECTATION_CATALOG: ExpectationSpec[] = [
37	  {
38	    type: 'expect_column_values_to_not_be_null',
39	    label: 'Column values not null',
40	    description: 'Every value in the column is non-null.',
41	    fields: [COLUMN],
42	  },
43	  {
44	    type: 'expect_column_values_to_be_unique',
45	    label: 'Column values unique',
46	    description: 'Values in the column are distinct (no duplicates).',
47	    fields: [COLUMN],
48	  },
49	  {
50	    type: 'expect_column_values_to_be_between',
51	    label: 'Column values in range',
52	    description: 'Numeric values fall within [min, max].',
53	    fields: [
54	      COLUMN,
55	      { name: 'min_value', label: 'Minimum', type: 'number', optional: true },
56	      { name: 'max_value', label: 'Maximum', type: 'number', optional: true },
57	    ],
58	  },
59	  {
60	    type: 'expect_column_values_to_be_in_set',
61	    label: 'Column values in set',
62	    description: 'Every value is one of an allowed set.',
63	    fields: [
64	      COLUMN,
65	      {
66	        name: 'value_set',
67	        label: 'Allowed values',

70	      },

25	/**
26	 * Author a GX expectation (v1's only check kind). The expectation Select drives
27	 * which config fields render (from EXPECTATION_CATALOG); the submitted `config`
28	 * is rebuilt from only the selected expectation's declared fields, so switching
29	 * types never leaks stale kwargs to the backend.
30	 */
31	export function CheckDrawer({
32	  open,
33	  suiteId,
34	  check,
35	  onClose,
36	  onSaved,
37	}: {
38	  open: boolean;
39	  suiteId: string;
40	  /** undefined = create; a check = edit. */
41	  check?: Check;
42	  onClose: () => void;
43	  onSaved: () => void;
44	}) {
45	  const { message } = App.useApp();
46	  const [form] = Form.useForm();
47	  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
48	  const isEdit = check !== undefined;
49	  const selectedType = Form.useWatch('expectation_type', form) as string | undefined;
50	  const spec = selectedType ? EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[selectedType] : undefined;
51	
52	  // Reset first (antd keeps values for unmounted fields, so stale config can
53	  // survive an open→close→open with a different check), then prefill on edit.
54	  useEffect(() => {
55	    if (!open) return;
56	    form.resetFields();
57	    if (check) {
58	      form.setFieldsValue({
59	        name: check.name,
60	        expectation_type: check.expectation_type,
61	        config: configToForm(EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[check.expectation_type], check.config),
62	        warn_threshold: check.warn_threshold ?? undefined,
63	        fail_threshold: check.fail_threshold ?? undefined,
64	        critical_threshold: check.critical_threshold ?? undefined,
65	      });
66	    }
67	  }, [open, check, form]);
68	
69	  const onSubmit = async () => {
70	    let values: Record<string, unknown>;
71	    try {
72	      values = await form.validateFields();
73	    } catch {
74	      return; // inline validation errors
75	    }
76	    const activeSpec = EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[values.expectation_type as string];
77	    const payload = {
78	      name: values.name as string,
79	      expectation_type: values.expectation_type as string,
80	      config: formToConfig(activeSpec, (values.config ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>),
81	      warn_threshold: numOrNull(values.warn_threshold),
82	      fail_threshold: numOrNull(values.fail_threshold),
83	      critical_threshold: numOrNull(values.critical_threshold),
84	    };
85	    setSubmitting(true);
86	    try {
87	      if (isEdit) {
88	        await updateCheck(suiteId, check.id, payload);
89	        message.success(`${payload.name}: saved`);
90	      } else {
91	        await createCheck(suiteId, payload);
92	        message.success(`${payload.name}: created`);
93	      }
94	      onSaved();
95	    } catch (err) {
96	      message.error(`Save failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
97	    } finally {
98	      setSubmitting(false);
99	    }
100	  };
101	
102	  return (
103	    <Drawer
104	      title={isEdit ? `Edit “${check.name}”` : 'New check'}
105	      open={open}
106	      onClose={onClose}
107	      width={520}
108	      destroyOnHidden
109	      extra={
110	        <Flex gap={8}>
111	          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>
112	          <Button type="primary" loading={submitting} onClick={onSubmit}>
113	            {isEdit ? 'Save' : 'Create'}
114	          </Button>
115	        </Flex>
116	      }
117	    >
118	      <Form form={form} layout="vertical">
119	        <Form.Item name="name" label="Name" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
120	          <Input placeholder="e.g. order_id not null" />
121	        </Form.Item>
122	        <Form.Item name="expectation_type" label="Expectation" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
123	          <Select
124	            placeholder="Select an expectation"
125	            options={EXPECTATION_CATALOG.map((e) => ({ value: e.type, label: e.label }))}
126	          />
127	        </Form.Item>
128	
129	        {spec && (
130	          <>
131	            <Typography.Paragraph type="secondary" style={{ marginTop: -8 }}>
132	              {spec.description}
133	            </Typography.Paragraph>
134	            {spec.fields.map((field) => (
135	              <ConfigFieldItem key={field.name} field={field} />
136	            ))}
137	          </>
138	        )}
139	
140	        <Divider style={{ margin: '8px 0 16px' }}>Severity thresholds (optional)</Divider>
141	        <Typography.Paragraph type="secondary" style={{ marginTop: -8 }}>
142	          Band the GX unexpected-% to warn / fail / critical (higher = worse). Leave blank for a
143	          binary pass/fail.
144	        </Typography.Paragraph>
145	        <Flex gap={12}>
146	          <Form.Item name="warn_threshold" label="Warn ≥" style={{ flex: 1 }}>
147	            <InputNumber min={0} max={100} style={{ width: '100%' }} />
148	          </Form.Item>
149	          <Form.Item name="fail_threshold" label="Fail ≥" style={{ flex: 1 }}>
150	            <InputNumber min={0} max={100} style={{ width: '100%' }} />
151	          </Form.Item>
152	          <Form.Item name="critical_threshold" label="Critical ≥" style={{ flex: 1 }}>
153	            <InputNumber min={0} max={100} style={{ width: '100%' }} />
154	          </Form.Item>
155	        </Flex>
156	      </Form>
157	    </Drawer>

161	/** Split a comma-separated list field into trimmed, non-empty items. */
162	function parseList(value: unknown): string[] {
163	  return String(value ?? '')
164	    .split(',')
165	    .map((s) => s.trim())
166	    .filter(Boolean);
167	}
168	
169	function ConfigFieldItem({ field }: { field: ConfigField }) {
170	  const label = field.optional ? `${field.label} (optional)` : field.label;
171	  const rules: Rule[] = field.optional ? [] : [{ required: true }];
172	  // A required list of only delimiters ("," / " , ") is non-empty (so it passes
173	  // `required`) but parses to zero items — reject it inline rather than letting
174	  // the check save with an empty value_set that only fails later at GX run time.
175	  if (field.type === 'list' && !field.optional) {
176	    rules.push({
177	      validator: (_: unknown, value: unknown) =>
178	        parseList(value).length > 0
179	          ? Promise.resolve()
180	          : Promise.reject(new Error('Enter at least one value')),
181	    });
182	  }
183	  return (
184	    <Form.Item name={['config', field.name]} label={label} rules={rules} extra={field.help}>
185	      {field.type === 'number' ? (
186	        <InputNumber style={{ width: '100%' }} />
187	      ) : (
188	        <Input placeholder={field.type === 'list' ? 'value1, value2, value3' : undefined} />
189	      )}
190	    </Form.Item>
191	  );
192	}
193	
194	function numOrNull(v: unknown): number | null {
195	  return typeof v === 'number' ? v : null;
196	}
197	
198	/** Build the GX `config` kwargs from only the selected expectation's fields. */
199	function formToConfig(
200	  spec: ExpectationSpec | undefined,
201	  raw: Record<string, unknown>,
202	): Record<string, unknown> {
203	  const config: Record<string, unknown> = {};
204	  if (!spec) return config;
205	  for (const field of spec.fields) {
206	    const value = raw[field.name];
207	    if (value === undefined || value === null || value === '') continue;
208	    if (field.type === 'list') {
209	      const items = parseList(value);
210	      if (items.length > 0) config[field.name] = items;
211	    } else {
212	      config[field.name] = value;
213	    }
214	  }
215	  return config;
216	}
217	
218	/** Inverse of formToConfig for edit-mode prefill (list array → comma string). */
219	function configToForm(
220	  spec: ExpectationSpec | undefined,
221	  config: Record<string, unknown>,
222	): Record<string, unknown> {
223	  const form: Record<string, unknown> = {};
224	  if (!spec) return form;
225	  for (const field of spec.fields) {
226	    const value = config[field.name];
227	    if (value === undefined) continue;
228	    form[field.name] = field.type === 'list' && Array.isArray(value) ? value.join(', ') : value;
229	  }
230	  return form;
231	}
232	
```

  "content": "import { Divider, Flex, Form, Input, InputNumber, Typography } from 'antd';\nimport type { Rule } from 'antd/es/form';\n\nimport type { CheckCreate } from '../../api/suites';\nimport { type ConfigField, EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE, type ExpectationSpec } from './expectationCatalog';\n\n/**\n * Shared check-authoring form logic, used by both the edit drawer (`CheckDrawer`)\n * and the dedicated create page (`CheckNew`): the dynamic config-field renderer,\n * the severity-threshold block, and the form↔payload conversions. Keeping these\n * in one place means the two surfaces can't drift on validation or kwarg shaping.\n */\n\n/** Split a comma-separated list field into trimmed, non-empty items. */\nexport function parseList(value: unknown): string[] {\n  return String(value ?? '')\n    .split(',')\n    .map((s) => s.trim())\n    .filter(Boolean);\n}\n\nexport function ConfigFieldItem({ field }: { field: ConfigField }) {\n  const label = field.optional ? `${field.label} (optional)` : field.label;\n  const rules: Rule[] = field.optional ? [] : [{ required: true }];\n  // A required list of only delimiters (\",\" / \" , \") is non-empty (so it passes\n  // `required`) but parses to zero items — reject it inline rather than letting\n  // the check save with an empty value_set that only fails later at GX run time.\n  if (field.type === 'list' && !field.optional) {\n    rules.push({\n      validator: (_: unknown, value: unknown) =>\n        parseList(value).length > 0\n          ? Promise.resolve()\n          : Promise.reject(new Error('Enter at least one value')),\n    });\n  }\n  return (\n    <Form.Item name={['config', field.name]} label={label} rules={rules} extra={field.help}>\n      {field.type === 'number' ? (\n        <InputNumber style={{ width: '100%' }} />\n      ) : (\n        <Input placeholder={field.type === 'list' ? 'value1, value2, value3' : undefined} />\n      )}\n    </Form.Item>\n  );\n}\n\n/** The optional warn / fail / critical severity-threshold inputs (ADR 0016). */\nexport function SeverityThresholdFields() {\n  return (\n    <>\n      <Divider style={{ margin: '8px 0 16px' }}>Severity thresholds (optional)</Divider>\n      <Typography.Paragraph type=\"secondary\" style={{ marginTop: -8 }}>\n        Band the GX unexpected-% to warn / fail / critical (higher = worse). Leave blank for a binary\n        pass/fail.\n      </Typography.Paragraph>\n      <Flex gap={12}>\n        <Form.Item name=\"warn_threshold\" label=\"Warn ≥\" style={{ flex: 1 }}>\n          <InputNumber min={0} max={100} style={{ width: '100%' }} />\n        </Form.Item>\n        <Form.Item name=\"fail_threshold\" label=\"Fail ≥\" style={{ flex: 1 }}>\n          <InputNumber min={0} max={100} style={{ width: '100%' }} />\n        </Form.Item>\n        <Form.Item name=\"critical_threshold\" label=\"Critical ≥\" style={{ flex: 1 }}>\n          <InputNumber min={0} max={100} style={{ width: '100%' }} />\n        </Form.Item>\n      </Flex>\n    </>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction numOrNull(v: unknown): number | null {\n  return typeof v === 'number' ? v : null;\n}\n\n/** Build the GX `config` kwargs from only the selected expectation's fields. */\nfunction formToConfig(\n  spec: ExpectationSpec | undefined,\n  raw: Record<string, unknown>,\n): Record<string, unknown> {\n  const config: Record<string, unknown> = {};\n  if (!spec) return config;\n  for (const field of spec.fields) {\n    const value = raw[field.name];\n    if (value === undefined || value === null || value === '') continue;\n    if (field.type === 'list') {\n      const items = parseList(value);\n      if (items.length > 0) config[field.name] = items;\n    } else {\n      config[field.name] = value;\n    }\n  }\n  return config;\n}\n\n/** Inverse of formToConfig for edit-mode prefill (list array → comma string). */\nexport function configToForm(\n  spec: ExpectationSpec | undefined,\n  config: Record<string, unknown>,\n): Record<string, unknown> {\n  const form: Record<string, unknown> = {};\n  if (!spec) return form;\n  for (const field of spec.fields) {\n    const value = config[field.name];\n    if (value === undefined) continue;\n    form[field.name] = field.type === 'list' && Array.isArray(value) ? value.join(', ') : value;\n  }\n  return form;\n}\n\n/** Assemble the create/update payload from validated form values. Rebuilds\n *  `config` from only the selected expectation's fields, so switching types\n *  never leaks stale kwargs. */\nexport function buildCheckPayload(values: Record<string, unknown>): CheckCreate {\n  const spec = EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[values.expectation_type as string];\n  return {\n    name: values.name as string,\n    expectation_type: values.expectation_type as string,\n    config: formToConfig(spec, (values.config ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>),\n    warn_threshold: numOrNull(values.warn_threshold),\n    fail_threshold: numOrNull(values.fail_threshold),\n    critical_threshold: numOrNull(values.critical_threshold),\n  };\n}\n"
}

1	"""Dispatch a persisted `Run` to the Celery worker — the one place that publishes.
2	
3	Publishes ``run_suite`` **by name** via ``celery_app.send_task`` rather than
4	importing the task object. That decoupling is deliberate: ``worker.tasks``
5	imports service modules (e.g. ``orchestration_service``), so a service importing
6	``worker.tasks`` back would be a cyclic import (CodeQL `py/cyclic-import`). By
7	name there is no import edge service → worker, and the broker resolves the task
8	on the worker side. The ``before_task_publish`` signal still fires, so the
9	``request_id`` correlation header is carried exactly as for ``.delay``.
10	
11	Raises on a broker/publish failure; the caller owns the policy for a stuck run
12	(the probe endpoint surfaces 503; the pipeline-trigger path marks the run
13	``failed`` so it isn't left ``queued``).
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	import uuid
19	
20	from backend.app.worker.celery_app import celery_app
21	
22	_RUN_SUITE_TASK = "run_suite"
23	
24	
25	def dispatch_run(run_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
26	    """Publish the ``run_suite`` task for ``run_id``. Raises if the broker is down."""
27	    celery_app.send_task(_RUN_SUITE_TASK, args=[str(run_id)])
28

235	    value: Any | None
236	    count: int

240	    column: str
241	    null_count: int

249	class ProfileRead(BaseModel):
250	    """Profile result. Identity fields are type-specific: SQL datasources fill
251	    `table` / `schema` (+ `catalog` for Unity Catalog), flat-file datasources fill
252	    `path` / `file_format`."""
253	
254	    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)
255	
256	    row_count: int
257	    columns: list[ColumnProfileRead]

260	    catalog: str | None = None
261	    path: str | None = None
262	    file_format: str | None = None

266	    "/suites/{suite_id}/profile",
267	    response_model=ProfileRead,

274	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],

276	) -> ProfileRead:
277	    # sync def → threadpool; the datasource connect + scans/downloads are blocking.
278	    # Authoring aid → 'edit', same as the dry-run. Connection FK is RESTRICT.
279	    suite = require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="edit")

286	        table=payload.table,
287	        schema=payload.schema_,
288	        catalog=payload.catalog,
289	        path=payload.path,
290	        file_format=payload.file_format,
291	        secret_store=secret_store,
292	    )
293	    return ProfileRead(
294	        row_count=result.row_count,
295	        table=result.table,
296	        schema_=result.schema,
297	        catalog=result.catalog,
298	        path=result.path,
299	        file_format=result.file_format,
300	        columns=[
301	            ColumnProfileRead(
302	                column=c.column,
303	                null_count=c.null_count,
304	                null_fraction=c.null_fraction,
305	                distinct_count=c.distinct_count,
306	                min_value=c.min_value,
307	                max_value=c.max_value,
308	                top_values=[TopValue(value=t["value"], count=t["count"]) for t in c.top_values],
309	            )
310	            for c in result.columns
311	        ],
312	    )

1	"""Execute a suite's checks via a datasource adapter and persist the results.
2	
3	This is the GX-agnostic core of a run: it drives the `Run` lifecycle, calls a
4	`CheckRunner` (injected — Snowflake in production, a fake in tests), and maps the
5	returned `SuiteOutcome` onto `Result` rows. GX/Snowflake specifics live behind
6	the adapter; this layer only knows the DTOs in ``datasources.base``.
7	
8	Run.status describes *execution*, not data quality: a run that completes is
9	``succeeded`` even when checks fail (the failures live in ``Result.status`` /
10	``SuiteOutcome.success``). ``failed`` means the run could not execute — the
11	adapter raised (e.g. could not reach the warehouse).
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import uuid
17	from datetime import UTC, datetime
18	
19	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
20	
21	from backend.app.core.jsonsafe import sanitize_json
22	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
23	from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckOutcome, CheckRunner, CheckSpec
24	from backend.app.db.models import Check, Result, Run
25	from backend.app.services.severity import derive_status, extract_metric
26	
27	log = get_logger(__name__)
28	
29	
30	def _now() -> datetime:
31	    return datetime.now(UTC)
32	
33	
34	def _build_result(run_id: uuid.UUID, check: Check, outcome: CheckOutcome) -> Result:
35	    """Map a check + its GX outcome to a `Result`, deriving the severity tier.
36	
37	    The unexpected-percent badness scalar is extracted once and used both to band
38	    the tier (ADR 0005 / 0016) and to persist as the durable, SQL-aggregatable
39	    `metric_value` (ADR 0012). `duration_ms` stays NULL in v1 — per-check timing
40	    isn't separable from GX's single suite-level `validate()` (reserved seam).
41	    """
42	    metric = extract_metric(outcome)
43	    status = derive_status(
44	        success=outcome.success,
45	        metric_value=metric,
46	        warn_threshold=check.warn_threshold,
47	        fail_threshold=check.fail_threshold,
48	        critical_threshold=check.critical_threshold,
49	    )
50	    return Result(
51	        run_id=run_id,
52	        check_id=check.id,
53	        status=status,
54	        metric_value=metric,
55	        observed_value=sanitize_json(outcome.observed_value),
56	        expected_value=sanitize_json(outcome.expected_value),
57	        sample_failures=sanitize_json(outcome.sample_failures),
58	    )
59	
60	
61	_EXPECTATION_KIND = "expectation"
62	
63	
64	def _specs_for_checks(checks: list[Check]) -> list[CheckSpec]:
65	    """Dispatch checks by `check.kind` to their runner input (ADR 0012).
66	
67	    v1 implements only the `expectation` kind (the GX `CheckRunner`). The other
68	    reserved kinds (`freshness`/`volume`/`schema_drift`/`anomaly`/`comparison`)
69	    are constraint-valid but have no runner yet, so a run containing one raises
70	    `NotImplementedError` rather than silently feeding it to GX as an
71	    expectation. This dispatch composes with the connection-type `CheckRunner`
72	    selection (Week 5, ADR 0011): `kind` chooses the *monitor*, `connection.type`
73	    chooses the *adapter*.
74	    """
75	    unsupported = sorted({c.kind for c in checks if c.kind != _EXPECTATION_KIND})
76	    if unsupported:
77	        raise NotImplementedError(
78	            f"no run path for check kind(s) {', '.join(unsupported)}; "
79	            f"only {_EXPECTATION_KIND!r} is implemented in v1"
80	        )
81	    return [CheckSpec(expectation_type=c.expectation_type, kwargs=dict(c.config)) for c in checks]
82	
83	
84	def execute_run(
85	    session: Session,
86	    *,
87	    run: Run,
88	    checks: list[Check],
89	    runner: CheckRunner,
90	    table: str,
91	    schema: str | None = None,
92	) -> Run:
93	    """Run ``checks`` against ``table`` via ``runner`` and persist the outcome.
94	
95	    ``run`` must already be persisted (it carries the id the results link to).
96	    Returns the same `Run`, updated to ``succeeded`` or ``failed``.
97	    """
98	    run.status = "running"
99	    run.started_at = _now()
100	    session.commit()
101	    log.info(
102	        "run_started",
103	        run_id=str(run.id),
104	        suite_id=str(run.suite_id),
105	        n_checks=len(checks),
106	        table=table,
107	    )
108	
109	    # Everything from here — dispatching by kind, running the adapter, building
110	    # rows, and persisting them — is guarded so any failure drives the run to a
111	    # terminal 'failed' state. Without this, a DB error during add_all/commit (or
112	    # an unrunnable check kind) would leave the run stuck in 'running' forever.
113	    # rollback() discards any partial result inserts before we record the failure.
114	    try:
115	        specs = _specs_for_checks(checks)
116	        outcome = runner.run_checks(table=table, schema=schema, checks=specs)
117	        rows = [
118	            _build_result(run.id, check, check_outcome)
119	            for check, check_outcome in zip(checks, outcome.checks, strict=True)
120	        ]
121	        session.add_all(rows)
122	        run.status = "succeeded"
123	        run.finished_at = _now()
124	        session.commit()
125	    except Exception:
126	        session.rollback()
127	        run.status = "failed"
128	        run.finished_at = _now()
129	        session.commit()
130	        log.exception("run_failed", run_id=str(run.id), table=table)
131	        return run
132	
133	    log.info(
134	        "run_completed",
135	        run_id=str(run.id),
136	        suite_success=outcome.success,
137	        n_results=len(rows),
138	    )
139	    return run
140

1	"""Suite authorization — the single primitive every suite-scoped endpoint gates on.
2	
3	A user's effective permission on a suite is the highest of: **owner** (they are
4	`suite.created_by` — implicit, immutable, never a share row) or their `shares`
5	row (`view` < `edit` < `admin`). Capability ladder (decided for v1):
6	
7	    view   — read the suite, its checks, its results
8	    edit   — + create/update/delete checks, update the suite, trigger runs
9	    admin  — + manage shares (grant/revoke) AND delete the suite
10	    owner  — same capabilities as admin, but it is the creator: cannot be
11	             revoked or demoted, and granting a share to the owner is rejected.
12	
13	`require_permission` is the gate the API layer calls: it 404s a suite the user
14	can't see at all (existence is hidden), and 403s one they can see but lack the
15	level for. It returns the `Suite` so callers don't re-fetch.
16	
17	FastAPI-free (takes a `Session` + the user id); the API layer passes
18	`current_user.id`.
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import uuid
24	
25	from sqlalchemy import select
26	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
27	
28	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
29	from backend.app.db.models import Share, Suite
30	from backend.app.services.suite_service import SuiteNotFoundError
31	
32	OWNER = "owner"
33	
34	# Ordered capability ranks. `owner` ranks above `admin` so it always clears an
35	# admin gate, even though their capabilities are identical — the distinction is
36	# that owner is the immutable creator, not a grantable/revocable share.
37	_RANK = {"view": 1, "edit": 2, "admin": 3, OWNER: 4}
38	
39	
40	class SuiteForbiddenError(DataQError):
41	    status_code = 403
42	    code = "suite_forbidden"
43	
44	
45	def effective_permission(session: Session, suite: Suite, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> str | None:
46	    """The user's level on `suite` (`owner`/`admin`/`edit`/`view`), or None."""
47	    if suite.created_by == user_id:
48	        return OWNER
49	    share = session.scalars(
50	        select(Share).where(Share.suite_id == suite.id, Share.user_id == user_id)
51	    ).first()
52	    return share.permission if share is not None else None
53	
54	
55	def require_permission(
56	    session: Session,
57	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
58	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
59	    *,
60	    minimum: str,
61	) -> Suite:
62	    """Return the suite iff the user has at least `minimum` permission on it.
63	
64	    Raises `SuiteNotFoundError` (404) if the suite doesn't exist **or** the user
65	    has no access at all (existence is hidden), and `SuiteForbiddenError` (403)
66	    if they have some access but below `minimum`.
67	    """
68	    suite = session.get(Suite, suite_id)
69	    if suite is None:
70	        raise SuiteNotFoundError("suite not found", detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id)})
71	    level = effective_permission(session, suite, user_id)
72	    if level is None:
73	        # No access → indistinguishable from "doesn't exist" (don't leak the id).
74	        raise SuiteNotFoundError("suite not found", detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id)})
75	    if _RANK[level] < _RANK[minimum]:
76	        raise SuiteForbiddenError(
77	            f"this action requires {minimum!r} permission on the suite",
78	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "have": level, "need": minimum},
79	        )
80	    return suite
81

1	"""Week 1 exit-gate probe endpoint.
2	
3	POST seeds the probe fixtures, creates a queued Run, and dispatches the
4	``run_suite`` Celery task (GX → Snowflake DEV). GET reads a run back with its
5	results. This is a thin demonstrator of the full async path — not the general
6	run API, which arrives with suite/check CRUD in Weeks 3-5.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import uuid
12	from typing import Annotated, Any
13	
14	from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status
15	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
16	from sqlalchemy import select
17	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
18	
19	from backend.app.core.auth import get_current_user
20	from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
21	from backend.app.db.models import Result, Run, User
22	from backend.app.db.session import get_db
23	from backend.app.services import run_dispatch
24	from backend.app.services.probe import ensure_probe_fixtures
25	
26	router = APIRouter(tags=["probe"])
27	
28	
29	class ProbeRunResponse(BaseModel):
30	    run_id: uuid.UUID
31	    status: str
32	
33	
34	class CheckResultResponse(BaseModel):
35	    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
36	
37	    check_id: uuid.UUID
38	    status: str  # pass | warn | fail | critical (ADR 0005)
39	    metric_value: float | None  # the unexpected-% badness scalar (ADR 0012)
40	    observed_value: dict[str, Any] | None
41	    expected_value: dict[str, Any] | None
42	
43	
44	class RunStatusResponse(BaseModel):
45	    run_id: uuid.UUID
46	    status: str
47	    results: list[CheckResultResponse]
48	
49	
50	@router.post(
51	    "/_probe/snowflake-suite",
52	    response_model=ProbeRunResponse,
53	    status_code=status.HTTP_202_ACCEPTED,
54	    summary="Trigger the Snowflake probe suite",
55	    description=(
56	        "Seeds the dev Snowflake connection + canned suite, queues a run, and "
57	        "dispatches it to the Celery worker. Returns the run id to poll."
58	    ),
59	)
60	def trigger_snowflake_probe(
61	    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
62	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
63	) -> ProbeRunResponse:
64	    settings = get_settings()
65	    _, suite, _ = ensure_probe_fixtures(db, user=current_user, settings=settings)
66	
67	    run = Run(suite_id=suite.id, status="queued", triggered_by=f"probe:{current_user.id}")
68	    db.add(run)
69	    db.commit()
70	    db.refresh(run)
71	
72	    try:
73	        run_dispatch.dispatch_run(run.id)
74	    except Exception as exc:  # broker unreachable — don't leave the run stuck queued
75	        run.status = "failed"
76	        db.commit()
77	        raise HTTPException(
78	            status_code=status.HTTP_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
79	            detail="failed to dispatch run",
80	        ) from exc
81	    return ProbeRunResponse(run_id=run.id, status=run.status)
82	
83	
84	@router.get(
85	    "/_probe/runs/{run_id}",
86	    response_model=RunStatusResponse,
87	    summary="Read a probe run and its results",
88	)
89	def get_probe_run(
90	    run_id: uuid.UUID,
91	    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
92	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
93	) -> RunStatusResponse:
94	    run = db.get(Run, run_id)
95	    if run is None:
96	        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail="run not found")
97	    results = list(db.scalars(select(Result).where(Result.run_id == run_id)))
98	    return RunStatusResponse(
99	        run_id=run.id,
100	        status=run.status,
101	        results=[CheckResultResponse.model_validate(r) for r in results],
102	    )
103

3	from decimal import Decimal

7	    Boolean,
8	    CheckConstraint,
9	    DateTime,

11	    Index,

19	from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB, UUID
20	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship
21	
22	from backend.app.db.base import Base
23	
24	# ── Status / type value sets (TEXT + CHECK; not native PG enums for migration ergonomics) ──
25	CONNECTION_TYPES = ("snowflake", "adls_gen2", "s3", "unity_catalog", "adf", "airflow")
26	RUN_STATUSES = ("queued", "running", "succeeded", "failed", "cancelled")
27	# Result statuses. The four severity tiers (ADR 0005) are health-score-bearing —
28	# the score aggregate sums their weights over N. The two operational statuses
29	# (#122) are orthogonal: 'skip' = not evaluated, 'error' = evaluation threw
30	# (distinct from 'fail', a successful evaluation that breached). Operational
31	# statuses carry NO penalty weight and MUST be excluded from the health-score N
32	# (i.e. aggregate WHERE status IN the four tiers only).
33	_RESULT_SEVERITY_TIERS = ("pass", "warn", "fail", "critical")
34	_RESULT_OPERATIONAL_STATUSES = ("skip", "error")
35	RESULT_STATUSES = _RESULT_SEVERITY_TIERS + _RESULT_OPERATIONAL_STATUSES
36	# Monitor-kind discriminator (ADR 0012; `comparison` reserved by ADR 0014). v1
37	# only ever writes 'expectation'; the rest are constraint-valid but unused.
38	CHECK_KINDS = ("expectation", "freshness", "volume", "schema_drift", "anomaly", "comparison")
39	PIPELINE_RUN_STATUSES = ("queued", "running", "succeeded", "failed", "cancelled")
40	ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS = ("adf", "airflow")
41	PERMISSIONS = ("view", "edit", "admin")
42	ENVS = ("dev", "qa", "uat", "prod")

45	def _uuid_pk() -> Mapped[uuid.UUID]:
46	    return mapped_column(
47	        UUID(as_uuid=True),
48	        primary_key=True,
49	        server_default=text("gen_random_uuid()"),
50	    )
51	
52	
53	def _created_at() -> Mapped[datetime]:
54	    return mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False, server_default=func.now())
55	
56	
57	def _updated_at() -> Mapped[datetime]:
58	    return mapped_column(
59	        DateTime(timezone=True),
60	        nullable=False,
61	        server_default=func.now(),
62	        onupdate=func.now(),
63	    )
64	
65	
66	def _in_check(column: str, values: tuple[str, ...], name: str) -> CheckConstraint:
67	    quoted = ", ".join(f"'{v}'" for v in values)
68	    return CheckConstraint(f"{column} IN ({quoted})", name=name)

71	class User(Base):
72	    __tablename__ = "users"
73	
74	    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = _uuid_pk()
75	    aad_object_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(64), nullable=False, unique=True)
76	    email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(320), nullable=False)

83	class Connection(Base):
84	    __tablename__ = "connections"
85	    __table_args__ = (
86	        _in_check("type", CONNECTION_TYPES, "type_valid"),
87	        _in_check("env", ENVS, "env_valid"),
88	        UniqueConstraint("name", "env", name="uq_connections_name_env"),
89	        # Orchestration providers (ADF, Airflow) are singletons per env: at most
90	        # one connection per (provider, env), the binding `trigger_bindings`
91	        # assumes (ADR 0004, #72). Datasources are deliberately excluded — e.g.
92	        # Snowflake DEV can have many connections (different databases) — so this
93	        # is a *partial* unique index over the orchestration types only.
94	        Index(
95	            "uq_connections_orchestrator_type_env",
96	            "type",
97	            "env",
98	            unique=True,
99	            postgresql_where=text(
100	                "type IN (" + ", ".join(f"'{p}'" for p in ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS) + ")"
101	            ),
102	        ),
103	        Index("ix_connections_created_by", "created_by"),
104	    )
105	
106	    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = _uuid_pk()
107	    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(128), nullable=False)
108	    type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(32), nullable=False)
109	    env: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(16), nullable=False)
110	    config: Mapped[dict[str, Any]] = mapped_column(
111	        JSONB, nullable=False, server_default=text("'{}'::jsonb")

114	    # once a credential is written, but is NULL for (a) the transient window

116	    # credential-less auth — managed identity (ADLS) / IAM role (S3), deferred to

118	    # are all secret-bearing and enforce presence in the service layer
119	    # (test_connection → 502 without a stored credential), so the column stays
120	    # NULL-able for the W7 credential-less modes without a later migration.
121	    secret_ref: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(256))
122	    created_by: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(

124	    )

1	"""Suite CRUD — datasource-type-agnostic, FastAPI-free.
2	
3	A suite is a named collection of checks bound to exactly one connection
4	(CLAUDE.md §10). This layer validates the connection exists on create, then
5	treats `connection_id` as immutable — re-pointing a suite at a different
6	connection would silently invalidate every child check's table/column semantics,
7	so it is not an update path.
8	
9	Like `connection_service` / `run_service`: takes a `Session`, returns ORM
10	models, raises `DataQError` subclasses; the API layer owns request/response
11	shapes and dependency wiring. Share-based access control is layered on separately
12	(the Week-3 suite-sharing task); this service is authenticated CRUD only.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import uuid
18	from typing import Any
19	
20	from sqlalchemy import or_, select
21	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
22	
23	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
24	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
25	from backend.app.db.models import Connection, Share, Suite
26	from backend.app.services import run_target
27	
28	log = get_logger(__name__)
29	
30	
31	class SuiteNotFoundError(DataQError):
32	    status_code = 404
33	    code = "suite_not_found"
34	
35	
36	class SuiteConnectionInvalidError(DataQError):
37	    status_code = 422
38	    code = "suite_connection_invalid"
39	
40	
41	def create_suite(
42	    session: Session,
43	    *,
44	    name: str,
45	    description: str | None,
46	    connection_id: uuid.UUID,
47	    created_by: uuid.UUID,
48	    target: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
49	) -> Suite:
50	    """Create a suite bound to an existing connection.
51	
52	    Raises `SuiteConnectionInvalidError` (422) if the connection does not exist
53	    — caught here so a bad `connection_id` is a clean validation error, not a
54	    raw FK IntegrityError surfacing as 500. A provided ``target`` is validated
55	    against the connection's datasource type (422 if malformed); a suite may also
56	    be created targetless (NULL) and have a target set later via update.
57	    """
58	    connection = session.get(Connection, connection_id)
59	    if connection is None:
60	        raise SuiteConnectionInvalidError(
61	            "connection not found", detail={"connection_id": str(connection_id)}
62	        )
63	    if target is not None:
64	        run_target.validate_target(connection.type, target)
65	    suite = Suite(
66	        name=name,
67	        description=description,
68	        connection_id=connection_id,
69	        created_by=created_by,
70	        target=target,
71	    )
72	    session.add(suite)
73	    session.commit()
74	    session.refresh(suite)
75	    log.info("suite_created", suite_id=str(suite.id), connection_id=str(connection_id))
76	    return suite
77	
78	
79	def list_suites(
80	    session: Session, *, user_id: uuid.UUID, connection_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
81	) -> list[Suite]:
82	    """Suites the user can access: owned (`created_by`) or shared with them."""
83	    shared = select(Share.suite_id).where(Share.user_id == user_id)
84	    stmt = (
85	        select(Suite)
86	        .where(or_(Suite.created_by == user_id, Suite.id.in_(shared)))
87	        .order_by(Suite.created_at.desc())
88	    )
89	    if connection_id is not None:
90	        stmt = stmt.where(Suite.connection_id == connection_id)
91	    return list(session.scalars(stmt))
92	
93	
94	def get_suite(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID) -> Suite:
95	    suite = session.get(Suite, suite_id)
96	    if suite is None:
97	        raise SuiteNotFoundError("suite not found", detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id)})
98	    return suite
99	
100	
101	def update_suite(
102	    session: Session,
103	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
104	    *,
105	    name: str | None = None,
106	    description: str | None = None,
107	    target: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
108	) -> Suite:
109	    """Partial update of name / description / target. `connection_id` is immutable.
110	
111	    A provided ``target`` is validated against the suite's connection type (422
112	    if malformed) and replaces the existing target. ``None`` means "leave the
113	    target unchanged" (the same partial-update semantics as name/description), so
114	    this path sets/replaces a target but never clears one back to NULL.
115	    """
116	    suite = get_suite(session, suite_id)
117	    if name is not None:
118	        suite.name = name
119	    if description is not None:
120	        suite.description = description
121	    if target is not None:
122	        connection = session.get(Connection, suite.connection_id)
123	        assert connection is not None  # FK is RESTRICT; a suite always has its connection
124	        run_target.validate_target(connection.type, target)
125	        suite.target = target
126	    session.commit()
127	    session.refresh(suite)
128	    log.info("suite_updated", suite_id=str(suite.id))
129	    return suite
130	
131	
132	def delete_suite(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
133	    """Delete a suite; its checks cascade (Suite.checks delete-orphan + FK)."""
134	    suite = get_suite(session, suite_id)
135	    session.delete(suite)
136	    session.commit()
137	    log.info("suite_deleted", suite_id=str(suite_id))
138

1	"""Celery tasks for asynchronous suite execution.
2	
3	``run_suite`` is the worker entry point dispatched by the manual-run / probe /
4	pipeline-trigger paths. It loads the run's suite / connection / checks, resolves
5	the suite's datasource-shaped **target** (#215) to the runner's
6	``(table, schema, catalog)``, builds the datasource adapter, and hands off to
7	``run_service.execute_run``. The DB-touching core is factored into ``_run_suite``
8	so it can be unit-tested with a fake session + fake runner (no Postgres, no
9	Snowflake); real-DB integration coverage is a Week 8 item.
10	
11	The target lives on the suite (``Suite.target``, resolved by
12	``run_target.resolve_target``): a targetless suite drives the run to ``failed``
13	with a clear log rather than running against an unknown table.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	import uuid
19	from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
20	
21	from sqlalchemy import select
22	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
23	
24	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
25	from backend.app.core.secrets import SecretStore, get_secret_store
26	from backend.app.datasources.registry import build_check_runner
27	from backend.app.db.models import ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS, Check, Connection, Run, Suite
28	from backend.app.db.session import get_session
29	from backend.app.orchestration.registry import get_orchestration_provider
30	from backend.app.services import orchestration_service, run_service, run_target
31	from backend.app.worker.celery_app import celery_app
32	
33	# Polling fallback (#171): look back slightly further than the 10-min beat
34	# interval so a run can't slip through the gap between consecutive polls.
35	_POLL_LOOKBACK = timedelta(minutes=15)
36	
37	log = get_logger(__name__)
38	
39	
40	def _run_suite(session: Session, *, run_id: uuid.UUID) -> str:
41	    """Load the run's graph, resolve its target, build the runner, execute.
42	
43	    The suite's datasource-shaped ``target`` (#215) resolves to the runner's
44	    ``(table, schema, catalog)`` via ``run_target.resolve_target``; dispatch by
45	    ``connection.type`` through the runner registry gives a Snowflake / Unity
46	    Catalog / flat-file suite its correct `CheckRunner` (#146).
47	
48	    Failures while loading, resolving the target (targetless or malformed suite),
49	    or building the runner (missing rows, bad connection config, unresolved
50	    secret) drive the run to ``failed`` so it never lingers in ``queued``;
51	    execution failures are handled inside ``execute_run``.
52	    """
53	    run = session.get(Run, run_id)
54	    if run is None:
55	        log.error("run_suite_run_not_found", run_id=str(run_id))
56	        return "not_found"
57	
58	    try:
59	        suite = session.get(Suite, run.suite_id)
60	        connection = session.get(Connection, suite.connection_id) if suite is not None else None
61	        if suite is None or connection is None:
62	            raise RuntimeError("suite or connection not found for run")
63	        target = run_target.resolve_target(connection.type, suite.target)
64	        checks = list(session.scalars(select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == suite.id)))
65	        runner = build_check_runner(
66	            conn_type=connection.type,
67	            config=connection.config,
68	            secret_ref=connection.secret_ref,
69	            secret_store=get_secret_store(),
70	            catalog=target.catalog,
71	        )
72	    except Exception:
73	        run.status = "failed"
74	        run.started_at = run.started_at or datetime.now(UTC)
75	        run.finished_at = datetime.now(UTC)
76	        session.commit()
77	        log.exception("run_suite_setup_failed", run_id=str(run_id))
78	        return "failed"
79	
80	    run_service.execute_run(
81	        session, run=run, checks=checks, runner=runner, table=target.table, schema=target.schema
82	    )
83	    return str(run.status)
84	
85	
86	@celery_app.task(name="run_suite")  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery task decorator is unannotated
87	def run_suite(run_id: str) -> str:
88	    """Worker entry point. ``run_id`` is a string so it serialises over JSON.
89	
90	    The target is resolved from the suite (``Suite.target``), so the only
91	    argument the dispatcher supplies is the run id.
92	    """
93	    session = get_session()
94	    try:
95	        return _run_suite(session, run_id=uuid.UUID(run_id))
96	    finally:
97	        session.close()
98	
99	
100	def _poll_orchestration_runs(
101	    session: Session, *, secret_store: SecretStore, now: datetime | None = None
102	) -> dict[str, int]:
103	    """Poll every orchestrator connection for recent succeeded runs (#171, ADR 0004).
104	
105	    The polling fallback for runs that never produced a webhook: iterate each
106	    ADF / Airflow connection, ask the provider's `list_recent_runs` for runs
107	    updated within the lookback window, and hand them to `ingest_polled_runs`
108	    (upsert + trigger-on-success). Goes through the `OrchestrationProvider` seam —
109	    no per-provider branching. Each connection is isolated: a transport/auth
110	    failure logs + continues so one bad connection can't starve the rest.
111	    """
112	    since = (now or datetime.now(UTC)) - _POLL_LOOKBACK
113	    summary = {"connections": 0, "recorded": 0, "triggered": 0, "skipped": 0, "errors": 0}
114	    connections = list(
115	        session.scalars(
116	            select(Connection).where(
117	                Connection.type.in_(ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS),
118	                Connection.secret_ref.isnot(None),
119	            )
120	        )
121	    )
122	    for connection in connections:
123	        if not connection.secret_ref:  # defensive; the query already filters
124	            continue
125	        try:
126	            provider_impl = get_orchestration_provider(connection.type)
127	            secret = secret_store.get(connection.secret_ref)
128	            updates = provider_impl.list_recent_runs(dict(connection.config), secret, since)
129	            result = orchestration_service.ingest_polled_runs(
130	                session,
131	                provider_impl=provider_impl,
132	                connection=connection,
133	                updates=updates,
134	                skip_updated_since=since,
135	            )
136	            summary["connections"] += 1
137	            summary["recorded"] += len(result.pipeline_runs)
138	            summary["triggered"] += len(result.triggered_runs)
139	            summary["skipped"] += result.skipped
140	        except Exception:
141	            summary["errors"] += 1
142	            session.rollback()
143	            log.exception(
144	                "orchestration_poll_failed",
145	                connection_id=str(connection.id),
146	                provider=connection.type,
147	            )
148	    log.info("orchestration_poll_completed", **summary)
149	    return summary
150	
151	
152	@celery_app.task(name="poll_orchestration_runs")  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery task decorator is unannotated
153	def poll_orchestration_runs() -> dict[str, int]:
154	    """Celery-beat entry point — the 10-min orchestration polling fallback."""
155	    session = get_session()
156	    try:
157	        return _poll_orchestration_runs(session, secret_store=get_secret_store())
158	    finally:
159	        session.close()
160

1	"""Resolve a suite's datasource-shaped target to the runner's (table, schema, catalog).
2	
3	A suite's `target` (#215) is a small JSONB document shaped like the column
4	profiler request (``table`` / ``schema`` / ``catalog`` / ``path`` /
5	``file_format``), datasource-typed. The `CheckRunner` interface is *table-shaped*
6	— for a flat-file datasource the file path rides the ``table`` argument
7	(``flatfile.py``) — so every datasource resolves to the same triple the worker
8	hands to ``run_service.execute_run`` and ``build_check_runner``:
9	
10	    snowflake      → table (+ schema)
11	    unity_catalog  → table (+ schema) + catalog        (catalog.schema.table)
12	    adls_gen2 / s3 → path  (carried as `table`; schema/catalog unused)
13	
14	`resolve_target` is the run-time path (raises if a required field is missing).
15	`validate_target` is the write-time path (same rules; used by `suite_service`
16	when a target is set on a suite, so a malformed/wrong-datasource target is a
17	clean 422 at save rather than a failed run later).
18	
19	FastAPI-free: takes a connection type + the stored dict, raises `DataQError`.
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	from dataclasses import dataclass
25	from typing import Any
26	
27	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
28	
29	_FLATFILE_TYPES = {"adls_gen2", "s3"}
30	
31	
32	class SuiteTargetInvalidError(DataQError):
33	    status_code = 422
34	    code = "suite_target_invalid"
35	
36	
37	@dataclass(frozen=True)
38	class ResolvedTarget:
39	    """The runner inputs a suite resolves to. ``table`` carries the file path for
40	    flat-file datasources; ``catalog`` is set only for Unity Catalog."""
41	
42	    table: str
43	    schema: str | None
44	    catalog: str | None
45	
46	
47	def resolve_target(conn_type: str, target: dict[str, Any] | None) -> ResolvedTarget:
48	    """Resolve ``target`` for a ``conn_type`` connection, or raise (422).
49	
50	    Raises `SuiteTargetInvalidError` if the suite is targetless, the target is
51	    missing the field its datasource requires (`path` for flat files, `table`
52	    for SQL, `catalog` for Unity Catalog), or the connection type has no run path
53	    (orchestration providers — they are never suite datasources).
54	    """
55	    if not target:
56	        raise SuiteTargetInvalidError(
57	            "suite has no target configured", detail={"connection_type": conn_type}
58	        )
59	
60	    if conn_type in _FLATFILE_TYPES:
61	        path = _require(target, "path", conn_type)
62	        return ResolvedTarget(table=path, schema=None, catalog=None)
63	
64	    if conn_type == "snowflake":
65	        table = _require(target, "table", conn_type)
66	        return ResolvedTarget(table=table, schema=_str_or_none(target.get("schema")), catalog=None)
67	
68	    if conn_type == "unity_catalog":
69	        table = _require(target, "table", conn_type)
70	        catalog = _require(target, "catalog", conn_type)
71	        return ResolvedTarget(
72	            table=table, schema=_str_or_none(target.get("schema")), catalog=catalog
73	        )
74	
75	    raise SuiteTargetInvalidError(
76	        f"connection type {conn_type!r} has no run path (not a datasource)",
77	        detail={"connection_type": conn_type},
78	    )
79	
80	
81	def validate_target(conn_type: str, target: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
82	    """Write-time guard: a non-null target must resolve for its datasource.
83	
84	    Reuses `resolve_target`'s rules so a target saved on a suite is always
85	    runnable. Callers only invoke this when a target is *provided* — a suite may
86	    be created/updated targetless (NULL), which is valid-but-not-yet-runnable.
87	    """
88	    resolve_target(conn_type, target)
89	
90	
91	def _require(target: dict[str, Any], field: str, conn_type: str) -> str:
92	    value = target.get(field)
93	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
94	        raise SuiteTargetInvalidError(
95	            f"target for a {conn_type!r} suite requires a non-empty {field!r}",
96	            detail={"connection_type": conn_type, "missing": field},
97	        )
98	    return value
99	
100	
101	def _str_or_none(value: Any) -> str | None:
102	    return value if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip() else None
103	
```

183	def _trigger_suites(
184	    session: Session, *, provider: str, connection: Connection, update: RunUpdate
185	) -> list[Run]:
186	    """Create one queued `Run` per enabled `trigger_binding` for a succeeded run.
187	
188	    Idempotent on the ``triggered_by`` marker ``<provider>:<pipeline>:<run_id>``:
189	    a replayed event (or a webhook + poll double-delivery) does not spawn a
190	    second run for the same (suite, pipeline-run).
191	
192	    Each created run is handed to Celery (``run_suite``) once committed; the
193	    worker resolves the suite's target (#215) and fails the run cleanly if the
194	    suite is targetless. A broker failure marks that run ``failed`` rather than
195	    leaving it stuck ``queued`` (the 10-min poll won't re-dispatch a stale row).
196	    """
197	    marker = f"{provider}:{update.pipeline_or_dag_id}:{update.provider_run_id}"
198	    bindings = list(
199	        session.scalars(
200	            select(TriggerBinding).where(
201	                TriggerBinding.provider == provider,
202	                TriggerBinding.pipeline_or_dag_id == update.pipeline_or_dag_id,
203	                TriggerBinding.env == connection.env,
204	                TriggerBinding.enabled.is_(True),
205	            )
206	        )
207	    )
208	    created: list[Run] = []
209	    for binding in bindings:
210	        already = session.scalar(
211	            select(Run.id).where(Run.suite_id == binding.suite_id, Run.triggered_by == marker)
212	        )
213	        if already is not None:
214	            continue
215	        run = Run(suite_id=binding.suite_id, status="queued", triggered_by=marker)
216	        session.add(run)
217	        created.append(run)
218	
219	    if created:
220	        session.commit()
221	        for run in created:
222	            session.refresh(run)
223	        log.info(
224	            "suite_runs_triggered",
225	            provider=provider,
226	            pipeline=update.pipeline_or_dag_id,
227	            run_marker=marker,
228	            count=len(created),
229	        )
230	        for run in created:
231	            try:
232	                run_dispatch.dispatch_run(run.id)
233	            except Exception:
234	                # Broker down: don't leave the run stuck 'queued'. Mark it failed
235	                # with the worker's terminal-failed shape — finished_at set,
236	                # started_at NULL (it never started) — so run-history/duration
237	                # views stay consistent across dispatch paths.
238	                run.status = "failed"
239	                run.finished_at = datetime.now(UTC)
240	                session.commit()
241	                log.exception("suite_dispatch_failed", run_id=str(run.id))
242	    return created
243	
244	
245	@dataclass(frozen=True)
246	class IngestResult:
247	    pipeline_run: PipelineRun | None
248	    triggered_runs: list[Run] = field(default_factory=list)
249

"""Pipeline-run persistence for orchestration events, provider-agnostic.

Consumes the normalised `RunUpdate` (from any `OrchestrationProvider`) and lands
it in `pipeline_runs` with an idempotent upsert keyed on
(`provider`, `provider_run_id`) — the ADR 0006 replay-neutraliser: a duplicate
or replayed webhook delivery updates the same row instead of inserting a new one
(and, once triggering lands, does not re-fire a suite).

The run is attributed to an orchestrator connection by matching the event's
`resource_name` (ADF factory) against `connections.config->>'factory_name'` for
the provider's connections; that connection supplies `connection_id` (a NOT NULL
FK) and `env`. An unattributable event (no matching connection) is ignored —
the caller acknowledges it (200) per ADR 0006 rather than erroring, since a
late-arriving event for a deleted connection must not retry-storm Azure Monitor.

FastAPI-free by design (like `connection_service` / `run_service`): takes a
`Session`, returns ORM models, never raises for the ignore case.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import insert as pg_insert
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
from backend.app.core.secrets import SecretStore
from backend.app.db.models import Connection, PipelineRun, Run, TriggerBinding
from backend.app.orchestration.base import OrchestrationProvider, RunUpdate
from backend.app.orchestration.registry import get_orchestration_provider
from backend.app.services import run_dispatch

log = get_logger(__name__)


def _resolve_connection(
    session: Session, *, provider_impl: OrchestrationProvider, resource_name: str
...TAIL...

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/api/v1/runs.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Run / result / pipeline-run read API — the results surface (PR-C0b).\n\nRead-only views over `runs`, `results`, and `pipeline_runs` for the in-app\nresults page. The DQ-run reads (`/runs`, `/runs/{id}`) are **suite-scoped**: the\nlist filters to suites the caller can access and the detail gates on\n`require_permission(view)`, so per-suite sharing + existence-hiding hold exactly\nas for suites/checks (this is why reading Postgres directly — e.g. a Grafana\npanel — is rejected as the primary surface: it bypasses this authz + the sample\nredaction below). `/pipeline_runs` is orchestration monitoring, not suite-scoped,\nso it is gated on authentication only.\n\nManual run *triggering* lives on `POST /suites/{id}/run` in `suites.py` (the\nsuite-scoped, edit-gated write); this module owns the reads.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport uuid\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom typing import Annotated, Any\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Query, status\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.core.auth import get_current_user\nfrom backend.app.db.models import User\nfrom backend.app.db.session import get_db\nfrom backend.app.services import orchestration_service\nfrom backend.app.services import run_service as svc\nfrom backend.app.services.suite_authz import require_permission\n\nrouter = APIRouter(tags=[\"runs\"])\n\n_LIST_LIMIT_DEFAULT = 50\n_LIST_LIMIT_MAX = 200\n\n\nclass RunRead(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"A DQ suite run (execution lifecycle; `status` is execution, not pass/fail).\"\"\"\n\n    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)\n\n    id: uuid.UUID\n    suite_id: uuid.UUID\n    status: str  # queued | running | succeeded | failed | cancelled\n    triggered_by: str | None\n    started_at: datetime | None\n    finished_at: datetime | None\n    created_at: datetime\n\n\nclass ResultRead(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"One check's result within a run. `metric_value` is the SQL-aggregatable\n    badness scalar (ADR 0012); `sample_failures` is sanitised at write time and\n    only reaches a caller who cleared the suite-view gate.\"\"\"\n\n    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)\n\n    id: uuid.UUID\n    check_id: uuid.UUID\n    status: str  # pass | warn | fail | critical | skip | error\n    metric_value: float | None\n    duration_ms: int | None\n    observed_value: dict[str, Any] | None\n    expected_value: dict[str, Any] | None\n    sample_failures: dict[str, Any] | None\n\n\nclass RunDetailRead(RunRead):\n    results: list[ResultRead]\n\n\nclass PipelineRunRead(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"A monitored orchestrator pipeline/DAG run (`pipeline_runs` ≠ `runs`).\"\"\"\n\n    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)\n\n    id: uuid.UUID\n    provider: str  # adf | airflow\n    connection_id: uuid.UUID\n    provider_run_id: str\n    pipeline_or_dag_id: str\n    env: str\n    status: str\n    started_at: datetime | None\n    finished_at: datetime | None\n    failure_reason: str | None\n    created_at: datetime\n\n\n@router.get(\"/runs\", response_model=list[RunRead], summary=\"List runs\")\ndef list_runs(\n    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],\n    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],\n    suite_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,\n    run_status: Annotated[str | None, Query(alias=\"status\")] = None,\n    limit: int = Query(default=_LIST_LIMIT_DEFAULT, ge=1, le=_LIST_LIMIT_MAX),\n) -> list[RunRead]:\n    # When a suite is named, gate on it up front so an inaccessible/unknown suite\n    # 404s (existence hidden) rather than silently returning []. With no suite,\n    # the service scopes to every suite the caller can access.\n    if suite_id is not None:\n        require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum=\"view\")\n    runs = svc.list_runs(\n        db, user_id=current_user.id, suite_id=suite_id, status=run_status, limit=limit\n    )\n    return [RunRead.model_validate(r) for r in runs]\n\n\n@router.get(\"/runs/{run_id}\", response_model=RunDetailRead, summary=\"Get a run with its results\")\ndef get_run(\n    run_id: uuid.UUID,\n    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],\n    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],\n) -> RunDetailRead:\n    run = svc.get_run(db, run_id)\n    if run is None:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail=\"run not found\")\n    # Gate on the run's suite: a caller who can't see the suite can't see its\n    # runs (404 hides the run id too, matching the suite existence-hiding rule).\n    require_permission(db, run.suite_id, current_user.id, minimum=\"view\")\n    results = svc.list_results(db, run_id)\n    detail = RunDetailRead.model_validate(run)\n    detail.results = [ResultRead.model_validate(r) for r in results]\n    return detail\n\n\n@router.get(\n    \"/pipeline_runs\",\n    response_model=list[PipelineRunRead],\n    summary=\"List monitored orchestrator pipeline/DAG runs\",\n)\ndef list_pipeline_runs(\n    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],\n    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],\n    provider: str | None = None,\n    run_status: Annotated[str | None, Query(alias=\"status\")] = None,\n    limit: int = Query(default=_LIST_LIMIT_DEFAULT, ge=1, le=_LIST_LIMIT_MAX),\n) -> list[PipelineRunRead]:\n    pipeline_runs = orchestration_service.list_pipeline_runs(\n        db, provider=provider, status=run_status, limit=limit\n    )\n    return [PipelineRunRead.model_validate(p) for p in pipeline_runs]\n"
}

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/api/v1/suites.py",
  "old_string": "    require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum=\"admin\")\n    svc.delete_suite(db, suite_id)\n\n\n# ───────────────────────── export / import (portable documents) ─────",
  "new_string": "    require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum=\"admin\")\n    svc.delete_suite(db, suite_id)\n\n\n# ───────────────────────── manual run trigger ──────────────────────\n\n\n@router.post(\n    \"/suites/{suite_id}/run\",\n    response_model=RunRead,\n    status_code=status.HTTP_202_ACCEPTED,\n    summary=\"Trigger a run of the suite\",\n)\ndef trigger_suite_run(\n    suite_id: uuid.UUID,\n    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],\n    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],\n) -> RunRead:\n    \"\"\"Queue a run of the suite and dispatch it to the worker.\n\n    `edit` gates this (the capability ladder grants 'trigger runs' at edit). The\n    suite's target (#215) is resolved up front so a targetless/misconfigured\n    suite fails fast with a 422 instead of a queued→failed run the caller has to\n    poll to discover. A broker outage marks the run `failed` (never left stuck\n    `queued`) and surfaces 503 — the same contract as the probe endpoint.\n    \"\"\"\n    suite = require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum=\"edit\")\n    connection = db.get(Connection, suite.connection_id)\n    assert connection is not None  # FK is RESTRICT; a suite always has its connection\n    # Raises SuiteTargetInvalidError (422) for a targetless / wrong-datasource target.\n    run_target.resolve_target(connection.type, suite.target)\n\n    run = Run(suite_id=suite.id, status=\"queued\", triggered_by=f\"manual:{current_user.id}\")\n    db.add(run)\n    db.commit()\n    db.refresh(run)\n\n    try:\n        run_dispatch.dispatch_run(run.id)\n    except Exception as exc:  # broker unreachable — don't leave the run stuck queued\n        run.status = \"failed\"\n        db.commit()\n        raise HTTPException(\n            status_code=status.HTTP_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,\n            detail=\"failed to dispatch run\",\n        ) from exc\n    return RunRead.model_validate(run)\n\n\n# ───────────────────────── export / import (portable documents) ─────"
}

"""Suite endpoint tests against a real Postgres (db_session) via TestClient.

get_db is overridden to the shared test session; auth runs in dev-bypass mode
(conftest), which upserts the dev user for the suite's created_by. A connection
(with its own owner) is inserted directly for the FK. Skips without
TEST_DATABASE_URL.
"""

import uuid
from collections.abc import Iterator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

import pandas as pd
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import func, select

from backend.app.core.auth import get_current_user
from backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Suite, User
from backend.app.db.session import get_db
from backend.app.main import app
from backend.app.services import profile_service


@pytest.fixture
def client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
    try:
        yield TestClient(app)
    finally:
        app.dependency_overrides.clear()


def _connection(db_session: Any) -> Connection:
    """Insert a connection (with its own owner) for suites to bind to."""
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email="owner@example.com")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"sf-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type="snowflake",
        env="dev",
        config={"account": "ab12345.eu-west-1"},
        secret_ref="kv-sf",
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.commit()
    return conn


def _payload(connection_id: uuid.UUID, **overrides: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    body: dict[str, Any] = {
        "name": "finance-checks",
        "description": "row + null checks for finance tables",
        "connection_id": str(connection_id),
    }
    body.update(overrides)

# ───────────────────────── create ──────────────────────────────────


def test_create_returns_201(client: TestClient, db_session: Any) -> None:
    conn = _connection(db_session)
    resp = client.post("/api/v1/suites", json=_payload(conn.id))
    assert resp.status_code == 201
    body = resp.json()
    assert body["name"] == "finance-checks"
    assert body["connection_id"] == str(conn.id)
    assert body["created_by"] is not None  # the dev-bypass user
    # persisted
    assert db_session.get(Suite, uuid.UUID(body["id"])) is not None


def test_create_unknown_connection_returns_422(client: TestClient) -> None:
    resp = client.post("/api/v1/suites", json=_payload(uuid.uuid4()))
    assert resp.status_code == 422
    assert resp.json()["error"]["code"] == "suite_connection_invalid"


def test_create_blank_name_returns_422(client: TestClient, db_session: Any) -> None:
    conn = _connection(db_session)
    resp = client.post("/api/v1/suites", json=_payload(conn.id, name=""))
    assert resp.status_code == 422


def test_create_allows_null_description(client: TestClient, db_session: Any) -> None:
    conn = _connection(db_session)
    resp = client.post("/api/v1/suites", json=_payload(conn.id, description=None))
    assert resp.status_code == 201
    assert resp.json()["description"] is None


# ───────────────────────── run target (#215) ───────────────────────


def test_create_with_target_persists_storage_shape(client: TestClient, db_session: Any) -> None:
    conn = _connection(db_session)  # snowflake
    resp = client.post(
        "/api/v1/suites",
        json=_payload(conn.id, target={"table": "ORDERS", "schema": "SALES"}),
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 201
    # Stored with the canonical `schema` key (not the `schema_` alias), no nulls.
    assert resp.json()["target"] == {"table": "ORDERS", "schema": "SALES"}


def test_create_without_target_is_null(client: TestClient, db_session: Any) -> None:
    conn = _connection(db_session)
    resp = client.post("/api/v1/suites", json=_payload(conn.id))
    assert resp.status_code == 201
    assert resp.json()["target"] is None


def test_create_with_wrong_datasource_target_returns_422(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any
) -> None:
    conn = _connection(db_session)  # snowflake needs `table`, not `path`
